- **Settings** opens the settings pages. See [Settings](/docs/settings/).

Collapse the sidebar to a narrow rail with its toggle; the rail keeps New chat, Home, Agents, the attention indicator, Settings and Buddy as icons.

## A Conversation

The conversation's header shows its name (click it to rename), **Find** to search the conversation, **Export**, and **Conversation details**. The **details card** beside the conversation lists what the conversation is **Working on** (its designs and code folders), its **Outputs** (each thing it made, once, finished work first), its **Goal**, and the **Agents** it started. A delegated agent's own conversation shows the way back to its parent in the header. See [Chat](/docs/chat/).

## Panels And The Terminal

A design opens in a **Design panel** and a code folder in a **Developer panel**, beside the conversation. Open them from the details card or the header's **Open panel** menu; drag the divider to resize. A video Row-Bot makes opens in the **Video** panel from its card's **Open** (see [The Video Panel](/docs/chat/tools-approvals-and-terminal#the-video-panel)). See [Designs](/docs/designer/) and [Code Folders](/docs/developer/).

In the desktop app, the **terminal** opens docked under the conversation with the terminal button, **Open panel › Interactive terminal**, or Ctrl+`. See [Tools, Approvals And Background Work](/docs/chat/tools-approvals-and-terminal#interactive-terminal).

## The Command Palette

Press ⌘K (Ctrl+K on Windows and Linux), or the search button in the sidebar's top row, to open the command palette. Type what you want in your own words:

- **Requests** such as "connect a model", "phone", "connect telegram", "add mcp server", "install a skill", "change model", "connect gmail" or "back up" go straight to the exact place it is done. Words can come in any order.
- **Conversations and messages** are found by title and by words in their messages.
- **Commands** open Home tabs, the conversation library, Setup Center, Settings or the Agents dialog, and toggle the sidebar, the details card or the terminal. Each shows its shortcut.
- **Settings pages and rows** open at the exact row.
- **Switches** flip a setting in place, showing its current state, with **Undo** afterwards: for example "turn off shell", "turn on developer tools", the browser tool, Dream Cycle, learning new skills, or tracking. "dark mode", "light mode" and "follow the system appearance" change this device's appearance.
- **Agents** and **workflows**: "Chat with …" starts a chat with an agent; "Run …" runs a workflow.

Enter runs the top result only when it matches what you typed; otherwise choose a result with the arrow keys.

## Keyboard Shortcuts

| Shortcut | Action |
| --- | --- |
| ⌘K / Ctrl+K | Open the command palette |
| ⌘⇧O / Ctrl+Shift+O | New chat |
| ⌘. / Ctrl+. | Show or hide the conversation details card |
| Ctrl+` | Open or close the terminal |
| / | Find a setting, on a Settings page |
| ⌘Enter / Ctrl+Enter | Approve the focused approval |
| ⌘Z and ⌘⇧Z / Ctrl+Z and Ctrl+Shift+Z | Undo and redo in the Design panel |
| Esc | Close the palette, a menu or a dialog |

## On A Phone Or Tablet

On a narrow screen, the sidebar becomes a drawer opened from the top bar, panels open as full-screen sheets, and the conversation header's **⋯** menu holds Find, Conversation details, Export, the panels and the command palette. See [Phone And Native Desktop](/docs/mobile-native/).

## What Is Saved

Conversations, their names, models, profiles, workflows, knowledge, settings and logs are saved in the local Row-Bot data directory. Panel sizes, the terminal's height, favourite agents and appearance are remembered on each device.

## Troubleshooting

- If a conversation is missing from the sidebar, use **Show all**, the type filter, or the conversation library's search.
- If a panel looks stale, close and reopen it from the details card.
- If a button is disabled, check the related Settings page and Monitor for readiness messages.

## Home: Overview

Route: /docs/home/overview

Start from Home Overview: ask Row-Bot anything, answer what needs you, and pick up recent work, in one calm column.

# Home: Overview

Overview is the first page Row-Bot opens. It is one calm column that says the most important thing first: what needs you, then where you left off, then what is happening today. It shows only what exists, so a quiet day is a short page. Everything on it opens the place where the work actually lives.

## Where To Find It

Choose **Home** in the sidebar. Overview is the first of the Home tabs: Overview, Workflows, Knowledge, Monitor and Insights, and [Learning](/docs/learning/) while it's on. Until a default model exists, opening Row-Bot opens [first launch](/docs/getting-started/first-launch) instead; if you choose **Set up later**, Overview shows only **Choose a model** under the greeting.

## The Greeting And The Ask Box

- One sentence under the greeting says the most important thing: how many things need you, else when the next workflow runs, else **All quiet**.
- **Ask Row-Bot anything, or describe what to make…** starts a new chat with your text. Use **Add files in a new chat** to attach files first, then **Start chat**.
- Three small icons under the Ask box are quick starts (hover or focus one to see its name):
  - **New design** and **New code folder** set up a design or a code folder and open it in a new chat with its panel beside it. See [Designs](/docs/designer/) and [Code Folders](/docs/developer/).
  - **New workflow** opens the workflow editor on the Workflows tab.

## Needs You

**Needs you** appears only when something waits for you, with the same count as the sidebar's indicator:

- **Approvals** from any conversation, workflow or delegated agent show **Approve** and **Deny** right in the row, with how long each has waited. Open the conversation or workflow when you want the full context first.
- **Posts and emails to review**: one row, such as **2 posts and 1 email to review**, that takes you to **Review**.
- **Conversations waiting on you**: interrupted agent work offers **Resume** or **Dismiss**; a goal waiting for your answer opens its conversation.
- **Failed workflows** offer **Run … again**, or open the workflow to see why.
- **Apps that need you**: an app that is on but needs a sign-in, its key or attention shows as **Sign in to _app_**, **_App_ needs its key** or **_App_ needs attention**. Its fix opens the app in [Settings › Apps](/docs/settings/apps) with that fix started.
- **Problems** such as a stopped channel or a red health check carry their one-click fix, such as restarting the channel, reconnecting an account, choosing a model, or checking again. See [Monitor](/docs/monitor/).
- **Finish setup** shows as the last row while Setup Center still has steps. It is a reminder, not a need, so it isn't counted; hide it once you are done.

Three items show at first; **+N more waiting** shows the rest.

## Review

**Review** shows each post or email waiting to go out as its full card: the account or recipients, the whole text, each picture or file, and, for a post with a time, when it goes out. Each card has **Approve** (**Approve for then** for a post with a time), **Deny**, the pencil to edit a post, and **Not now**, which sets it aside here while it keeps waiting. It works the same on a phone.

A post approved for a time is listed under **Scheduled** until it goes out. Choose **Cancel this post** to stop it. Row-Bot posts it at its time, while it is running. A post whose time passed more than 12 hours ago while Row-Bot was closed, or whose file changed after you approved it, isn't sent: you get a notice instead.

## Recent

**Recent** lists your last three chats, workflow conversations or code folders, newest first, each with when you last used it. **All** opens the [Conversation library](/docs/chat/#find-export-and-clean-up).

## Today

**Today** shows up to four short rows, and only the ones that exist:

| Row | Opens |
| --- | --- |
| An agent at work | Monitor |
| When the next workflow runs | That workflow on the Workflows tab |
| A health warning, with its fix beside it | Monitor |
| Memories saved this week | Knowledge |

A warning Monitor kept from an earlier check, such as a channel you have since turned off, isn't shown until the checks run again. If a source can't be read, Today says so in one quiet line.

With [Proactive Row-Bot](/docs/guides/proactive) on, Today becomes **For you**, placed after Review: what Row-Bot brought up, grouped by **Now**, **Later today** and **Ready when you are**, starting with [your morning brief](/docs/guides/morning-brief) and ending with **That's everything for today.** Today's rows move into it. With Proactive **Off**, Today stays as described here.

The rest of what used to sit here lives in its tab: agent and workflow activity in [Monitor](/docs/monitor/) and [Workflows](/docs/home/workflows), memories in [Knowledge](/docs/knowledge/), and insights in [Home: Insights](/docs/home/insights).

## What Is Saved

Overview stores nothing of its own. It reads your conversations, workflows, approvals, memories and Monitor checks, and every action runs through the same reviewed command as the place it comes from.

## Troubleshooting

- If Overview opens Setup instead, finish choosing a model or choose **Set up later**.
- If Today says it couldn't read something, refresh the page; Monitor shows whether the service behind it is healthy.
- Approving from Overview is the same decision as approving in the conversation. Open the conversation first when the request is not obvious from its title.

## Proactive Row-Bot

Route: /docs/guides/proactive

How Row-Bot speaks first: what it brings up, the four levels, when it speaks, privacy, Why this?, your rules, the activity log, and turning it down or off.

# Proactive Row-Bot

Proactive Row-Bot speaks first when something is worth your attention: a reply you're still waiting for, a meeting about to start, a birthday coming up, a meeting that moved. It gets things ready in the background, such as a meeting brief or a drafted reply, and tells you at a good moment.

It never sends or changes anything without you. Background work only reads; anything that would send, post or change something goes through the same approval card as in a chat, at your approval level.

Most of the time it stays silent, and that is by design. A quiet day is a short Home.

## What It Brings Up

Each thing Row-Bot brings up is a **moment**: one line, what was prepared, and at most two actions.

| Kind | Example | What Row-Bot prepares |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **Follow-ups** | "Priya hasn't replied about the Q3 numbers (4 days)." | A drafted follow-up, saved, not sent |
| | "Tom asked about the venue on Tuesday." | A drafted reply |
| | "You said you'd send Ana the deck by Friday." | The file it found |
| **Meeting prep** | "Design review with Priya and Tom in 10 min." | A brief: who's coming, the last thread, open items and files |
| **Dates** | "Dad's birthday is Sunday." "Car insurance renews on 2 Dec." | What you've saved about it |
| **Changes** | "Your 1:1 with Ana moved to 15:30." "The visa appointments page changed." | What changed |
| | "The weekly report didn't finish." "Gmail needs you to sign in again." | The run, or the fix |
| **Workflow ideas** | "You've asked for the sales summary 3 Mondays running. Make it a workflow?" | A workflow ready to save; nothing is scheduled until you save it |
| **Morning brief** | "Good morning. 3 meetings, 2 follow-ups, and Dad's birthday is Sunday." | Your day in a few lines. See [Your Morning Brief](/docs/guides/morning-brief) |
| **End-of-day wrap** | "Wrap-up: 4 things done, 1 moved to tomorrow." | What got done and what moved. Off until you turn it on |

Row-Bot checks again just before it shows anything. If the meeting was cancelled or the reply arrived in the meantime, the moment is dropped and you never see it. It never acts on a question: asking about a restaurant is not booking it.

## Where You See It

Row-Bot uses one place at a time, the quietest that fits:

1. **Buddy's glance.** Buddy looks up at you with a small, held change of expression. No words, no sound.
2. **Buddy's bubble.** At a good moment, one line beside Buddy with one or two actions and a **⋯**. It fades by itself; nothing piles up. On a phone, or a narrow window, it shows as a short strip above the tab bar instead.
3. **A desktop notification**, only when Row-Bot's window isn't in front.
4. **Your phone**, only when this computer is idle or locked, and only if you turned on notifications on that phone.
5. **A chat app** such as Telegram, only for kinds you marked urgent, only when you're away.

Every moment also waits on **Home › For you** until it's done or no longer matters, so a bubble that fades is never lost.

Moments are offers, not demands: they never count in **Needs you** or the sidebar's indicator.

### Home › For You

With Proactive on, Home's **Today** becomes **For you**, grouped by time:

- **Now**: due within the hour, such as a meeting brief.
- **Later today**: things with a time today, including briefs Row-Bot plans to prepare and today's workflow runs.
- **Ready when you are**: things that can wait, such as follow-ups with drafts and dates ahead.

Choose a row to open what was prepared, or use its icons. **⋯** has **Not now**, **Less like this** and **Why this?**. The list ends with **That's everything for today.** Things that no longer matter leave on their own, without a notice.

### Drafts

Replies Row-Bot drafted wait in **Drafts**, from the **Drafts** link in For you's heading or a draft's own row. Drafts are saved in Row-Bot, never sent and never put in your mailbox by a background run.

1. Choose a draft to read it.
2. Edit the recipients, subject or text if you like. Your changes are saved as you type.
3. Choose **Send…**. The normal approval card appears with the exact message; approve it to send, or deny it to go back to the draft.

If someone replied after the draft was written, the draft says so. Drafts older than 14 days are removed.

## The Levels

Choose a level in **Settings › Proactive**. Every install starts at **Quiet**.

| Level | What it means |
| --- | --- |
| **Off** | Row-Bot doesn't check anything or speak first. Home shows **Today** as before. |
| **Quiet** | Things wait on Home. Buddy speaks only for what's about to happen, and once in the morning. Up to 3 a day. |
| **Balanced** | Buddy speaks at good moments. Desktop notifications when Row-Bot isn't in front; your phone only when you're away. Up to 6 a day. |
| **Eager** | Row-Bot brings up more, and earlier. Up to 12 a day. |

The daily number counts every bubble, notification and message together. Buddy's glance and Home › For you never count: they don't interrupt. Under the level picker, **Today at _level_ you'd have seen** lists what each level would have shown you today, so you can compare before you choose.

The level is how loud Row-Bot is. **What to bring up** is separate: each kind has its own switch, and changing the level never changes them.

## When It Speaks

Row-Bot waits for a natural break: when you open Row-Bot, come back to your computer, finish a call, finish a chat turn, or start your day. It never speaks:

- while you're typing;
- while a dialog or sheet is open;
- in a call, with your microphone or camera in use;
- in Focus or Do Not Disturb on your computer;
- in your **Quiet hours** (22:00 to 07:30 to start with).

What came up in the meantime waits on Home. Something urgent, such as a meeting in ten minutes, goes first.

### Desktop Activity

**Use desktop activity for timing**, on by default in the desktop app, lets Row-Bot pick better moments. It checks only whether you're away, locked, in a call or in Focus, and what kind of app is in front. It never reads window titles, contents or screenshots, and it stays on this computer. Turn it off in **Settings › Proactive › When**; Row-Bot then only knows when you open it.

## Privacy

- Watching for changes happens on this computer. Row-Bot compares your mail, calendar, chats, memory and workflows with what it saw last time, and does nothing when nothing changed.
- To decide what's worth your attention, short summaries of what changed go to your main model. The settings page and the first introduction name the provider. With a main model that runs on this computer, nothing leaves it.
- Only apps you've connected are used, and each source has its own switch and a line saying what it reads. Row-Bot never asks you to connect more.
- Instructions inside emails are never followed. When an email asks for something to be done, **Why this?** says so: Row-Bot only noticed it.
- A phone notification shows the moment's title and one line, which can name a person or a subject. It's encrypted end to end for that device, so the push service passes on only ciphertext. Turn off **Show details in notifications** in Settings › Devices & remote access and each one says only "Row-Bot is waiting for you". A message in a chat app goes through that app's servers, as one line.
- The activity log, your rules and your drafts stay on this computer. There is no telemetry about Proactive.

## Why This?

Every moment explains itself. Choose **⋯ › Why this?** on a bubble, a For you row or a draft to see:

- **What Row-Bot saw**: the email, event, memory or chat it came from, with the part that mattered. Emails show as plain text, without pictures or links you can click. **Open** takes you to the original.
- When it last checked that it's still true, such as **Still no reply · checked just now**.
- **Why now**: the timing and the moment it chose.
- **What let it through**: the kind, your level, how many of today's were used, and any rule that applied.
- **What Row-Bot prepared**, and the line **Row-Bot only read. Nothing was sent or changed.**

## Less Like This And Your Rules

Choose **⋯ › Less like this** on anything Row-Bot brings up. It asks one question, about what:

- **this person**: "Follow-ups about Priya stay in For you";
- **this kind**: "All follow-ups stay in For you";
- **this time of day**: "Nothing before 11:00 on weekdays".

Your choice becomes a rule straight away, with **Undo**. A rule made this way keeps matching moments on Home only: no bubble, notification or message.

**Settings › Proactive › Your rules** lists every rule in words. **Edit** changes who or what it covers, its hours, or makes it **Don't show at all**; **Delete** removes it, with **Undo**.

If you keep skipping one kind, Row-Bot quiets it by itself and says so in **Your rules**, with **Bring back**. **Not now** on a single moment keeps it on Home and stops Row-Bot bringing it up again.

## The Activity Log

**Settings › Proactive › Activity** lists every check Row-Bot made, including the silent ones, for the last 30 days:

- what it checked, and **Nothing to bring up** when nothing was worth it;
- what it showed, where, and what you did;
- what it dropped and why, such as **Dropped: Team lunch was cancelled**;
- what it plans to do, such as a brief for your 14:00, with **Take over** (opens a chat with the work so far) and **Cancel**.

Expand an entry to see what changed, what happened to each candidate, and what went to your main model. The filter above the list shows **All**, **Shown**, **Silent** or **Planned**. The page's **⋯ › Clear activity…** deletes the log.

## Turn It Down Or Off

- **Quieter**: choose **Quiet**, or turn off kinds you don't want under **What to bring up**.
- **Not at certain times**: set **Quiet hours**, or make a time rule with **Less like this**.
- **Not about something**: **Less like this** on one of its moments.
- **Not on your phone**: turn off **Phone notifications** in **Settings › Proactive › Away from your desk**.
- **Off**: choose **Off**. Row-Bot stops checking at once, and Home shows **Today** again. Your rules and drafts are kept in case you turn it back on.

The command palette (⌘K or Ctrl+K) also has **Turn Proactive off** and **Proactive settings**.

## The First Introduction

Once, after setup, or after the update that adds Proactive, Home shows a short card: what Proactive does, the level picker set to **Quiet**, and where your data goes. Choose **Done** to keep your choice. It doesn't come back.

## Check-ins In A Chat

Proactive Row-Bot is separate from **Check-ins**, an optional skill for people who want Row-Bot to ask questions and check in during a task. See [Check-ins](/docs/skills/#check-ins).

## Troubleshooting

- **Nothing ever comes up.** That can be right: a quiet day has nothing. Check the level isn't **Off**, the kinds are on, and **Activity** shows checks. If the page's status says **Waiting for a model**, choose a main model.
- **Something came up that wasn't true any more.** Open **Why this?**: it shows when Row-Bot last checked. Use **Less like this** if it keeps happening.
- **Buddy doesn't glance.** Check **Show Buddy** in [Settings › Buddy](/docs/settings/buddy). With reduced motion on, a small dot by Buddy shows instead.
- **No phone notifications.** Turn on notifications on the phone first ([Remote access](/docs/operations/remote-access)), then **Phone notifications** in Settings › Proactive. They arrive only when this computer is idle or locked.
- **A draft didn't send.** Sending needs your approval on the card, and a signed-in account. Check **Needs you** and [Settings › Apps](/docs/settings/apps).

## Your Morning Brief

Route: /docs/guides/morning-brief

Row-Bot's morning brief: when it appears, what it covers, how it ends, how to change it, and the optional end-of-day wrap-up.

# Your Morning Brief

The morning brief is your day in a few lines: today's meetings, replies you're owed or owe, dates coming up, and what Row-Bot prepared overnight. It ends, every time, with **That's everything for today.**

It is part of [Proactive Row-Bot](/docs/guides/proactive) and is on at every level except **Off**.

## When It Appears

The first time you open Row-Bot or come back to your computer each day, after 06:00 and after your quiet hours:

- **Buddy** says it in one line, such as "Good morning. 3 meetings, 2 follow-ups, and Dad's birthday is Sunday.", with **Open brief**.
- **Home › For you** shows it first, opened, until you close it or the afternoon starts. After midday it folds to its one line at the end of For you.

It is never sent to your phone or a chat app. It waits for you.

## What It Covers

```
Good morning. 3 meetings, 2 follow-ups, a birthday.
10:00  Design review with Priya and Tom · brief ready
13:00  Lunch with Sam
15:30  1:1 with Ana (moved from 14:00)
Priya hasn't replied about Q3 (4 days) · draft ready
Tom asked about the venue · draft ready
Dad's birthday is Sunday
Overnight: Row-Bot drafted 2 replies and a brief.
That's everything for today.
```

- **Meetings** for today, with a brief where one is ready and any change since yesterday.
- **Follow-ups**: replies you're waiting for and ones waiting on you, with drafts where Row-Bot wrote one.
- **Dates** coming up: birthdays, renewals, trips and deadlines.
- **Overnight**: what Row-Bot prepared while you were away, such as meeting briefs and drafts. This line shows only when there is something.

Each line opens its own thing: the brief, the draft, the event. Things in the brief don't also show as separate rows that day, unless they become urgent; a meeting brief still appears ten minutes before the meeting.

On a quiet day the brief is short ("Good morning. A quiet day: one meeting at 15:00."). With nothing on, Buddy says nothing and For you shows only "Good morning. Nothing on today."

The brief only reads. Nothing is sent or changed; sending a draft always goes through its approval card.

## Change It

The brief is a workflow you can edit, like any other:

- **⋯ › Edit brief** on the brief opens it in the workflow editor. Change its message to cover what you want, such as "Also list my top three tasks from the Tracker".
- **⋯ › Open conversation** opens the brief's own conversation, where each day's brief is a turn. You can reply there to ask about it.
- **⋯ › Less like this** and **⋯ › Why this?** work as they do for every moment.

See [Workflows](/docs/guides/workflows) for the editor.

## Turn It Off

Choose **⋯ › Turn off the morning brief**, or turn off **Morning brief** in **Settings › Proactive › What to bring up**. Proactive keeps working without it; the things it would have listed still wait on Home.

## The End-Of-Day Wrap-Up

The wrap-up is the brief's evening partner, off until you turn it on in **Settings › Proactive › What to bring up**. At the time you choose (17:30 to start with), Buddy says something like "Wrap-up: 4 things done, 1 moved to tomorrow." and For you shows:

- what got done today;
- what moved to tomorrow;
- what is still waiting on someone else.

It ends with **That's everything for today.** Like the brief, it is an editable workflow and never goes to your phone or a chat app.

## Troubleshooting

- **No brief this morning.** Check that Proactive isn't **Off** and **Morning brief** is on. It comes at your first open after 06:00 and after quiet hours; a day with nothing on has no bubble.
- **The brief misses meetings or mail.** It uses the calendars and mail accounts you've connected and switched on under **Sources** in Settings › Proactive.
- **It came at the wrong time.** It comes at your first open after your quiet hours: set **Quiet hours** in Settings › Proactive.

## Chat

Route: /docs/chat/

Use Row-Bot conversations: the composer, models, incognito chats, attachments, tables, charts, choices and visuals in answers, pages, questions, context and token usage, apps and skills in a chat, approvals, the details card, and the conversation library.

# Chat

A conversation is the main place to work with Row-Bot. It can stay a simple chat, or use memory, documents, tools, approvals, attachments, skills, voice, agents, goals, designs and code folders.

## Start A Conversation

- Choose **New chat** in the sidebar (⌘⇧O / Ctrl+Shift+O), or type into the Ask box on [Home › Overview](/docs/home/overview).
- Use the **▾** beside **New chat**, a favourite agent in the sidebar, or **Chat with …** in the command palette to start with an agent profile.

A new conversation is named from the first words of your first message straight away, then gets a short name of its own after the first reply. Click the name in the header to rename it; a name you choose is kept.

You don't need to name a feature to use it. Ask in your own words, and Row-Bot picks the right tool:
- a plan, checklist or comparison becomes a [page](#pages);
- a choice only you can make comes as a [question](#questions);
- research on several things goes to helpers;
- a server or watcher runs in the background;
- "keep me on track" gets a plan and a weekly check-in.

## Incognito Chats

An incognito chat keeps what you say in it out of Row-Bot's memory.

- Start one with **New chat ▾ › New incognito chat**, or switch the open chat with the **⋯ › Incognito** in its header. In a messaging channel, send `/incognito on` or `/incognito off`.
- The header shows an incognito mark, and the composer reads "Message Row-Bot (incognito)". Hover the mark for "Incognito: nothing here is saved to memory".
- Row-Bot and its helpers can still use what they already remember. Nothing in the chat is read for memory, and nothing is saved unless you choose **Save** on the card that asks. That card appears at every approval level, Hands-off too, and for a helper's saves as well.
- Turning incognito on keeps memories already saved from this chat. The notice offers **Review**, which opens [Settings › Memory](/docs/settings/knowledge). Turning it off never reaches back: memory reads the chat only from then on.
- Searching your past conversations never finds an incognito chat.
- [Learning](/docs/learning/#what-it-records) never records a chat that is or was incognito.

## The Conversation

- **Header**: the conversation's name, **Find** to search it (⌘F / Ctrl+F), **Export**, and **Conversation details** (⌘. / Ctrl+.).
- **Transcript**: your messages and Row-Bot's replies, each with a small speaker mark (your Buddy's picture for Row-Bot), plus tool steps, how long Row-Bot thought, charts, images, generated media, approval cards and the agents a turn started. The finished work Row-Bot presents shows large in its reply; what it made on the way folds into one **working files** row under the reply's steps (see [Finished Work And Working Files](/docs/chat/tools-approvals-and-terminal#finished-work-and-working-files)).
- **Composer**: type the next request. Enter sends and Shift+Enter adds a line. **Send** becomes **Stop** while Row-Bot replies. A message you type while the previous one is still being sent stays in the composer on its own.
- **Retry** and **Send again** run your last message again in place of its answer, without a second copy of the message, when nothing is running or waiting for an approval. A turn that already used tools stays on record, so its retry is sent as a new message.
- **Maths** in a reply is typeset:
  - `\( … \)` and `$ … $` inline (`$` only where it can't be a price);
  - `\[ … \]` and `$$ … $$` on their own line.

  The typesetting ships with Row-Bot and loads only for a message that has maths.

## Edit An Earlier Message Or Fork A Chat

When a chat went the wrong way a few turns ago, go back to that point in a new conversation. The original stays exactly as it was.

- **Edit and resend** (the pencil on one of your messages): your message becomes a text field in place. Change it and press Enter (or the send button) to continue in a new conversation that holds everything before that message, with your edited text sent as its next message. Escape cancels. The message's files go with it.
- **Fork from here** (the branch icon on a reply): continue in a new conversation that holds everything up to the end of that reply, including the tools it used.

Both actions are hidden while Row-Bot is replying. On a phone, long-press a message to find them.

The new conversation is named after the original with "(fork)" and starts with a line saying where it came from, with **Open original**. It keeps the original's model, profile, skills, apps, approval level and incognito setting, works on the same code folder or design, and has its own copies of the files its messages name. Memory never reads the copied messages a second time.

What a fork does not do:

- It doesn't undo anything. Files changed, messages sent or anything else done after that point in the original stay done. To revert code changes, use **Undo** in the Developer panel.
- Goals, waiting items, linked conversations and helpers stay with the original. A helper card in the copied history opens the helper's conversation from the original.

## Composer Controls

- **Model** chooses the model for this conversation. See [Model Picker](/docs/chat/model-picker).
- **Thinking** appears beside the model only when that exact model exposes supported reasoning choices. See [Reasoning Controls](/docs/chat/reasoning-controls).
- **Approvals** sets how actions are reviewed in this conversation, and its menu says what each level does:
  - **Ask** asks before anything that makes changes;
  - **Auto**: a reviewer approves what you asked for, and the rest asks;
  - **Hands-off**: nothing asks, and every action runs and is recorded. You confirm it once for a chat;
  - **Block**: nothing that makes changes runs.

  See [Approvals](/docs/chat/tools-approvals-and-terminal).
- The **+** menu (**Add files and more**) holds **Attach file**, **Add resource…** (a design or code folder), **Skills…**, **Apps**, **Agent** (each agent with a line on what it does), and **Mode**: **Agent** uses tools and agents, **Chat only** answers without tools.
- **Skill chips** above the composer show the skills in use, including default ones; × removes one from this conversation. **Skills…** (or `/skills`) opens **Smart Skills**, which ends with **Find more skills** to open Settings › Skills.
- **Voice** buttons: the microphone dictates into the draft, and **Talk** opens the voice bar for a spoken conversation (its menu also offers Live voice). One stretch of speech can run up to five minutes. See [Voice And Buddy](/docs/voice-and-buddy/).

## Apps In A Chat

The apps you connect in [Settings › Apps](/docs/settings/apps) can be used in every chat. **+ › Apps** says how many are on in this chat (such as "2 on", or "None yet") and lists each ready app with its logo and a check box:

- Clear an app's check box to stop this chat using it, and check it again to bring it back. This changes only this chat; other chats and the app's own settings stay as they are. An app you connect later starts checked.
- An app this chat's agent profile doesn't include is listed but can't be checked: "This chat's agent profile doesn't use it."
- Only ready apps are listed. One that needs a sign-in or a key, or is turned off in Settings, appears once it is fixed on its app page.
- A built-in way without chat tools, such as the GitHub account or a channel, is listed without a check box and says why, for example "Used by skills and Developer, not by chat tools."
- **Find more apps** opens Settings › Apps. To start a chat with an app, use **Try it** on its page there: it opens a new chat with a draft that uses the app, and nothing is sent until you send it.

### Mention An App Or A Skill

- Type `@` to mention something. The list's **Apps** group shows this chat's apps with their logos ("Use only this app for this message"), beside **Agents**, **Resources** and **Files**. Mentioning an app focuses that message on it: for that turn Row-Bot uses only the apps you mentioned.
- Type `/` and choose a skill from the **Skills** group. Chosen while your message has other text, `/skill-name` stays in the message and focuses that turn on the skill. Chosen in an empty message, it turns the skill on for the whole chat, and it shows as a skill chip.
- A message can mention up to 8 apps and 8 skills.

Switches and mentions only narrow what a chat can use; they never widen it. The chat's agent profile sets the limit. A mention never turns on an app that is off in this chat, not connected, or outside the profile; a mentioned skill must already be on and allowed by the profile; and approvals still apply as usual.

### When No App Can Do It Yet

If you ask for something none of your apps can do, Row-Bot can suggest apps from its own catalog, the copy kept on this computer. A card says "Row-Bot can do this with one of these apps." (or "with an app." for one) and lists up to three. Each shows what Row-Bot's catalog knows about it, never text from the model or a web page: its logo and name, who publishes it (**by _publisher_** with a check when the service's own vendor publishes it, **Built in**, or **Community · _publisher_**) and its status.

- **Details** opens the app's page in Settings › Apps.
- **Connect** (or **Sign in**, **Set up** or whatever the app needs next) opens the same **Connect _app_** sheet and setup as Settings › Apps, right in the chat, ending with **Here's what _app_ can do** and **Allow**. For an app built into Row-Bot, **Set up** opens its own settings instead.
- An app you added but turned off offers **Turn on** instead of connecting it again. An app set to look things up only offers **Allow changes** when the work is a change.
- When the app is ready, its row offers **Continue**. That sends "It's connected now. Please continue with my request." as your next message.

Suggesting is all Row-Bot does on its own: it looks only in the local catalog, and never installs or connects anything, agrees for you, or asks for keys in the chat. If no app fits, it says so and doesn't point you to websites or downloads.

### App Views

Some apps can show a result as an interactive view, such as a chart, a form or a board, under the step that made it, headed with the app's name and the step. A view runs apart from Row-Bot: it can't see your other chats, files or settings, it loads only from addresses its app declares, which the card lists ("This view also loads from …"), and it opens a link only when you click in it.

- Anything a view asks to do goes through the app's access and this chat's **Approvals**, like any other call. When it must ask, the approval card appears inside the view.
- Turn views off for every app with **Settings › Apps › Advanced › Show app views in chat**, or for one app with **Show views in chat** on its page. Both are on for apps whose setup included a view.
- If a view doesn't open, **Open again** tries again. "Views from this app are off. Turn them on from its page in Apps." means a switch is off: the app's **Show views in chat**, the one in Apps › Advanced, or the app in this chat's **+ › Apps**.

## Tables, Charts And Choices In Answers

When an answer is really data, Row-Bot can show it as a small part of the reply instead of a wall of text: a table, a bar or line chart, a checklist, a few headline numbers, or progress against a target. They follow your light or dark theme and fit a phone.

- **Tables** sort from their headers: click or press Enter on a header for ascending, again for descending, and a third time for the reply's own order. Numbers, money, percentages and dates sort by value. **Copy as CSV** copies the table in the order shown. Every table Row-Bot writes in Markdown sorts the same way.
- **Checklists** and Markdown task lists (`- [ ]`) tick. Your ticks are kept with the chat and follow you to your other devices, but they're yours: Row-Bot doesn't see them unless you tell it.
- **Charts** use the same card as other charts in a chat: **Show data table**, **Download PNG** and **Expand**.
- **Choices**: a reply can end with a few buttons, such as "Groceries · Subscriptions · Next month's budget". A tap sends the button's words as your own message, just as if you'd typed them; nothing else happens and no tool runs. Like **Send**, the buttons wait while Row-Bot is still answering. The button you picked shows **Sent**, and the others switch off. Other parts can carry reply buttons too, such as **Find savings** under a table.
- In Telegram, Slack, WhatsApp and other chat apps, the same parts arrive as plain text: a table as text, a checklist as ticked lines, choices as a numbered list you can answer in words.

### Visuals

When a picture explains something better, Row-Bot can draw it right in the reply: a diagram, or a small interactive explanation such as a slider that shows how savings grow. Each one is labelled **Made by Row-Bot**.

- **Expand** opens it larger, **Open as page** opens it beside the chat as a page, and **Copy source** copies its code.
- A visual runs apart from Row-Bot, like a page: it has no internet, can't see your chats, files or settings, can't open pop-ups or downloads, and can't send anything. One that tries to open another page is stopped.
- In a chat app, a visual arrives as a note that it's in the chat in Row-Bot.

## Pages

Ask for something you'll use rather than read: a plan to approve step by step, a checklist, a dashboard, options to compare, a form or a small calculator. Row-Bot makes it as a **page**, and the chat shows a card such as "Launch plan · page" with **Open**. You don't have to ask for a page: when the answer is a plan, a checklist, a comparison or numbers to track, Row-Bot makes one by itself and keeps its reply short.

- On a computer the page opens beside the chat; on a phone it fills the screen, with **Back** to the chat.
- Approve, change (with a note) or skip steps right in the page. Your decisions gather under it: "3 decisions · Send to Row-Bot". Click the count to see them in words. **Send to Row-Bot** posts them to the chat as one message, marked "Sent from a page". Nothing is sent until you click it, and a decision never approves a tool call: anything that needs approval still asks.
- What a page remembers, such as the ticks on a checklist, is saved with the chat on every device you're signed in on.
- Row-Bot keeps a page current as it works, with progress or fresh numbers; an open page shows the new version. The last 10 versions are kept.
- **Download as HTML** saves a copy that works on its own in any browser (in the desktop app it goes to Row-Bot's Exports folder).
- **Library › Pages** lists every page with its chat.

A page runs apart from Row-Bot: it has no internet, can't see your chats, files or settings, and can't call tools or send anything by itself. Deleting a chat deletes its pages.

## Questions

When the best answer depends on a choice only you can make, such as your budget, a date or what you'll use something for, Row-Bot asks in a card titled **Row-Bot has a question**.

- Each option has a line of description, and Row-Bot tags the one it recommends **Recommended**. **Other…** opens **Write your answer**.
- Several questions show as steps in one card, then **Answer**. Keys 1–4 pick an option and Enter answers.
- **Skip** lets Row-Bot carry on with its recommendation.
- Questions can come from a chat, a helper or a workflow. In Telegram, Discord, Slack and WhatsApp, tap an option, or reply with its number or your own words.
- An answer is never an approval: anything that needs approval still asks.

## Conversations Row-Bot Starts

For longer work that deserves its own chat, Row-Bot can start a conversation of its own, propose one, or message another conversation and hear back.

- **Started**: the new conversation runs its first turn at once and shows in the sidebar with a shared-message icon. Its first message reads **From** and the conversation that started it, with a link. The chat that started it shows a card with its state (working, waiting for you, done) and **Open**. A turn starts at most three.
- **Proposed**: a card with **Start** and **Not now**. Nothing runs until you tap **Start**. A proposal expires after a week.
- **Messages between conversations**: a message to another conversation, a workflow's included (by its name), starts a turn there and shows as **From** the conversation that sent it. When that turn ends, its reply comes back as **Reply from**. A conversation that's busy gets the message after its current turn. An update that needs no answer brings nothing back, and a note for a workflow can wait for its next run.
- **Never you**: a message from another conversation is never your request. It can't approve anything, and under **Auto** the reviewer never reads it as yours. A started conversation keeps the approval level of the chat that started it, or a stricter one, and never **Hands-off**, which only you turn on.
- **Keep going?**: conversations that message each other ten times without you stop and ask you, whatever the approval level.

Helpers stay as they are: quick sub-tasks whose results come back in the same turn.

## Messages While Row-Bot Works

You can keep typing while Row-Bot works. What you send waits above the message box (**1 message waiting · Row-Bot reads it at its next step**), and Row-Bot reads it at its next step, as part of what it is doing: to steer it ("use the blue logo instead"), or to add the next thing to do. Until it is read you can **Edit** or **Discard** it; once read it shows **Row-Bot read this**, and the transcript shows it in its place when the turn ends. A message Row-Bot has no step left to read is sent as the next turn. After **Stop**, waiting messages stay until you send them.

## Conversation Details

The details beside a conversation show what it is working on, its outputs and goal, and, when it has any:

- **Waiting**: what it waits for, each with **Stop waiting**.
- **Running**: its background processes, recordings and video edits, each with **Stop**.
- **Workflow**: for a workflow's conversation, its schedule, next run and last run; the button opens its runs.
- **Linked conversations**: the conversation that started this one, and the ones it started.

**Outputs** shows each thing the conversation made once, whatever it is (a film, a picture, a sound, a document): its final version, or its latest draft marked **Draft**, with its other versions in its **⋯** menu. Recordings, frames, contact sheets and voice lines made on the way stay out of sight until you turn on **Show working files**. **Save to workspace** copies a file, under its own name, into the **Saved outputs** folder of your workspace. **Library › Media** lists the same outputs across conversations, finished ones first, with **Uploads** and **Working files** on their own chips; on a phone, **Chats › Files** does.

## Waiting For Something

A chat can wait for something and carry on by itself when it happens: a background process to finish, a check to pass (a build, a CI run, a deploy, a page showing a word), a time, or another conversation or workflow to finish. Nothing runs while it waits, so it costs nothing.

- **Conversation details** list what it waits for and how often it looks, such as **CI on PR 590 is green · checks every 2 min**, each with **Stop waiting** (with details hidden, one line above the message box says the same). The conversation shows an hourglass in the sidebar, and **Home › Waiting** lists every wait.
- When it happens, a turn starts in that chat: **Checked back: …**, with what happened. If the wait runs out first (2 hours unless Row-Bot set longer, at most a day; a time can be up to a week ahead), the turn says so.
- A check that runs a command asks once, by the chat's approval level, showing the exact command and how often it runs; a read-only command such as `git status` asks nothing. A check never reads Row-Bot's own data.
- Waits for a time or a check survive a restart. A wait for a background process ends when Row-Bot quits, and says so. A chat waits for at most five things at once.

## Attachments

Attach files with **+ › Attach file**, by dropping them on the conversation, or by pasting. Each file shows as a small tile above the text: pictures show a preview, other files their type, name and size. Tiles show upload progress and offer **Retry** if an upload fails. You can keep adding files while others upload; **Send** waits for them. Click a tile to preview it, or × to remove it.

## Context And Usage

The small ring beside **Send** shows how much of the model's context the conversation fills. It appears after the first reply, and the mark on it shows where compaction starts.

- **Hover** over the ring for one line, such as "43% of context · compacts at 88% · 1.2M tokens used, 82% from cache". The tokens are what this conversation's model calls have used so far. The share from cache is how much of their input the provider read from its prompt cache, which providers usually charge less for.
- **Click** the ring for the details: the approximate tokens against the usable amount, where compaction starts, what fills the context, and the conversation's total. When a provider reports a cost, as OpenRouter does, the details show it too; Row-Bot keeps no price list of its own. **Details** at the bottom opens the model's window and the more technical lines.
- On a phone or in a narrow window, the composer is one line, and the context line is in its **+** menu.

For usage beyond one conversation, ask Row-Bot in Agent mode, for example "How many tokens did I use this week?" It answers from its own record: this conversation, the last 24 hours, 7 days and 30 days, with a breakdown by model and by kind of work, such as your chats, compaction, memory extraction and Dream Cycle. The record holds token counts and timings only, never prompts, replies or files. It stays on this computer, counts older than 90 days are removed, and deleting a conversation deletes its counts.

After each reply, the details also show what fills the context, as a thin bar and one line each: **Row-Bot's instructions**, **Tools** (with how many are on), **Skills and guides**, the **Memories** recalled into the conversation, and the **Conversation** itself, including any summary of earlier turns. Each has its approximate tokens and its share, and together they add up to the ring's number. Empty parts are left out, so a Chat Only conversation shows no tools. While a newer count moves the ring, the parts read **As of the last reply**. When the provider reports its prompt cache, a line says how much of the last request came from the cache, and how much over the whole conversation; a local model reports none, and the line is left out. The parts are estimates counted on your computer, and hold numbers only.

### Long Conversations

When a conversation gets long, Row-Bot first clears older tool output from what it sends the model; the steps stay in your transcript. Only when that is no longer enough does it compact the conversation: it summarizes earlier turns and keeps the recent ones. The ring shows **Compacting context…** while that runs.

On a cloud model, Row-Bot writes that summary ahead of time, after a reply, once the conversation is close to the point. When the point comes, the summary is ready and the reply goes on without the pause. The ring's details then say **A summary of older messages is ready**. Nothing else changes: it is the same summary, it counts as compaction in your usage, and it is set aside if you edit an earlier message or change the model. Local models summarize at the point, as before, so a summary never holds your computer's model while you type.

Compaction starts near the end of the model's window, leaving room for the reply and the summary: at about 967,000 tokens on a 1M-token model, and at 167,000 to 177,000 on a 200,000-token one, depending on the provider. Smaller local models keep about a quarter of the window free. A **Cloud reading limit** in [Settings › Models](/docs/settings/models#cloud-reading-limit) makes a cloud model's window smaller; a local model's context is in its own settings.

## The Details Card

**Conversation details** stays open on a wide window as a card under the header's buttons, beside the conversation. With less room it sits in a rail along the conversation's right edge, so it never covers the messages, and the conversation centres in the space beside it. In a narrower window it opens from the header's **Conversation details** button instead. It shows:

- **Working on**: the designs and code folders bound to this conversation. Choose one to open its panel, or unbind it from its **⋯** menu. **Add resource** binds another.
- **Outputs**: each thing the conversation made, its final or its latest draft, with **Show working files** (see [Conversation Details](#conversation-details)).
- **Goal**: the conversation's goal and its progress. Without one, the card shows only a small **Set a goal**. See [Profiles, Goals, And Agents](/docs/profiles-goals-agents/).
- **Agents**: the agents this conversation started, each with its status, **Message** and **Stop**.

Its **⋯** menu offers **Manage conversation**, **Open browser** and **Delete conversation**. After you confirm, the conversation is deleted at once, and **Undo** in the notice brings it back for a few seconds.

## Approvals

When Row-Bot needs your decision, an approval card appears in the conversation with **Approve** and **Deny**. When the action belongs to an app, the card shows the app's logo and name, and so does the tool step for anything an app did. Approvals wait until you answer, and they also show in the sidebar's attention indicator, on Overview and in Buddy, so you can decide from wherever you are. See [Tools, Approvals And Background Work](/docs/chat/tools-approvals-and-terminal).

## Beginner Workflow

1. Start a new chat.
2. Choose a model that is ready for chat.
3. Ask one clear question or task.
4. Attach files only when the task needs them.
5. Review any approval before allowing Row-Bot to act.

## Power Workflow

1. Start a chat with the agent profile for the kind of work.
2. Pick a stronger tool-capable model.
3. Bind the design or code folder you are working on.
4. Set a goal when the work needs several turns.
5. Let Row-Bot use tools, but approve file writes, browser actions, shell commands, account actions, channel sends, MCP calls, and plugin tools deliberately.

## Continue From The Buddy Overlay

In the native Windows and macOS apps, drag Buddy from the sidebar onto the desktop for a compact view of the selected conversation. Its composer shares that conversation's saved draft, model, tools, approval mode, and active response. Simple approvals can appear in the overlay; open the full thread for complex approvals, attachments, transcript history, tool traces, model controls, Talk, or Dictate. See [Settings: Buddy](/docs/settings/buddy).

## Find, Export, And Clean Up

- **Export** in the header opens the conversation's actions: change its **Name**, **Pin** it to the top of the sidebar, or **Export** it as **Markdown** or **PDF**, then **Save export** to choose where the file goes.
- A sidebar row's **⋯** menu exports or deletes one conversation too.
- **Conversation library**, at the end of the sidebar's list, lists every conversation; its **Pages** view lists every page Row-Bot made.
- Its **Media** view lists the pictures, videos and sounds from your chats, newest first, from the same list as each conversation's **Outputs**. **Made** (the default) shows what Row-Bot made for you: each output's final, else its latest draft, and what AI models made. **Uploads** shows the files you added, and **Working files** what was made on the way, such as recordings, frames and voice lines. Search names, tags and chats, show only **Pictures**, **Videos** or **Sound**, and tag an item with the tag button. Each opens its chat. Row-Bot finds them too, and can copy one into another chat or workflow. An incognito chat's files never show there.

In the library, **Search titles and messages** as you type: every matching title comes first, then messages, newest first, with plain-text excerpts; **Continue search** looks further back. Filter by type (All, Chats, Designs, Code, Workflows), and select conversations. The selection bar at the top pins or unpins them, exports them as Markdown or PDF, or deletes them; **Clear selection** (Esc) starts again. Exported files go to Row-Bot's Exports folder; **Show in folder** opens it.

Deleting a conversation stops its running work, then removes its messages, drafts, attachments, media, tool sessions, workflow state and agent state after you confirm. Bound designs and code folders remain. Developer worktrees with changes and sandboxes with unimported work are kept and reported, so deletion does not discard source work. Deleting one conversation from the sidebar or the details card offers **Undo** for a few seconds; deleting a selection in the library asks first ("Delete 3 conversations?") and cannot be undone, so export anything you need before confirming.

## What Is Saved

Conversation names, messages, model choices, per-model reasoning selections, approval mode, profile, attachments copied into Row-Bot-managed storage, and tool results are saved locally. External providers receive prompt content only when you choose their models.

## Privacy And Safety

Local model runs can stay on your machine. Hosted models, web search, browser actions, account tools, MCP servers, plugins, and channels can send data outside the app when configured and used. Row-Bot should not insert secrets into chat; enter credentials only through Settings or the provider's sign-in flow.

## Troubleshooting

- If Row-Bot cannot answer with the current model, choose a more capable model in the picker.
- If the Thinking control is missing or a saved choice resets, read [Reasoning Controls](/docs/chat/reasoning-controls#troubleshooting).
- If attachments are ignored, check that their tiles finished uploading and that they are relevant to the prompt.
- If a tool is unavailable, check the composer's **Mode**, the conversation's agent profile, approval mode, and Settings.
- If an app isn't used, check that it is checked in **+ › Apps** for this chat and that it is **Ready** in [Settings › Apps](/docs/settings/apps). A mention can only narrow a turn to apps the chat already has on.
- If an external tool is enabled but not selected automatically, use a more specific request or review [Progressive Tools And Skills](/docs/guides/progressive-tools-and-skills).
- If a reply is stuck, press **Stop**, then retry with a narrower prompt.

## Model Picker

Route: /docs/chat/model-picker

Choose a conversation's model from one list across local, subscription, pay-per-use and custom providers, and troubleshoot missing models.

# Model Picker

The model picker in the composer chooses which model answers in the current conversation. It is where provider setup becomes visible in day-to-day use.

## Where Models Come From

Models appear after Row-Bot discovers them from a connected provider or local runtime:

- Local Ollama models come from the Ollama service running on your computer.
- Subscription models come from your ChatGPT or Grok plan, signed in from Settings › Models, or your Claude plan through Claude Code, which you sign in to with Claude's own sign-in (**Use my Claude plan**).
- Pay-per-use models come from a provider connected with an API key in Settings › Models.
- Custom endpoint models come from the compatible endpoint details you provide.
- Your models, the ones you starred, appear first.

The same list is used everywhere a model is chosen: the composer, and the Main model, Vision, Image and Video pickers in Settings › Models.

## Using The Picker

- **Your models** and **Recent** (the models you used last) come first, then every other model you can choose, under its provider: the models Settings › Models counts.
- **Search models** searches every connected provider's models, not only the ones listed: what isn't listed appears under **All models**, and you can choose it for this conversation.
- In search results, a model that several providers offer, such as Claude through Anthropic, OpenRouter and Requesty, is one row. It shows one way to reach it: the model you're using, then a starred one, then your plan, this computer, the maker's own API, and a router last. **+2 routes** (or the right arrow) lists the others with how each is paid for; choose any of them. Row-Bot never switches routes by itself.
- Models are grouped by provider, each marked **Connected** or **Not connected**, and tagged with how they are paid for: **Subscription**, **Pay per use**, **Credits**, or **Local · free** (runs on this computer).
- **Connect** on a model whose provider isn't connected, and **Reconnect** on one that stopped working, open that provider in Settings › Models.
- A model that can't be used right now, for example because its provider is disconnected, shows as **Unavailable** with the reason.
- **Chat only** marks models that can't use tools.
- The choice applies to this conversation only; it doesn't change your default model in Settings › Models.

## Choosing Well

Use a smaller or local model for quick private chats. Use a stronger tool-capable model for workflows, designs, code folders, long context, or multi-step tool use. For local and self-hosted endpoints, prefer a context window large enough for Row-Bot's instructions and tool schemas.

Reasoning choices belong to the exact provider-qualified model, not just its display name. After choosing a supported model, use the conditional Thinking control described in [Reasoning Controls](/docs/chat/reasoning-controls).

## Your Models

- A model row's **star** (or Shift+F10 on it) adds it to **Your models** or takes it out.
- Your models are listed first in every picker. Once you star a model from a provider, that provider's other models leave the pickers; they stay in Settings › Models.
- The model you chose as your main model is always listed.
- **Settings › Models** does the same with each model's star. See [Settings › Models](/docs/settings/models#catalog).

## Troubleshooting

- If the picker says there are no models yet, choose how Row-Bot thinks in Setup, or connect a provider in Settings › Models › Add a provider.
- If a model is missing, open its provider in Settings › Models and refresh its model list.
- If a model shows as unavailable, read its reason; reconnecting its provider usually fixes it.
- If a model appears but fails with tools, choose a model that isn't marked **Chat only**.
- If custom endpoint models look duplicated, use the provider-qualified name.

## Reasoning Controls

Route: /docs/chat/reasoning-controls

Choose provider-aware reasoning effort, thinking toggles, and token budgets for the active Row-Bot model.

# Reasoning Controls

Reasoning controls let you change how much supported models reason before answering without switching models. Row-Bot shows only choices that the exact provider-qualified model reports or that Row-Bot can identify from a maintained model route.

## Where To Find The Control

- In every conversation, including those working on a design or code folder, the **Thinking** control sits beside the model picker in the composer. In narrow windows, the composer progressively compacts labels while keeping each icon paired with its own menu.
- On a phone, the composer's controls fold into a smaller set of buttons; Thinking still appears next to Model when the selected model supports it.
- In Chat or a connected messaging channel, use `/reasoning` to inspect the current choice and the valid choices for the active model.

The control is intentionally absent when Row-Bot does not have exact, actionable reasoning capability data for the selected model. A generic model name or a provider-wide assumption is not enough.

## What The Choices Mean

| Choice | Effect |
| --- | --- |
| Provider default | Sends no per-thread reasoning override and lets the provider or endpoint choose its normal behavior. This is the safest compatibility choice. |
| Low, Medium, High, XHigh, or another effort | Requests one of the exact effort levels supported by the selected model. The list varies by model. |
| On or Off | Enables or disables thinking only when that model exposes a true toggle. Models with mandatory reasoning do not offer Off. |
| Token budget | Sets a positive reasoning-token budget within the minimum and maximum reported for that model. This appears only for budget-capable models. |

More reasoning can increase latency and provider token usage. It can help with planning, coding, analysis, and multi-step tool use, but a higher setting is not automatically better for every request.

## Scope And Persistence

A selection is saved locally for one thread and one exact provider-qualified model. Switching models does not apply an incompatible value to the new model. If you return to a model in the same thread, Row-Bot can restore that model's valid saved choice.

A new conversation starts on the choice you last made for each model, in the app or with `/reasoning`; choosing **Provider default** forgets it. Conversations you already have keep their own choice.

Changing the global default model does not rewrite existing thread choices. Conversations working on designs and code folders use the same thread-scoped behavior as any other conversation.

Your choice applies to the conversation's own replies. Row-Bot's background work, such as checking a goal's progress, compacting a long conversation, memory extraction and Dream Cycle, uses the lowest effort that model offers instead, when Row-Bot knows its choices. Otherwise, or if the model refuses it, background work uses Provider default.

## Slash And Channel Commands

Run `/reasoning` with no argument, or `/reasoning status`, to show the active setting and valid choices. Supported examples include:

```text
/reasoning high
/reasoning default
/reasoning on
/reasoning off
/reasoning budget 4096
```

Row-Bot validates the command against the active model. Unsupported efforts, toggles, or budgets are rejected without replacing the previous valid selection. Messaging channels use their conversation's active thread and model, so the setting remains isolated from unrelated chats.

## Providers And Custom Endpoints

Row-Bot maps native reasoning controls for supported OpenAI and Codex, Anthropic and Claude (your Claude plan), xAI, Google, Ollama and Ollama Cloud, OpenRouter, and compatible endpoint routes when exact capability data is available. Available models and choices can change as provider catalogs change; the control itself is the authoritative list for the selected model.

For a custom OpenAI-compatible endpoint, open **Settings -> Providers**, edit or add the endpoint, then expand **Advanced -> Reasoning**. Keep **Reasoning mode** on Auto unless the endpoint's metadata is missing or wrong. Thinking budget, returned reasoning content, replay, and extra request JSON are advanced compatibility settings that apply to every model exposed by that endpoint. Enable replay only when the endpoint explicitly supports receiving preserved reasoning history.

A Qwen3, Qwen3.5 or Qwen3.8 model on a llama.cpp, vLLM or SGLang server on this computer, including Row-Bot's own **Run on this computer** models, gets **On** and **Off** in the chat, and that choice wins over the endpoint's **Reasoning mode**. LM Studio's chat API doesn't take a per-request thinking switch, so its models keep the endpoint-wide setting. On **Run on this computer**, every model thinks by default.

## Responses And Compatibility Fallback

When a provider returns reasoning content, Row-Bot can stream it separately and retain it as a collapsed **Thinking** section instead of mixing it into the final answer.

If a provider rejects a valid-looking explicit reasoning choice before returning response content, Row-Bot retries once with Provider default, clears the rejected saved override (new conversations stop starting on it too), and shows a notice. Authentication failures, rate limits, timeouts, cancellations, and server failures are not silently retried as reasoning compatibility problems.

## Privacy And Safety

The selected control is stored locally with thread settings, but hosted providers receive the resulting reasoning parameter and may bill for additional tokens. Reasoning content returned by a provider can contain sensitive intermediate material. Do not enable reasoning replay for a custom endpoint unless you trust that endpoint and understand its message format.

## Troubleshooting

- **The control is missing:** confirm the active model is provider-qualified, refresh Providers and Models, and check that its catalog entry exposes exact reasoning capabilities.
- **A choice disappeared after switching models:** choices are model-specific; inspect the new model's menu or run `/reasoning`.
- **A saved choice reset to Provider default:** the provider rejected it or refreshed capability metadata no longer supports it. Read the notice, refresh the catalog, and choose from the current list.
- **A custom endpoint returns reasoning in the wrong place:** review its Advanced Reasoning settings, especially returned reasoning content and replay. Keep replay off unless required.
- **High reasoning is slow or expensive:** choose a lower supported effort, a smaller budget, or Provider default.

## Tools, Approvals And Background Work

Route: /docs/chat/tools-approvals-and-terminal

Row-Bot's tools and tool steps, the approval levels, background processes, Row-Bot's browser, video editing, images, sending files, and the terminal.

# Tools, Approvals And Background Work

Tools are actions Row-Bot can take beyond writing text. They can search documents, read files, use a browser, run commands, work on designs and code folders, inspect knowledge, call MCP servers, use plugins, or send through channels.

## Progressive Discovery

With **Only the ones a request needs (recommended)** in Settings › Tools, the tools Row-Bot uses all the time are always there, and it finds the rest when a request needs them: enabled MCP, plugin, Custom Tool and channel tools, and rarely used built-in ones such as the tracker, video editing or the updater. Each tool's guide is read when the tool is first needed. This keeps a new chat's first request small, so the first reply comes sooner. Once a conversation makes a video, a picture or a sound, its media tools (video, video editing, voice and music, recording, and showing and sending files) stay ready for the rest of that conversation, so Row-Bot never has to find them again (on a small model, the ones it has used and presenting do).

Discovery does not widen permissions. The selected provider, Agent Profile, workspace policy, approval mode, and execution budget still apply. Live and reopened traces group results under the real integration name. See [Progressive Tools And Skills](/docs/guides/progressive-tools-and-skills) for the complete flow and the eager compatibility option.

## How Tool Use Appears

When Row-Bot uses tools, the turn shows a tool step: what Row-Bot tried, what came back, and whether more action is needed. A step that used an app starts with that app's logo and name. Open it for each call's details. Each result also records whether approval was needed, given or denied, so Row-Bot reports it truthfully. A denied action shows as skipped, never as done, and Row-Bot is told that it did not run.

### Finished Work And Working Files

When Row-Bot finishes what you asked for (a film, a picture, a page or a document), it presents it: the final shows large in the reply that delivers it, under its name, marked **Final**. Pictures and clips an AI model makes show as they're made. A video Row-Bot is still working on shows once, as one card that updates in place in the reply that last made or changed it, and plays once it's made.

What Row-Bot makes on the way doesn't fill the conversation: screen recordings, video edits, frames, contact sheets, voice lines and test renders fold into one row under that reply's steps, such as **12 working files**, which opens them. They stay in the conversation's files, and **Outputs** shows them with **Show working files** (see [Conversation Details](/docs/chat/#conversation-details)). A recording or a voice file you asked for is itself the final, and shows.

## Approvals

Approval cards appear when an action can change local files, run commands, contact external systems, use accounts, start servers, send messages, call MCP or plugin tools, or do something else that deserves review. The composer's **Approvals** control sets the level for the conversation.

A new conversation, workflow or Developer workspace starts at the level you last chose for a conversation (in the app, with **Use Auto in this chat** on a card, or with `/approval` in a channel), and at **Auto** until you choose one. Hands-off is turned on in each conversation, so after it new ones start at **Auto**. A conversation another conversation starts takes that conversation's level, Auto at most. Conversations you already have keep their level.

### Approval Levels

| Level | What happens to an action that needs approval |
| --- | --- |
| **Ask** | You approve each one on its card. |
| **Auto** (the default) | A reviewer approves what clearly matches what you asked for in this conversation; anything else, and anything it isn't sure of, asks you. |
| **Hands-off** | Every action runs without asking, and each one is recorded. |
| **Block** | Anything that would change something is refused. |

**Auto's reviewer** is one short call to the conversation's own model at its lowest effort, made just before the action. It sees only your own recent messages in the conversation (or a workflow's saved steps), the folder in play and the action as its card describes it, never tool results, web pages, files or app output, so text an action picked up can't talk it into approving. A message, email or file to someone you named, saying what you asked for, is within your request, and so is reading your data or capturing the screen when the task needs it. It asks you when an action goes beyond your request, reaches people you didn't name, posts publicly, moves money, grants access or changes permissions, deletes something you didn't ask to change, or when it can't decide: an error, no answer within 30 seconds or no model available all mean it asks. When it asks, the card says why ("The reviewer asked you: …"). Actions it approved show **Reviewer approved** in the conversation's tool steps, with its reason in the step's details. Read-only actions never reach it.

**Hands-off** skips every approval, including screen and camera captures, high-impact app actions and reading Row-Bot's own data when that setting is on, and workflows don't pause for approval. The first time you choose it, a dialog lists what it skips; after **Turn on** it doesn't ask again on this computer. While it's on, the Approvals control reads **Hands-off** in a warning colour, and Buddy says so while work runs. Each action that would have asked shows **Hands-off** in the tool steps. A conversation other people share (a Slack or Discord channel thread, or a group chat) runs on **Auto** at most, and Hands-off can only be turned on in the app, not with a channel command.

No level changes these limits: blocked commands, **Block**, capabilities switched off in Settings (such as the data-folder setting, or an app turned off in the chat), plugin isolation, the Developer sandbox's checks and network setting, a read-only helper's refusals, and secrets never being shown. Conversations, profiles and workflows saved with the old **Auto** use the reviewed Auto; nothing moves to Hands-off unless you choose it.

For the whole safety design in one place, and what is not a boundary, see [How Row-Bot Keeps An Agent In Bounds](/docs/privacy-safety/agent-in-bounds).

An app's tools also follow the access you chose for it in [Settings › Apps](/docs/settings/apps): **Read only**, **Ask before changes** or **Full access**. Deleting, sending, paying, publishing, running code and unknown actions ask first whichever access you choose. An approval card for an app's action shows the app's logo and name above the question, with **Details**, **Deny** and **Approve**. Under **Auto**, these go to the reviewer, which is told the app's access says to ask. Turning an app on or off for a chat, or mentioning it, never skips an approval; see [Apps in a chat](/docs/chat/#apps-in-a-chat).

**Approvals wait until you answer.** They no longer expire after a set time; a workflow step that sets its own time limit still honours it. Each one shows how long it has been waiting.

**Answer them where you are.** Every waiting approval, from this conversation, another conversation, a workflow or a delegated agent, shows with **Approve** and **Deny** in place:

- in its conversation, as an approval card;
- in the sidebar's attention indicator ("1 approval is waiting"), which opens the list;
- in Overview's **Needs you** card;
- in Buddy, including the desktop overlay;
- in the channel a workflow or channel-started task came from, when that channel supports approvals;
- on a phone that turned on **Notifications on this device** in Settings › Devices, as a notice such as "Approval needed: Send email to Sam?" that opens the conversation (see [Notifications On A Phone](/docs/privacy-safety#notifications-on-a-phone)).

A floating notice also says when a new one arrives. An answer in one place resolves it everywhere. When a delegated agent needs approval, its parent conversation shows it too. The card may include a short reason written by the model, but Row-Bot's approval policy still decides whether the action is blocked, allowed, or waiting for you.

Before approving, check:

- What action is being requested.
- What file, folder, account, channel, server, or provider is involved.
- Whether the action can send data outside the app.
- Whether the proposed command or file change matches your request.
- Whether denying is safer until you inspect settings.

Approving lets Row-Bot continue that action. Denying stops that action and returns control to the conversation.

An approval card offers **Details**, **Deny** and **Approve** (⌘/Ctrl+Enter), and in a chat also:

- **Allow in this chat**: approves this, and later actions of the same kind in this conversation, without asking again (commands count by what they do, so allowing `npm test` doesn't allow `git push`). It also covers the conversation's helper agents and, in a workflow's own chat, the workflow's later runs, and under **Auto** those actions skip the reviewer. It ends when the conversation is deleted or Row-Bot restarts. Sending, posting, sharing, deleting, paying, pushing or opening a pull request, reading Row-Bot's private data, high-risk app actions and anything only you can approve always ask.
- **Always allow…** (the ∞ icon, or **More choices** on a phone): approves this now and from now on, in any of your chats, until you turn it off. Before you save it, the sheet shows what the rule would have covered in the last 30 days, with any action you said no to first.
- **Use Auto in this chat** (under **Ask**): approves this and switches the chat to reviewed **Auto**.

### Always Allow

An Always allow rule is offered only for three kinds of action, decided by Row-Bot from the action itself:

- **An app's routine change**, such as **Notion › Create a page**: one tool of one app, and only a tool Row-Bot sees as an ordinary change (never one that deletes, sends or that it can't place).
- **One exact command in one folder**, such as `npm test` in **row-bot**: that text exactly, with no other command joined to it, and never an install, network use, a delete, a commit, a push, a pull request or a server.
- **Moving and renaming files** inside your workspace folder.

A rule applies under **Ask** and **Auto** (it skips the reviewer), never under **Block**, never in a chat other people share (a Slack or Discord channel thread, a group chat) and never to an action only you can approve. The step shows **Your rule**, and Settings › System › Activity shows **Allowed by your rule**.

**Settings › System › Activity › Always allow** lists your rules (at most 100) with how often each was used. Switch one off, delete it, or edit a command rule's exact command: the new command is checked like a new rule, and the sheet shows what it would have covered. A rule only ever starts from an approval card. If Row-Bot can't read your rules, nothing is allowed by them: every action asks as usual.

### Settings Row-Bot Changes

A setting Row-Bot would change, such as the Dream Cycle hours or turning on a tool, asks on a card that shows what it is now and what it becomes, with **Show in Settings**. Under **Auto**, turning on Shell, file tools, Browser, Computer use or MCP apps always asks you. After the change, its card offers **Undo**. See [Ask Row-Bot About Row-Bot](/docs/chat/about-row-bot).

### Files Outside The Workspace

Row-Bot's file tools work in the workspace folder. Give a full path elsewhere on this computer, such as `D:\Videos\trip.mp4`, and they ask first by the approval level, the card saying **Outside the workspace** and naming the paths. Row-Bot's own data folder is never read or changed this way. The video and picture tools take such a path too and read the file where it is, asking the same way; saving an edit and sending a file use the workspace, so Row-Bot copies a file in or out first (which asks).

### What Asks In A Code Folder

- A Developer command that isn't on the read-only list (such as `ls`, `git status`, `git diff` or `node --version`) counts as running a command: **Ask** asks ("Run a command?"), **Auto**'s reviewer decides or asks, **Hands-off** runs it, **Block** refuses it. Installs, deletes, network use, Git commits and pushes, and starting a server keep their own checks.
