- **Apply the sandbox changes?** applies every sandbox change waiting in this conversation, oldest first, with one approval.
- **Open a pull request?** opens one with the GitHub command-line tool (`gh`) on this computer, as a draft unless you ask otherwise. It follows the conversation's approvals, and needs `gh` installed and signed in.
- The Custom Tool Builder asks before it tests, installs dependencies for, creates, turns on or offers a custom tool in chats, and the card lists the commands it will run on this computer.

### Row-Bot's Own Data Folder

Row-Bot's data folder holds your conversations, settings and keys, so the Shell tool refuses commands that name it, and file tools refuse paths inside it. To let the agent read it, turn on **Let the agent read Row-Bot's data folder** in [Settings › System](/docs/settings/system) › Advanced; such commands then ask you under **Ask**; under **Auto** the reviewer approves one only when you clearly asked for it, **Hands-off** runs them, and **Block** still refuses them. With the setting off, no level reads the folder.

## Background Processes

Row-Bot can start a program that keeps running after its reply, such as a development server or a file watcher, in any folder and with extra environment variables. Starting one asks exactly as running a command does: **Ask** asks ("Start a background process?", with the command, its variables and the folder), **Auto**'s reviewer decides or asks, **Hands-off** starts it, and **Block** refuses anything that isn't read-only. Blocked commands and Row-Bot's own data folder stay out of reach at every level, through a variable's value or the folder too.

A command that is still running after 2 minutes, such as a long build or a download, carries on in the background the same way instead of holding up the reply. Row-Bot can also start a long command in the background straight away.

- **In the conversation**, the step leaves a card: what runs, for how long, the local address it serves (such as `localhost:5173`), **View output** and **Stop**. Once it ends, the card says how: finished, failed, or stopped and by whom. The exit code and process number are under **Details** in **View output**.
- **Home › Monitor › Background processes** lists every one with the conversation it belongs to, a **Stop** for each and **Stop all**; finished ones fold under **Recently finished**.
- **Stopping** ends the process and everything it started, and needs no approval. Row-Bot can stop only the processes of the conversation it is working in; you can stop any of them.
- **Limits**: at most 5 run at once in a conversation, and 12 in all. Each keeps the latest 4 MB of its output; Row-Bot reads the end and pages through the rest.
- **Row-Bot quitting** stops every background process, and deleting a conversation stops its own. If Row-Bot closed unexpectedly and left one running, it stops it on the next start and says so in Monitor's start-up warnings.

An app that a finished command opened (an editor, say) keeps running, as before; stopping a command that is still running ends everything it started.

## Row-Bot's Browser

Row-Bot's browser is Chromium with Row-Bot's own profile (your installed Chrome or Edge, or Row-Bot's own browser if neither is installed). It has no window of its own: you watch it in the **Browser pane** beside the chat, where you stay signed in to sites. Besides opening websites, it can open apps you run on this computer, take screenshots, show a page at a phone or tablet size, and record what it does.

### The Browser Pane

While a turn uses the browser, the chat shows **Using the browser · site** with a small live picture; tap it (or **⋯ › Open browser**) to open the pane. It shows the page live, with tabs, an address bar, **Back**, **Forward** and **Reload**. **Pop out** opens it in its own window (a new tab in a web browser). On a phone it fills the screen.

- **The page fits the pane**: sites lay out for the pane's size, docked, full screen or popped out, so they read as they would in a window that size. With the pane closed, the page is an ordinary desktop window.
- **One line says who's driving**: what Row-Bot is doing now ("Row-Bot: Clicking "Next"") with **Take control** and **Stop**, or **You have control** with **Give back**.
- **Click, type and scroll in the page yourself.** Doing so takes control; Row-Bot waits until you give it back.
- **Paste** with Ctrl+V (⌘V on a Mac) after clicking a field, or with **⋯ › Paste into the page**. The page gets it as its own paste, so a sign-in code split into boxes fills them all.
- **Signing in is yours.** Row-Bot never types a password, one-time code or card number. When a page asks for one, the pane says **Sign in here** and Row-Bot asks you in the chat. Sign-ins last across restarts, so it's usually once per site.
- **It works from any signed-in device**, and stops streaming whenever the pane is hidden.
- **If the browser stops**, the pane says "Row-Bot's browser stopped. Restart it?" with **Restart**. Your sign-ins stay.
- **Show Row-Bot how** (the toolbar's icon button; on a phone, **⋯ More browser actions**) records the steps of a task you do yourself and turns them into a skill you review. Passwords, codes and card numbers are never kept, and narration is transcribed on this computer only. See [Show Row-Bot How](/docs/skills/#show-row-bot-how).

### What Asks First

Most of what Row-Bot does on a page just runs, as you would click it. Paying, buying, booking with a charge, sending, posting, deleting and changing account settings ask first, with a card that says what will happen on which site and shows the page. **Ask** asks you, **Auto**'s reviewer approves only what clearly matches what you asked for (and asks you otherwise), **Hands-off** runs it, and **Block** refuses. Uploading a file to a site asks too.

### Signed-In Sites

**Settings › System › Browser and computer use** lists the sites you're signed in to in Row-Bot's browser, with **Sign out** for one and **Sign out of all**. The pane's **⋯** menu has the same list.

### Apps On This Computer

An address on this computer, such as `localhost:5173` or `127.0.0.1:8000`, or on your network, such as a router, a file server, another computer, a Tailscale address or an intranet name like `http://jira`, opens only once it's allowed in that conversation. An address you type in the Browser pane yourself opens at once. **Ask** asks ("Allow Row-Bot's browser to open localhost:5173 in this chat?"), **Auto**'s reviewer decides or asks, **Hands-off** allows it, and **Block** refuses. A server Row-Bot started in the same conversation, and that is listening on that port, opens without asking; an address a program only printed doesn't count.

- **One address, one conversation, one hour.** Another port, or another conversation, asks again. The server's live-reload connection (same address) is included.
- **The list and Remove**: the Browser pane's **⋯ › Addresses on this computer** lists each allowed address, who allowed it and when it ends, with **Remove**.
- **Once allowed, the app works as any site does**: its forms and uploads included. Paying, sending, deleting and the rest still ask first.
- **Reading a page shares it**: an address allowed in the browser can be read with the URL reader in that conversation, and one allowed while reading opens in the browser. The URL reader asks the same way ("Allow Row-Bot to read localhost:5173 in this chat?").
- **Never allowed**: cloud metadata addresses (they hand out a computer's own credentials) and Row-Bot's own app. Row-Bot says so instead of asking.
- **Files**: a `file://` page doesn't open, since it could show any other file on this computer. To preview a page Row-Bot built, it starts a server in the page's folder in that conversation (such as `python -m http.server 8000`) and opens `http://localhost:8000`, which opens without asking.

### Screenshots And Page Sizes

Ask for a screenshot and Row-Bot saves a picture of the page (what's on screen, or the whole page) to the conversation's files and shows it in the chat. Password, one-time code and card fields are covered. Very long pages stop at about 10,000 pixels.

Row-Bot can also show the page at **phone**, **tablet** or **desktop** size (and another device scale) to check a responsive layout. The size stays until it's changed. Screenshots and page sizes only read Row-Bot's own browser, so they need no approval.

### Recordings

Ask Row-Bot to record what it does in its browser and it asks first, then records the conversation's page to a video saved to the conversation's files. Recording the whole screen works through [Computer Use](/docs/computer-use) and needs it set up.

- **While it records**, the conversation shows **Recording · 0:42** with **Stop**, and Buddy shows **Recording the browser** (or **the screen**).
- **It stops** when Row-Bot or you stop it, at its time limit (5 minutes unless asked otherwise; at most an hour), before the video gets too large for the chat (200 MB), when its conversation is deleted, and when Row-Bot quits. Stopping needs no approval.
- **The video** (MP4) is saved to the conversation's files, with a player, among the reply's working files. When the recording is what you asked for, Row-Bot shows it as the final.
- **Made to be watched**: browser recordings are 1920×1080 at 30 frames a second, sharp enough to zoom in on. While one records, the page keeps that 16:9 desktop size whatever size the Browser pane is (a phone or tablet size Row-Bot chose stays that shape), so the video fills its frame. While one records, Row-Bot's clicks, typing and scrolling go at a viewer's pace, and a drawn pointer glides to each control and rings where it clicks.
- **Beats**: as it works, Row-Bot marks moments as **live** (worth watching as it happens), **work** (a wait or busy stretch) or **cut** (leave it out). Ask for a video of the recording and Row-Bot makes one from its beats: live stretches as they happened, work sped up 4× with its badge, cuts left out. Edit it in the Video panel like any other.
- **Hidden in browser recordings**: pages with a password, one-time code or card field, and anything shown while you've taken over the browser, record as a blank frame.
- Recording needs Row-Bot's video support, which comes with the full install; Row-Bot says so if it's missing.

## Pictures And Clips Made By AI

Row-Bot makes pictures and short video clips with the image and video models you choose in [Settings › Models](/docs/settings/models), and each shows in the reply as it's made. To keep shots alike, it can give a model up to three reference pictures (a person, a product, a place), a saved character or style, a picture for the shot to end on, or an earlier clip to carry on. Each model gets only what its provider offers, and the result says what it left out. To save a character or a style, tag its picture in Library › Media `character: maya` or `style: noir`. A clip is made at the highest resolution the model offers for its length, up to 1080p, unless you ask for another; pictures can also be 16:9, 9:16 or 4:5.

## Video Editing

Row-Bot can edit videos you already have: its recordings, files in the conversation, and videos in the workspace folder (the one the file tools use; a conversation's code folder is for Developer work). Ask for the result you want, for example "cut the demo to the sign-up, speed up the typing with a label and add captions". One edit can trim, join several videos, speed up or slow down a part (with a visible "2×" label), add text badges and titles, zoom in on a detail for a while, crop, burn in captions, or take stills, and lay its sound: voice lines at their moments, music under them that dips while a voice speaks, and the video's own sound up or down, all brought to one even loudness. The result is an H.264 MP4 saved to the conversation's files, so nothing you have is replaced.

- **In the conversation**, the step leaves a card among the reply's working files: what the edit does, its progress and **Stop** while it's made, then the video with a player and **Download**. Stills are one contact sheet. **Details** says which ffmpeg made it. The finished video shows large in the reply.
- **Checks**: every video Row-Bot makes gets the finished check, and you can ask for it on any video. It measures the loudness (−23 to −9 LUFS, peaks under −1 dBTP), finds black, frozen and quiet stretches, and has your own vision model (**Settings › Models**) look once at a sheet of its frames for unreadable or cut-off words, zooms that miss, pictures that don't fit what's said and warped AI shots. With no vision model that look is skipped, and the check says so. Each finding names its scene and time and what to do; Row-Bot fixes those and makes the video again before it says it's ready, and tells you what's left if a problem is still listed after two tries.
- **Long edits** carry on in the background, so the reply isn't held up; they also show in **Home › Monitor › Background processes**. Stopping one needs no approval and saves nothing.
- **Into the workspace**: ask Row-Bot to save a finished edit there. Replacing a file that's already there asks first. A video keeps one name everywhere: its versions share it in the conversation, and saving or sending it uses the same name.
- Edits stop when their conversation is deleted and when Row-Bot quits. A result larger than a conversation can hold (200 MB) isn't saved; Row-Bot says how to make it smaller.

### The Video Panel

For a video with several parts, such as a demo, a tutorial or a reel, Row-Bot makes a **video project**: the video as scenes. Each scene's footage is a piece of a video (a recording, an AI shot, or a clip from the chat, the workspace or anywhere on this computer) or a picture (a photo, a screenshot, generated art), held with a slow push in, with its speed, a zoom on part of the picture, a title card over its first seconds, and its line: the words said over it, in your voice from **Settings › Voice**. Music can play under the whole video and dips while a line is said. The video is saved to the chat's files, and Row-Bot reads its checks before it says it's done.

- **Any footage**: clips from the workspace or elsewhere on this computer are used where they are, never copied into the chat, so a long 4K phone clip is fine and only the parts used are read. A file elsewhere is asked about by the approval level when it joins a video; that video then reads only that file, and any other file elsewhere asks again. If footage is moved or deleted later, the video names the scene that needs it. Clips of any shape, frame rate, colour or orientation play as one film, cropped to fill the frame, upright. A video holds up to 200 scenes from up to 100 videos and pictures.
- **Storyboard**: ask Row-Bot to make a video and it makes it; ask it to plan, draft or storyboard one, or to work on it together, and a video of several scenes starts as a storyboard, with nothing made yet: a one-line logline, then a card per scene with its footage (a clip, a picture, an AI shot, a title card or a screen recording), a frame of it, what it shows, its length, its line and its music cue. Approve a card, comment on it ("make this one moodier": your words reach Row-Bot in the chat), swap it to other footage, or ask for a new take of an AI shot or picture. **Make video** makes it; footage still to make, such as an AI shot, Row-Bot makes first. A quick change, a video of one scene, or a video a workflow makes is made at once.
- **In the chat**, the video has one card, with its name, its version and whether it's made, and once it's made it plays there. The card follows the newest version, so a draft updates in place, and it folds into the working files of the reply that presents the finished video. **Open** shows it in the **Video** panel beside the chat (full screen on a phone).
- **The player** plays the version shown, with frame steps, **Loop** and **Download**. Tap a scene's frame to play from there. While you edit, it previews your edits at once instead: each scene's own video from its start to its end at its speed, zoomed in, with its card, its caption and its voice. A line you changed is said once the video is made.
- **Scenes**: change a line and it's said again when the video is made; set a scene's speed (2× and faster shows a badge) or its card; move scenes up or down, remove one, or trim it under **Trim**. **Captions** shows each line under its scene. Nothing changes until you save: **Save** keeps a storyboard's changes, and **Save and make** makes a made video again. Making it again draws only the scenes that changed, and the panel says which were made again and which were reused.
- **Timeline** (on a computer, one click from **Storyboard**): the scenes as blocks on tracks for the video, the lines, the title cards and the music, sized by their length. Drag a block's edges to trim it, drag a block to move it, click one to play from it, and zoom with the slider. Keys: Space plays, J and L step back and on, K pauses, I and O set the selected scene's start and end at the playhead, S splits it there, Delete removes it and Ctrl+Z undoes.
- **Versions**: every change, yours or Row-Bot's, is a new version with a note of what changed, and the panel marks the scenes it changed. Go back to the version before in one tap, or pick an older one and choose **Use this version**. Going back is a new version too, so nothing is lost.
- **Review**: once a version is made, its checks show, by scene and time: a scene shown more than 2× larger than its footage (soft), words over what's being done or over a face, words in a tall or square video's edges where apps lay their buttons, the loudness, and black or frozen stretches. Lines starting **Check** are worth a look but don't hold the video back: a scene shown 1.5 to 2× larger (a little soft), a jump cut inside a scene, an AI shot that may not look like the others of its character or style (tagged `character: …` or `style: …` in Library › Media), and what the vision model saw on its review sheet (the frames of each scene, in the chat's files). **Save to workspace** and **Post to X** ask Row-Bot in the chat, so posting shows its card first, with its own approval.
- **Brand kit**: one look for every video, under **Brand kit** in the panel: a colour for title cards and speed badges, how captions show (in a box, bold and outlined, or large and centred), a logo from your pictures in Library › Media in a corner, an intro and an outro card on the colour, and the music mood Row-Bot picks. Changes apply the next time a video is made; turn **Brand** off for one version to make it plain.
- **Recordings**: a scene from a recording of Row-Bot's browser, or of your screen while Row-Bot uses the computer, eases in on each click and rings the control; where a control is too big to zoom to, the rest of the picture dims around it. **Camera** in the brand kit sets this for every video (**Follows what is done**, **Spotlights what is done**: no zoom, the rest dimmed, or **Stays still**), and you can ask Row-Bot for one video. Row-Bot's browser records at twice the page's size, so a zoom stays sharp; the video is the usual size. A recording with no beats marked becomes a scene for each burst of what was done, the waits between sped up.
- **Other shapes**: under the review, make the same version **Wide 16:9** (X, YouTube), **Tall 9:16** (Shorts, Reels), **Square 1:1** or **Portrait 4:5** (Instagram, Facebook), each scene reframed around its zoom with its words kept clear of that shape's edges, or a **GIF**. Each says where it fits and warns when the video is longer than that place allows. Download each once it's made. Ask Row-Bot for a shape and it does the same.
- **Ready to publish**: name where a video is going (YouTube, Shorts, TikTok, Reels, Instagram, Facebook, X or LinkedIn), in the chat or with **Ready to publish** under the review, and Row-Bot makes its publish kit; it makes none until you do. The kit has the video in each place's shape, a thumbnail in that shape (a picture Row-Bot made with your image model, or a still of the video, with the video's name in your brand kit's title style), a title and a description to copy (a YouTube video's lists its chapters), and subtitles as SRT and WebVTT from what's said in it. Posting stays with you, or with an app such as X or YouTube, which shows the post and asks first.
- Making a video needs ffmpeg: Row-Bot asks to download it the first time it makes one.

### Voice, Music And Transcripts

Three tools make the pieces a video needs, on this computer, and save each in the chat's files by name, so a video edit or **Send to my phone** uses it.

- **Voice files** (`speak`): Row-Bot's local voice reads a script whole, never cut short like a spoken reply. Choose a voice and a speed, and say how to pronounce words (for example "Qwen" as "Kwen"). It needs the Kokoro voice from **Settings › Voice**.
- **Music** (`make_music`): original, royalty-free background music for a video's length, made on this computer from no samples. Pick a mood (calm, upbeat, focused or warm) and the moments it should build.
- **Transcripts** (`transcribe`): local Whisper writes down what's said in a recording or a clip, with each line's time, and saves subtitles (`.srt`). It needs the Whisper model from **Settings › Voice** and ffmpeg.

### ffmpeg

Video editing uses [ffmpeg](https://ffmpeg.org). Row-Bot doesn't include it: it uses the ffmpeg already on this computer (on `PATH`) when there is one. Otherwise, the first time it's needed, Row-Bot asks "Video editing needs ffmpeg (about 30 MB) from PyPI. Download it now?" as a network download: **Ask** asks, **Auto**'s reviewer may approve it when you asked for an edit, **Hands-off** allows it, and **Block** refuses.

- It downloads the `imageio-ffmpeg` 0.6.0 package for this computer from PyPI (`files.pythonhosted.org`) by its exact address, checks it against fingerprints saved in Row-Bot, and keeps only its ffmpeg program in Row-Bot's data folder. Nothing is installed with pip, and Row-Bot's own files aren't changed.
- **Licence**: these ffmpeg programs are free software under the GNU GPL (version 3 or later on Windows and Linux, version 2 or later on Macs with Apple silicon). Row-Bot runs ffmpeg as a separate program; the source is at [ffmpeg.org](https://ffmpeg.org/download.html).
- **Intel Macs and Windows on Arm**: Row-Bot can't download ffmpeg for these. Install it yourself (for example `brew install ffmpeg` on a Mac, or `winget install Gyan.FFmpeg` on Windows), then restart Row-Bot.
- Recording the screen on Windows uses the same ffmpeg (see [Computer Use](/docs/computer-use)).

## Looking At Images

Row-Bot can look at up to 8 pictures in one go: files in the conversation, pictures in the workspace, the page in its browser, and frames from recordings and videos. For more, or to keep it quick, it tiles them into one **contact sheet**: a numbered, captioned picture, kept with the reply's working files, so you can see what it looked at. Frames from a video need ffmpeg (see above).

If the conversation's model can't see images, Row-Bot says so and gathers nothing; choose a model that can for **Vision** in **Settings › Models**, or switch the conversation to one. Looking at your screen or through your camera still asks first every time, on its own.

## Sending Files

Finished work already shows in the conversation, on every device signed in to Row-Bot. Ask Row-Bot to send you a file when you want it in front of you, for example "send the report to my phone" or "send it to me on Telegram". It sends files you already have: files in the conversation, its recordings and video edits, and files in the workspace folder. It never sends anything from elsewhere on the computer or from Row-Bot's own data folder. Up to 50 files go in one reply.

- **To your devices.** The files show in the conversation as a card, **Sent to your devices**, on every phone or computer signed in to Row-Bot (see [Phone And Native Desktop](/docs/mobile-native)). Each file is the conversation's own: a picture, video or sound plays in the card, and it stays for as long as the conversation keeps it. Each open Row-Bot window also shows **Row-Bot sent you report.pdf** with **Open**. A file too large for a conversation (over 200 MB, up to 500 MB) goes as a download instead, with **Download**: it needs that device's sign-in, and it ends after 7 days, when Row-Bot removes its copy. Sending to your own devices never asks, at any approval level. Sending a file doesn't send a phone notification: a device with Row-Bot closed finds the file in the conversation the next time it opens it. The desktop app saves a download into the workspace's **Exports** folder, with **Show in folder**.
- **To a chat app.** Telegram, Discord, Slack or WhatsApp, once it's set up in [Channels](/docs/integrations/channels). The files go to your own chat there, or, when the conversation came from that app, to that same chat; Row-Bot can't send them to any other chat. A file leaving Row-Bot asks like sending a message: **Ask** asks, **Auto**'s reviewer approves it only when you clearly asked for it, **Hands-off** allows it, and **Block** refuses. A conversation other people share (a Slack or Discord channel thread, a group chat) never sends on Hands-off. Each app has a size limit: Telegram 50 MB, Discord 10 MB, WhatsApp 16 MB and Slack 100 MB through Row-Bot.
- **When a file can't go**, the card says why in plain words (too big for the app, the app isn't connected, or it can't take files) and offers **Send to your devices instead**. SMS can't send files.

## Interactive Terminal

In the Row-Bot desktop app, a conversation can open a real interactive terminal docked at the bottom of the window. Open or close it with the terminal button in the header, **Open panel › Interactive terminal**, the command palette (**Toggle terminal**), or Ctrl+`.

- Type straight into it: colours, line editing, command history (the arrow keys) and Tab completion work as in your own terminal, and interactive programs answer.
- **Stop** (Ctrl+C) interrupts the running command, **Clear** clears the screen, **Open in your terminal** opens your own terminal app, and **Close** hides the dock. Closing and reopening keeps the session and its scrollback.
- Drag the divider to resize it; the height is remembered on this device. In a phone-sized window it opens as a full-screen sheet instead.
- After the shell exits, **Start again** opens a new one.

The terminal is for you: what you type runs as your own commands on this computer. Commands Row-Bot runs as tools still follow workspace boundaries, tool availability and approval mode, and appear in the conversation's tool steps. The terminal needs the Row-Bot desktop app: in a browser on this computer the dock says so, and other devices don't offer it.

## Common Workflow

1. Ask for a task that may need tools.
2. Let Row-Bot explain the intended action.
3. Review the approval card, wherever you see it.
4. Approve only if the action matches your intent.
5. Open the tool step to check the result.
6. Ask Row-Bot to summarize what changed.

## Troubleshooting

- If no approval appears, the action may be read-only, allowed by the conversation's **Auto** mode, or blocked before running.
- If a tool result is confusing, ask Row-Bot to explain the last tool call.
- If the terminal says it needs the Row-Bot desktop app, open the conversation there; the button is not offered on other devices.
- If you denied by mistake, ask Row-Bot to try again and review the next approval.
- If a background process won't start because too many are running, stop one in **Home › Monitor › Background processes**.
- If a local app shows "Nothing answered at localhost:5173", start its server first; if Row-Bot started it, check its card in the conversation.
- If Row-Bot asks again for a local address you allowed, its hour ran out or it was removed; allow it again.
- If video editing says ffmpeg couldn't be downloaded, check the internet connection and ask again, or install ffmpeg yourself and restart Row-Bot.
- If a file Row-Bot sent says **This download has ended**, it was too large for the conversation, so it went as a download, and its 7 days ran out; ask Row-Bot to send it again.

## Ask Row-Bot About Row-Bot

Route: /docs/chat/about-row-bot

Ask Row-Bot how to do something in Row-Bot, what it is running now, or what's wrong: it answers from its own guides, offline, shows each setting, changes some for you with your approval, and can undo them.

# Ask Row-Bot About Row-Bot

Row-Bot can answer questions about itself in the chat: how to do something, where a setting is, what it is running now, and what needs your attention. It answers from its own guides, which come with every install, so it works offline and matches the version you have.

## How Do I…?

Ask in your own words, such as "how do I turn off install stats?" or "where do I change the Dream Cycle hours?". Row-Bot searches its guides and answers in steps:

- Each setting it names is a chip, such as **Preferences › Dream Cycle**. Select it to open that row in Settings, highlighted, just as **Find a setting** does.
- The guide it used is a chip too. Select it to read that guide in a sheet beside the chat (from the bottom on a phone), opened at the section it cited. **Open on row-bot.ai** opens the same page on the web.
- If the guides don't cover something, Row-Bot says so instead of guessing.

## Settings Row-Bot Can Change

For some settings Row-Bot offers to make the change for you. It checks the value first, then asks on a card that shows what the setting is now and what it becomes, with **Show in Settings** to see the row. The chat's approval level decides who approves, as for any action:

- **Ask**: you choose **Change** (or **Turn on**), or **Not now**.
- **Auto**: the reviewer approves a change you clearly asked for and asks you about anything else. Turning on **Shell**, file tools, **Browser**, **Computer use** or **MCP** apps always asks you.
- **Hands-off**: it makes the change and records it.
- **Block**: it changes nothing.

Row-Bot can change your models (main, vision, image and video), the reading limit, its name and personality, **Learn new skills**, the Dream Cycle and its hours, **Live captions**, **Log detail**, which skills are available or pinned, and which tools are on.

After a change, its card in the chat offers **Undo**. Undo puts the old value back at once, with nothing to approve. If the setting has changed again since, Undo leaves it alone and says so. You can also ask Row-Bot to change it back.

Some settings stay yours alone. Row-Bot shows where they are but never changes them: approval levels, keys and sign-ins, devices and remote access, install stats, Learning, access to Row-Bot's data folder, updates, the workspace folder, appearance, anything that downloads or installs, and anything that deletes.

## What's Wrong?

Ask "what's wrong?" or "why didn't that work?". Row-Bot reads the same checks as [Monitor](/docs/monitor/) and Overview's **Needs you**, most urgent first, each with its one fix:

- It checks again when you ask. That contacts your providers and accounts, as Monitor's **Run diagnosis** does.
- Fixes only you can do, such as signing in again or restarting a channel, come back as a link to the exact place.
- Row-Bot never asks for a key and never signs in for you.

## Status

Type **/status** in the composer for a short summary: the version and any update, the model and whether it can use tools, this chat's approval level, and what needs you, each with its fix.

## In Chat Apps

In Telegram, Slack and other chat apps, Row-Bot writes settings as words, such as "Dream Cycle (Settings › Preferences)", and guides as their page on row-bot.ai.

## Progressive Tools And Skills

Route: /docs/guides/progressive-tools-and-skills

Understand how Row-Bot discovers external tools and task-specific skills without loading every capability into every prompt.

# Progressive Tools And Skills

Row-Bot can keep a large extension library enabled without sending every external tool schema and every skill instruction to the model on each turn. By default, it progressively discovers the capabilities that match the current request.

## How Tool Discovery Works

The Row-Bot tools it uses without being asked stay available on every turn: files, the shell and background programs, web search and reading pages, memory, tasks and waits, pages, questions, helpers, vision, the calculator, documents, conversation search, the browser's everyday steps, setting up a design or code folder, and Row-Bot's own status and guides.

Row-Bot's less-used tools are one search away instead of being sent with every message: sound and music, media, weather, Wikipedia, linked conversations, charts, trackers, the wiki, goals, YouTube, arXiv, updates, the browser's recording, sandboxes and less common steps, and a few rarer actions such as running a task now or linking memories. Nothing is switched off: when a request needs one, Row-Bot finds it and uses it with exactly the same approvals, and an Agent Profile with its own tool list keeps every tool it names. This keeps each message to the model small, so a model on this computer starts answering sooner.

Enabled external tools from MCP servers, plugins, Custom Tools, and channels are kept in a searchable catalog.

In **Only the ones a request needs** mode, Row-Bot:

1. Searches the enabled external-tool catalog when the request needs an integration.
2. Selects the matching tool without changing its underlying identity or provider contract.
3. Applies the same profile filtering, workspace policy, execution budget, prompt-injection handling, and approval rules as a directly bound tool.
4. Shows the real integration name in live and reopened tool traces rather than a generic invocation wrapper.

Discovery does not enable disabled integrations, add credentials, or bypass an approval. If two capabilities conflict with a core tool name, Row-Bot keeps the core boundary intact.

## How Skill Discovery Works

Skills are instruction packages, not executable permissions. Enabled skills can be searched when a request clearly matches their purpose. Row-Bot may then load the relevant skill for that task and show a **Using _skill_** receipt plus an active skill chip.

Automatically loaded skills are scoped to the current task. Reopening the task restores its active skills, while a different parent task or child Agent keeps independent activation state. Up to five automatically selected skills are retained per task; pinned skills are managed separately. Loading an already active skill is a no-op and should not create a duplicate receipt.

## Parent And Child Boundaries

Each child Agent receives its own profile, tool allow-list, approval mode, workspace policy, execution budget, and skill activation state. A child can use the skill discovery bridges when its runtime permits them, but loading a skill cannot grant a tool that its profile denies. Child skill choices also do not leak into the parent or a sibling child.

Use **Row-Bot Status** inside a child run when you need to distinguish globally configured tools from the tool groups actually bound to that child.

## Auto And Compatibility Modes

Open **Settings → Tools → How tools are offered**:

- **Only the ones a request needs (recommended)** keeps the prompt compact and discovers enabled external integrations as needed.
- **All of them, every time** is the eager compatibility mode. It sends every enabled external tool schema that survives the same provider and policy filters, which can use substantially more model context.

Changing this setting does not alter tool enablement, credentials, approvals, or saved Agent Profiles.

## What You See In Chat

- Skill discovery can show `skill_search`, followed by one **Using _skill_** notice after a successful load.
- External discovery can show a search step followed by a result grouped under the real integration name.
- Reopened transcripts preserve the real external-tool label.
- Direct tools in eager mode keep their existing labels and approval behavior.

## Troubleshooting

- If no matching tool is found, confirm the integration is installed, enabled, healthy, and allowed by the active profile.
- If a skill is not selected, confirm it is enabled and make the requested task specific enough to match its purpose.
- If a child can see a tool in global status but cannot call it, inspect the child's profile-selected tool groups. Global availability is not the same as runtime access.
- If a provider rejects a tool schema, try a compatible tool-capable model; discovery does not weaken provider schema validation.
- Use eager mode temporarily when diagnosing an older provider or integration that expects direct external-tool binding.

See [Tools Settings](/docs/settings/tools), [Skills Settings](/docs/settings/skills), [Skills](/docs/skills/), and [Extensions And Trust Boundaries](/docs/concepts/extensions-and-trust) for related controls and safety boundaries.

## Profiles, Goals, And Agents

Route: /docs/profiles-goals-agents/

Manage agent profiles in the sidebar's Agents dialog, give a conversation a goal that keeps going until done, and follow the agents it delegates to.

# Profiles, Goals, And Agents

These three features work together but solve different problems. An **agent profile** is a reusable role and policy. A **goal** is an objective a conversation keeps working toward, turn after turn. An **agent run** is one piece of delegated work, with its own conversation, status and result.

For the mental model behind delegation and hand-offs, read [How Profiles, Goals, And Agents Work](/docs/concepts/profiles-goals-and-agents).

## Agent Profiles

Open the **Agents** dialog with **All agents** in the sidebar's **Agents** section, **All agents…** under **New chat**'s **▾**, the Agents icon on the collapsed rail, or **Agents** in the command palette. It lists every profile in groups (Everyday, Creative, Developer, your own profiles, and profiles from workspaces, plugins or imports), with **Search profiles** and a scope filter.

Each profile row can:

- **Pin to the sidebar**: pinned profiles become favourites in the sidebar's **Agents** section and under **New chat**'s **▾**, one click from a new chat;
- **Start chat** with that profile;
- **View**, **Duplicate**, and, for your own profiles, **Edit**, turn on or off, or **Delete**.

**Create profile** describes a new role: its name, description and when to use it, instructions, capability (read only, write capable, or orchestrator), skills, context mode, workspace mode and approval mode. A profile lists no tools: every agent has the tools a chat has, and its capability and the approval level decide what it may do. **Read only** lets it look, never change or send. Keep the role narrow: describe the outcome, the sources it may use, and what it must not do.

To use a profile in an existing conversation, choose it from the composer's **+ › Agent**, which lists each agent with a line on what it does. Profiles do not grant capabilities by themselves. A tool must still be enabled, available, and allowed by the conversation's approvals.

## Goals

A goal is useful when work needs more than one turn. Set it from the conversation's details card: choose **Set a goal**, describe **What should this conversation achieve?**, and choose **Start goal**. Row-Bot starts at once and keeps going turn after turn; it stops for approvals and when it needs you.

- **No turn limit by default.** Overnight and multi-day goals keep going while they make progress. Set an optional **Turn limit** or **Time limit (hours)** when you want one. A default turn limit for new goals is in Settings › Models › Limits for long work.
- **Smart stop.** Row-Bot pauses the goal and says why when it stops making progress (no progress in the last 2 turns) or the same step fails 3 times. When a provider's usage limit stops a turn, the goal waits and continues by itself once the limit resets, if the provider says when.
- **Checked every turn.** After each turn Row-Bot checks the goal's progress. If it can't check it 2 times in a row, for example because the model it uses is unavailable, the goal pauses instead of going on unchecked, and you get a notification. **Resume** tries again.
- **Pauses when Row-Bot closes.** Goals that were working come back paused the next time you open Row-Bot, with one notice, such as "2 goals paused when Row-Bot closed". Choose **Resume** on a goal, in its conversation, to continue from its last saved turn. A goal waiting for your approval keeps waiting. A restart Row-Bot makes itself (installing an update) lets them continue by themselves.
- **Visible usage.** The card shows the goal's state (Working, Continuing, Waiting for your approval, Paused, Needs you, Done or Stopped), the turn it is on ("Turn 7", or "Turn 7 of 30" with a limit), how long it has been running and the tokens it has used.
- **Pause**, **Resume** and **Stop** control it. Stopping ends the goal; it does not delete the conversation or its evidence. Starting a new goal replaces the current one, and **Earlier goals** lists the ones before.

### Done means and checks

Open **Done means and check** in the goal form to say what "done" means in your own words, and to name a command that must pass before Row-Bot calls the goal done, such as `npm test`, `python -m pytest` or `gh pr checks 590`. In a conversation with a code folder, the project's own commands are offered to pick from. You can also type it: `/goal Ship the docs check: npm run build`.

- **Only you set the check.** Row-Bot can suggest one in words, but its goal tool has no way to set or change it.
- **You approve it once.** Before the goal starts, Row-Bot shows where the check runs: the conversation's code folder (in its Docker sandbox when it uses one) or Row-Bot's workspace folder, the one chosen in Settings that the file tools and the shell use, named by its path. Starting the goal approves that command, in that folder, for that goal, at every approval level. If the workspace folder changes later, the check doesn't run until you set it again. A command that can't run here, or that reads Row-Bot's own data folder, is refused. A chat on **Block** allows only checks that just read, such as `git status`.
- **It runs when the goal looks done.** When Row-Bot says the goal is done, the turn ends and the check runs, for at most 10 minutes. Each run checks the chat's approval level and the command again: if the chat moved to Block, or the command now counts as a different kind of command, it doesn't run and the goal pauses.
- **Exit 0 means done.** The card says **Verified by `npm test`** with the time. Any other exit code gives Row-Bot a turn to fix what the command reported, with its output in front of it; that turn counts like any other goal turn. After 3 failed checks in a row the goal pauses and says why. A check that times out or can't start pauses the goal too.
- **See the output.** The info button on the check line shows the last 2,000 characters the check printed, with Copy.

## Delegated Agents

A conversation can delegate parts of its work to agents, which Row-Bot also calls **helpers**. Row-Bot hands work to helpers by itself when a request has several separate parts, such as researching three products, and works on the rest while they run. Each agent works in its own conversation, reached from the conversation that started it: the sidebar, the conversation library and a new chat's **Recent** list show only your own chats. Search still finds an agent's conversation.

- **In the transcript**, the turn that started agents shows a small stub for each one, with its icon, name and live status (working, waiting for you, done, failed or stopped). A failed agent's stub says why. Click a stub to open that agent's conversation.
- **In the details card**, **Agents** lists them, live and failed ones first. **Message** sends an agent a note it reads at its next step; **Stop** ends its run.
- **In an agent's own conversation**, the header leads back to the parent conversation.
- **When an agent needs approval**, the request appears in the parent conversation and everywhere else approvals show. See [Tools, Approvals And Background Work](/docs/chat/tools-approvals-and-terminal#approvals).
- **If work was interrupted** before it finished, for example by a restart, the card and Overview's **Needs you** offer **Resume agent work** or **Dismiss agent work**.
- **Model and reasoning**: a helper uses the chat's model and reasoning unless you ask otherwise, for example "use a helper on Sonnet at low effort". Its stub and header show which. A helper keeps the chat's apps, and a read-only helper can only read with them. Helper conversations stay out of the Library.
- **Start one yourself** with `/agent [--worktree] [--model=…] [--reasoning=level] [profile] <task>`, for example `/agent --reasoning low summarise the thread`. Without a profile it uses the general **worker**.

A completed agent's result is evidence for the parent, not automatic permission to write files, send messages, commit code, or publish.

For coding work, a parent can assign an agent to an existing local folder. Row-Bot registers that folder as the agent's code folder and applies writer ownership to the resolved folder, not merely the process working directory. Agents assigned to distinct folders or worktrees can write in parallel; writers targeting the same folder wait and run serially.

New runs also receive a checkpointed work budget with no step limit to set: a run goes on while it makes progress. Settings › Models › **Limits for long work** shows helper levels, helpers at a time, and the optional helper time limit. Extra agents wait in a first-in, first-out queue when capacity is full; changing a setting affects new runs, not work already in progress.

If a run appears stuck, open its conversation to read its last update before stopping it. If several agents edit the same resource, give them distinct folders or worktrees, narrow their ownership, or run them sequentially. Keep consequential final actions with the parent and a human approval point.

Row-Bot saves the parent's first continuation checkpoint when asynchronous delegation begins. If a child process outlives its launching shell or the app restarts, resume repairs only genuinely unanswered tool calls with an interruption marker, then wakes the parent from durable child results. It does not replay previously executed work. If a checkpoint cannot be repaired safely, the run remains stopped for review.

Repeated model-and-tool states are detected before a run can loop indefinitely. The fourth identical no-progress state is blocked; a fifth ends the run cleanly with a durable reason. After a very long run of steps (a safety ceiling of 1,000) a turn stops and asks **Keep going?**; send **Continue** to pick up from there.

## What Is Saved

Profiles, goals, agent runs, edges, progress, results, and evidence are stored in the active local data directory. Favourite profiles are remembered on each device. Provider prompts still follow the privacy terms of the model route selected for each run.

## Workflows

Route: /docs/guides/workflows

Create, run, schedule, edit, deliver, and troubleshoot Row-Bot workflows.

# Workflows

Workflows are repeatable Row-Bot tasks. Use them for things you want to run again: a morning brief, inbox follow-up, document digest, research check, report draft, or channel delivery. A **reminder** is a simpler kind that just tells you something at a chosen time.

A workflow is a chat that runs on its own: each run sends your message to the workflow's own conversation, in the background, and Row-Bot works on it exactly as it would in a chat. It has every tool a chat has, finds apps and tools the same way, and asks before actions at the same approval level, on the same cards.

For the execution model behind schedules, persistent runs, approvals, and delivery, read [How Background Workflows Run](/docs/concepts/background-workflows).

## Where To Find Workflows

Choose **Home**, then the **Workflows** tab. Overview's **New workflow** quick start and the ⌘K command palette (**Run …**) also reach them.

## The Workflow List

- Each row shows the workflow's name, when it runs next, its last runs, and small tags for its profile and approvals. **Hands-off** stands out.
- **Run** starts the workflow at once, in one click. The row then shows its live state and **Stop**.
- **Enable** or **Disable** turns the workflow's schedule on or off.
- **Edit** opens the workflow editor.
- The row's **⋯** menu opens **Run history**, **Workflow settings** or the workflow's conversation (**Open conversation**), and can duplicate or delete the workflow.
- **Search workflows**, the filter and **Select workflows** help with long lists.
- **Delivery defaults** choose the external channels every workflow also sends results to, unless a workflow chooses its own. The app always shows the result.

## Create A Workflow

1. Choose **New workflow**. The editor opens on the page, as editing does.
2. Give it a name, an icon and a short description, and choose **Workflow** or **Reminder**.
3. Write the **Messages**: what you would type in a chat. One message is enough for most workflows; **Add message** sends another after the first is done, in the same conversation, so it can build on the answer. Say what to do when there is nothing to do. Type `{{` to add the date. Drag messages, or use the arrow keys, to reorder them.
   - Keep a message short and positive: what to make, for whom, in what voice, and where the results go. For example: "Each weekday, write one post for @rowbot_ai about something Row-Bot does well, for people who run AI on their own computer. Friendly and concrete. Post it."
   - Leave out the rules Row-Bot already keeps: the approval card for each post or email, the account it names, the length limit, and never sending the same thing twice.
4. Choose **When it runs**: manually, at a date and time, or repeating. Repeating can be every day, weekdays, chosen days, **Monthly**, every few hours or minutes, or a custom cron expression. **Timezone** starts at the timezone of the device you're using, and you can search for another. A daily time stays the same across daylight saving.
5. Choose **Send results to**: follow your defaults, choose channels only for this workflow, or keep results in the app.
6. Under **Change model and approvals**, pick an **Agent profile** and **Approvals**:
   - **Ask before actions**;
   - **Auto, reviewed**: a reviewer approves what matches the workflow's own messages;
   - **Hands-off**: nothing pauses;
   - **Block actions**.
7. Save, then **Run** it once and review the result.

## Its Conversation

- Every run of a workflow is a new turn in the same conversation, marked with when and how it started, such as **Scheduled run · 26 Oct, 08:00**. Open it with **Open conversation** to read what each run did, see its approval cards, or carry on in it yourself.
- A run's outcome comes from what its tools did, never from the model's own words: **Posted**, with the post's link, for example, or **Not sure it went through** when a tool couldn't confirm it. A run you said no to ends **You said no to …**, naming what you refused, and its notes keep a dated line so the next run knows and doesn't try it another way.
- A run that fails on a passing problem, such as the network or a busy provider, tries again by itself after a wait. Once something has gone out, it never tries again: nothing is posted or sent twice.
- A workflow that runs by itself (on a schedule, a webhook or after another workflow) and fails 5 runs in a row is switched off, so it doesn't keep spending model time on a run that can't succeed. One notice says so, its row shows **Off: failed 5 times in a row**, and its last delivery says it too. Open it to see why, then **Turn it back on**; its count starts again. **Run** still works while it is off.
- A workflow keeps short notes between runs: what it checked and when, ids it needs again, what's left. Each run reads them first and updates them before it ends, so it doesn't check again what an earlier run already did. Updating them shows as a step in the run.
- A run has the tools and skills a chat has, including skills you made in other chats.
- Workflows hand work on by sending it, by the other workflow's name: a trends workflow ends by sending its brief to the publisher workflow's conversation, which starts a turn there. An update that needs no answer is sent without asking for a reply, and a note can wait for the other workflow's next run instead of starting a turn now.
- A post made for a time slot waits in **Home › Review**, where you edit it, approve it or say no; approved, it goes out at its time.
- A run can wait for something and carry on when it happens: a build or check to pass, a page to change, a time, or another workflow to finish. Nothing runs while it waits. **Home › Waiting** and the conversation show what it waits for, with **Stop**. Pictures, clips and voice lines pass through **Library › Media**, where a workflow finds, tags and copies them. For real screenshots and clips, a workflow uses a [sandbox](/docs/operations/#sandboxes), never your own Row-Bot.
- A run has no step limit to set. It keeps going while it makes progress, and stops when you press **Stop** or when it keeps repeating the same thing. After a very long run of steps it stops and asks **Keep going?**: send **Continue** in its conversation to pick up from there.

## Watch Something From A Chat

For a quick check you don't need a workflow: a **watch** keeps an eye on something from the chat you're in and speaks up there only when it changes.

- Type `/watch` (or `/loop`) and what to watch. `/watch 10m https://status.example.com` watches a page and ``/watch 5m `gh pr checks 590` `` a command, set at once with no model call. Leave out the interval and it paces itself: every 5 minutes, slower while nothing changes, up to an hour.
- Anything else, such as `/watch is the PR ready to merge? every 30m`, goes to Row-Bot, which sets the watch. A question that needs judgement is checked by the chat's own model, at most every 15 minutes, with read-only tools only. A check that finds nothing new never shows in the chat.
- A command that only reads is set as it is. Any other command asks first, by the chat's approval level, once, when the watch is set; each check checks it again, and on **Block** only commands that just read run. Pages must be public.
- The watch's card, above the message box and in Conversation details, shows its last check, its changes and what its checks used, with **Check now**, **Pause**, **Watch 24 hours longer** and **Stop**.
- A watch lasts 24 hours, and up to 7 days. It stops after 20 changes, and Row-Bot keeps at most 10 watches across your chats. When one ends, or can't be extended any more, **Make this a workflow** on its card opens a new workflow filled in from it, to review and save; saving stops the watch. Choose a workflow for checks that should run for longer, on their own.

## Workflow Settings

- **Workflow settings** chooses the model and the trigger: manual and scheduled runs only, **When another workflow completes**, or **Webhook (HTTP POST)**. A webhook trigger creates a private secret when you save; download its configuration and keep it private.
- **If Row-Bot is closed at a scheduled time**, in Workflow settings:
  - **Skip it** (the default);
  - **Run once when Row-Bot starts**: only the latest missed time runs, and the run says it ran late.
- **Send results**, in Workflow settings, chooses when results reach the workflow's channels. Each one starts with what happened: **Sent** and what went out, **Finished · nothing was posted or sent**, **Not sure it went through**, or **Didn't finish**.
  - **After every run** (the default);
  - **Only when it needs me**: a run that didn't finish, or isn't sure something went through. Approvals still reach you;
  - **In a daily digest**: one message from 6 PM, with a line for each run that day.
- **Code folder**, in Workflow settings, gives the workflow a [code folder](/docs/developer/) of its own: its conversation works in it. **None: the conversation's folder** keeps today's behaviour. If the folder is removed, the next run stops, says why, and opens the settings at **Code folder** so you can choose another.
- **Always ask me**, in Workflow settings, makes actions in the apps you tick wait for your own approval on every run, even on Auto or Hands-off, for up to 16 apps. The card shows exactly what will happen.

## Workflows With Apps

- **Start from a template**, below the workflow list, offers workflows that use apps: **GitHub pull-request digest**, **Linear triage** and **Notion weekly summary**. Each is created switched off, with a schedule and **Ask before actions** approvals; turn it on when it suits you. A template whose app isn't connected shows **Connect** instead. Templates never add a webhook or change how Row-Bot can be reached.
- A workflow uses apps as a chat does. Mention an app in a message, such as `@notion`, to keep that message to it; otherwise Row-Bot finds what it needs. **Delivery** lists only the channels you have set up.
- On **Auto**, a reviewer approves what matches the workflow's own messages; anything else, including an app action its access asks about that the reviewer isn't sure of, pauses the run and waits for you. On **Hands-off**, which you turn on in the workflow's settings, nothing pauses for approval.

## Approvals In Workflows

An action that needs approval pauses the run on the same card a chat shows, with everything it will do: a post's full text and account, or an email's recipients and body. It waits until you answer. Answer it in the workflow's conversation, or from the sidebar's attention indicator or Overview's **Needs you**, whose **Review** opens the card. A run still waiting when the next one starts is replaced: its card is withdrawn, so a day-old post can't go out, and the run ends **Expired**, saying a newer run replaced it.

## What Is Saved

Workflow definitions, schedules, run history, delivery defaults, and status are local Row-Bot data. Results may be sent to channels only when configured and selected.

## Safety

Avoid workflows that send messages, write files, start servers, or call external systems without a review point. Use approvals for actions that can affect files, accounts, channels, MCP servers, plugins, or external services. Remember that **Run** starts at once, including any delivery outside the app.

## Troubleshooting

- If a workflow does not run on schedule, check that it is enabled. A run that starts while the one before is still working is skipped and says so. A run missed while Row-Bot was closed is skipped unless the workflow's settings say **Run once when Row-Bot starts**.
- If a run stopped with "Choose a folder", its code folder was removed: choose another in its settings, or **None**.
- If delivery fails, check the selected channel and its Settings page.
- If a run waits for approval, answer it from the attention indicator or Overview.
- If a run stopped and asked **Keep going?**, send **Continue** in its conversation.
- If results are too broad, make the message narrower, or add a second message that works on the first answer.

## Designs

Route: /docs/designer/

Create decks, documents, landing pages, app mockups and storyboards with Row-Bot, and edit, present, share and export them in a conversation's Design panel.

# Designs

Row-Bot can make visual work with you: decks, documents, landing pages, app mockups and storyboards, with your brand's colours, fonts and logo, charts, and generated images or video. Each design belongs to a conversation and opens in that conversation's **Design panel**, beside the chat, so you can ask for changes and see them land.

## Start A Design

- **Ask in a chat:** "Make a five-slide deck about our spring workshop." Row-Bot creates the design, and the finished design opens in the panel by itself when you are not typing.
- **Home › Overview › New design** sets one up and opens it in a new chat.
- **In a conversation**, open the composer's **+** menu, choose **Add resource…**, then **Design**. Choose **Create new** (the type, an optional name and brief, a template and canvas, and **Draft it now**) or **Open saved** to bring an existing design into this conversation.

The conversation's details card lists it under **Working on**; choose it there, or from the header's **Open panel** menu, to reopen the panel.

## The Design Panel

- **Preview** and **Edit** switch between looking and changing. In Edit, click anything on the page to change it, or ask Row-Bot about it; double-click text to edit it in place. Changes save as you go.
- **Undo** and **Redo** step through your changes; **Versions** lists saved versions and restores one.
- The **page strip** moves between pages, adds a page after the current one, or deletes one.
- **Size** chooses the canvas (16:9 widescreen, 4:3, square, A4 document, 9:16 phone, or a custom size). **Device width** previews pages at desktop, tablet or phone width, and the zoom control fits or scales the page.
- **Present** shows the design full screen.
- **Share** publishes a link (with a QR code), sends to a channel, or prepares an X post.
- **Export** saves the current saved version as **PDF**, **PNG**, **PowerPoint** (pictures for high fidelity, or editable text and shapes) or **HTML**, for all pages, the current page or a page range.
- The **⋯** menu opens the design command palette to search tools, pages and assets, imports a document, or duplicates the design.

## The Inspector

**Inspector** opens three tabs:

- **Selection** edits the chosen element: its text, font, size, weight, colour and alignment; an image's file, fit, crop, corners and description; width and borders; and what happens when it is clicked (go to a screen, toggle a state, play media). **Edit as CSS…** is there for exact control.
- **Brand** sets the design's **Colours** (primary, secondary, accent, background and text), **Fonts** for headings and body from a font picker (recently used, bundled, and fonts on this computer), and the **Logo**: upload one, then choose its placement, size, spacing, which pages show it, and automatic or manual placement. Save the brand as a preset to reuse it in other designs.
- **Library** inserts **Blocks**, **Your images**, saved **Styles** and **Interactions**.

**Review** checks the design and lists what to fix.

## Brand And Media Providers

Generated images or videos call the image and video models chosen in **Settings › Models**. Local design edits stay in local project data.

For xAI API image models, Row-Bot uses the provider's live image-generation catalog instead of guessing from the chat catalog. It exposes only the formats, aspect ratios, resolutions, and quality choices reported for that model. If xAI rejects an optional quality field, Row-Bot retries once without it; timeouts and other failures do not trigger an automatic second generation that could duplicate cost.

## What Is Saved

Designs, their versions and brand presets are local Row-Bot data. Deleting the conversation keeps the design; open it from another conversation with **Add resource… › Open saved**.

To delete a design itself, open it and choose **More design actions › Delete design…**. Its pages, saved versions and files are deleted, and it leaves every conversation that used it; those conversations keep their messages. It can't be deleted while a conversation using it is working. **Undo** on a **Created design** card in the chat deletes the design too, so it asks first (**Delete design?**).

## Troubleshooting

- If a first draft is thin, give a clearer goal, audience and length, and attach references.
- If an export looks wrong, preview each page first; exports use the last saved version.
- If an export says **Export unavailable** ("Exports need Browser Automation"), PDF, PNG and PowerPoint exports need Row-Bot's browser: open **Settings › System › Browser and computer use**, choose **Set up…**, and **Install** the **Browser runtime**, then export again. You do this once: it is kept in your data folder, so updates keep it.
- If a preview says a font "isn't available offline", it shows a bundled substitute; the design keeps its font, but offline exports embed only fonts bundled with Row-Bot, so choose one of those for a design you will export.
- If image generation is unavailable, choose an image model in Settings › Models and check its provider.
- If a change says the design changed meanwhile, let the panel reload the current version and try again.

## Code Folders

Route: /docs/developer/

Work on a folder or repository from a conversation: bind or clone it, review changes, run checks and use Git in the Developer panel.

# Code Folders

A code folder is a folder or Git repository on this computer that a conversation works on. Bind one to a conversation and Row-Bot can read its files, propose and make edits, run checks and commands you approve, and help with Git. The folder opens in the conversation's **Developer panel**, beside the chat.

## Bring A Folder Into A Conversation

**Ask in the chat.** Row-Bot binds folders by itself when you ask:

- "Use my Hello-World folder" binds a code folder you already use, by its name. If several names match, a **Which code folder?** card lets you choose; if none does, a **Use an existing folder** card asks you to choose the folder on this computer.
- "Clone https://github.com/octocat/Hello-World" shows a **Clone a repository** card with the address. Choose **Choose where** to pick the parent folder, and Row-Bot clones it there. An interrupted clone is kept for inspection and offers **Check clone status**; it is never cloned again automatically.

Either way, the conversation shows a **Using code folder …** card with **Open** and **Undo**. The turn pauses while a card waits for you and continues in the folder once it is bound. Row-Bot never chooses a path on its own: you choose every folder, in the picker or in Row-Bot's workspace folder (below).

**Or set it up yourself.** Open the composer's **+** menu, choose **Add resource…**, then **Code folder**:

| Folder setup | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| **New draft in the configured workspace** | Creates an empty folder under Drafts in your workspace folder. |
| **Register an existing folder** | Saves an existing folder's name and location; its files and Git state are unchanged. |
| **Create a new empty folder** | Creates one empty folder under a parent you choose. |
| **Clone a repository** | Downloads a repository into a new folder under a parent you choose. |

**Open saved** brings a code folder you used before into this conversation. Home › Overview's **New code folder** does the same in a new chat.

### From A Browser, Phone Or Another Computer

The desktop app chooses folders with this computer's own folder picker. A browser, a phone or another computer signed in to Row-Bot has no picker for this computer, so the same steps (Add resource, and the **Use an existing folder** and **Clone a repository** cards in the chat) show **Row-Bot's workspace folder** instead (Settings › System › Workspace folder), one folder at a time: tap a folder to open it, use the path above the list to go back, and choose **Use …** for the folder shown. Only folders inside the workspace folder are listed, so put a project there (or clone it there) to work on it from another device.

- There is no path to type. Row-Bot checks every folder it lists and every choice on the computer it runs on: anything outside the workspace folder, a link or Windows junction that leads out of it, or a hidden or Git-internal folder is refused.
- **Clone from URL** clones a repository into the folder shown, with this computer's own Git sign-in.
- Choosing a folder registers it exactly as the picker does: its files and Git history stay as they are.

### Cloning Asks First

A clone downloads from the internet, so it follows the conversation's **Approvals**: under **Ask** (and in a new conversation) Row-Bot shows where it downloads from and to, and clones when you confirm; **Auto** and **Hands-off** clone when you choose it; **Block** refuses.

The conversation's details card lists the folder under **Working on**. Its **⋯** menu, or **Undo** on the card, unbinds it from the conversation; the files stay on disk.

The Agents tool can also assign a child directly to an existing local folder. Row-Bot validates the path and registers it as that child's code folder; a folder assignment and a pre-existing workspace ID are alternative ways to select the workspace, not settings to combine.

## Project Notes

Many repositories keep instructions for coding agents: how to build, test and style the code. When a conversation works in a code folder, Row-Bot reads them from the folder's top level: `AGENTS.md`, `CLAUDE.md`, `.cursorrules` and `.github/copilot-instructions.md`.

- Together they are kept to 8,000 characters (2,000 on a small local model). A longer file is cut, and Row-Bot is told where to read the rest.
- Row-Bot treats them as the folder authors' notes, not your instructions. They can't change approvals, grant permissions, or ask it to send or reveal anything, and your own messages come first.
- A file is left out when it seems to give the agent new instructions, looks like it holds a password or key, links outside the folder, is over 64 KB, or isn't plain text.
- Under **Working on**, the folder shows **Project notes** with the files in use. The **ⓘ** button lists each file, whether it is used and why one was left out, and opens it in **Files**.

Nothing is read from folders above the one you chose, and `CLAUDE.md` imports (`@file`) are not followed. To stop Row-Bot reading a file, rename or remove it; an edit applies from your next message.

## The Developer Panel

- **Changes** lists changed files with their diffs (unified or split), and the agent's own change sets, each marked reviewed or not reviewed, with **Undo** or **Ask Row-Bot to undo** in its **⋯** menu. **Earlier agent changes** open their saved diffs.
- **Files** browses the folder and previews files.
- **Run** lists the checks Row-Bot detected (such as tests and linters) with their last result, runs a command you type (such as `npm test`) as a reviewed command, shows running processes with their output, and stops them. Sandbox changes waiting to be imported appear here too, each with its file count and when it was saved; commands Row-Bot runs for you show in the chat.
- **Git** switches or creates branches, commits with a suggested message, pushes (which asks first), opens a pull request through the GitHub command-line tool, and creates a separate worktree for this conversation. **Suggest pull request text** describes the branch from its commits and files. Confirmations and results appear beside the button that asked. Row-Bot can open a pull request from the conversation too, as a draft by default; see [What asks in a code folder](/docs/chat/tools-approvals-and-terminal#what-asks-in-a-code-folder).
- **Safety boundaries** shows what is allowed, what asks first and what is blocked here, where commands run, and whether the sandbox has network access.
- **Custom tools** turns the folder's commands into a reusable tool with the Custom Tool Builder. Your custom tools are also listed in **Settings › Tools › Custom tools**.

## End-To-End Workflow

1. Bind or clone the folder in a conversation.
2. Check the folder name, branch and changes in the panel.
3. Ask a question about the code, or describe the change you want.
4. Approve only the commands and edits you understand.
5. Run the checks from **Run**.
6. Review **Changes** before committing, then commit and push from **Git**.

## Parallel Child Workspaces

Writer ownership follows the resolved workspace folder. Children working in distinct folders or worktrees can edit concurrently, while writers aimed at the same folder are serialized to prevent overlapping changes. Changing only a shell working directory does not create an independent write boundary. Use a separate worktree or folder when two children genuinely need parallel write access.

## Sandbox Modes

Local mode lets Row-Bot operate in the selected workspace with your configured file and command permissions. Docker Sandbox mode, when available on a host installation, isolates command execution in a container and requires an import step before changes affect the real workspace. It requires a supported host Docker runtime and can differ from your local environment.

Inside the official Row-Bot application container, Developer Docker Sandbox is unavailable and a requested Docker workspace fails closed; Row-Bot never probes a nested daemon or silently runs that workspace locally. Local mode remains an explicit choice and can see only workspace paths deliberately mounted into the application container.

An approved risky Custom Tool is a third case: it deliberately executes in Local mode inside the application container against the selected visible Custom Tool path. That behavior is shown in the approval dialog and is not a nested Docker sandbox or fallback from a requested Docker workspace. See [Docker And VPS Operations](/docs/operations/docker#developer-and-headless-boundaries) for the complete container boundary.

For a host installation, start with Local mode on a disposable branch. Use Docker Sandbox when you want stronger isolation and the supported host runtime is available.

### The Sandbox Network And Prepare Sandbox

The Docker sandbox's network is **off** by default: commands there can't reach the internet, so they can't install packages either. Its image (`nikolaik/python-nodejs:python3.11-nodejs20`, Python and Node.js) has no pytest or project packages, so a project's first test run in the sandbox often can't start.

- When you choose Docker mode and the image isn't on this computer yet, **Git › Advanced › Sandbox** offers **Download image** (about 570 MB from Docker Hub). Docker downloads it once; the sandbox network stays off.
- When a test run in the sandbox can't start because pytest or the project's packages are missing, the chat says so and offers **Prepare sandbox**. It is also in **Git › Advanced › Sandbox**.
- **Prepare sandbox** reads what the tests need from the project's own files: the test extra or dependency group in `pyproject.toml` and the project itself, `requirements*.txt`, or `package.json` (installed by its lockfile), plus pytest for a Python project that has none. It asks first and shows what it will run.
- It turns the network on **for the install only**: the install runs in a separate, short-lived container of the sandbox's image, on the sandbox's copy of the folder. The sandbox's own network setting never changes. When the install finishes, fails or you press **Stop**, the install container is removed and the network is off again; the card says **Network off again** and **Details** records when it was on.
- Python packages go into the sandbox's copy only (`.row-bot-sandbox`), Node packages into its `node_modules`; neither is copied to your real folder.
- Row-Bot can prepare the sandbox itself when a test run fails this way. It asks by the conversation's **Approvals**, like any install: **Ask** asks, **Auto**'s reviewer may approve it when you clearly asked for the tests, **Hands-off** runs it, **Block** refuses.

When the sandbox network is **Ask** or **On**, and during Prepare sandbox's install, the sandbox reaches the **public internet only**. It sits on a private Docker network with no way out except Row-Bot's network gate, a small proxy container beside it. The gate refuses this computer (`host.docker.internal`, `localhost` and Docker's own addresses, so a local Ollama or Row-Bot itself), your local network and cloud metadata addresses, and connects only to the address it checked. `pip`, `npm`, `curl`, `git` over HTTPS, Python's own downloads and Node 24's `fetch` use it through the standard `HTTP_PROXY` and `HTTPS_PROXY` settings. Only HTTP and HTTPS get out: a program that ignores those settings can't connect, and neither can SSH, raw TCP, or UDP such as DNS lookups of its own. Git remotes over SSH (`git@github.com:…`) don't work in a networked sandbox: use the HTTPS remote (`https://github.com/…`) there.

The gate always runs from the default sandbox image (`nikolaik/python-nodejs:python3.11-nodejs20`), even when the folder uses another image, so that image needs to be on this computer. If the gate can't start, because that image is missing or Docker reports an error, the sandbox runs with its network **off**, never with Docker's ordinary network. The Developer panel then says **network off for now** and why, the agent is told in the command's result, and Row-Bot tries the gate again with the next command. Prepare sandbox doesn't install without the gate; its card says why.

**Safety boundaries** in the Developer panel says whether the sandbox network is on and what Prepare sandbox does.

## Troubleshooting

- If Row-Bot can't see your code, check that the folder is listed under **Working on** in the conversation's details card.
- If the folder you want isn't listed on a phone or in a browser, it isn't inside Row-Bot's workspace folder: move it there, clone it there, or choose it in the desktop app.
- If tests in the Docker sandbox say pytest or a module isn't installed, use **Prepare sandbox**; if Docker isn't running, start Docker Desktop (or Docker) and choose **Check again**.
- If an Agent folder assignment is rejected, confirm that the directory already exists and pass either that folder or an existing workspace ID, not both.
- If a command asks for approval, read the exact command and folder before approving. Only read-only commands such as `git status` run without asking in **Ask** mode.
- Undo on a **Created code folder** card in the chat removes the folder only while it is still empty; once files are added, it keeps them and says so.
- If Docker sandbox import is offered, review the patch before importing it into the real project.

## Knowledge

Route: /docs/knowledge/

Explore, search, review and correct what Row-Bot remembers in Home Knowledge, and configure memory in Settings Memory.

# Knowledge

Knowledge is Row-Bot's local memory: the facts, people, projects, preferences and relationships it has saved from conversations, documents and your own edits, connected as a graph. Row-Bot recalls relevant memories when they help a conversation.

For the relationship between thread history, memory, documents, the graph, Wiki Vault, and Dream Cycle, read [How Memory Becomes Knowledge](/docs/concepts/memory-knowledge-and-dream-cycle).

## Where To Find It

- **Home › Knowledge** is where you see and manage memories.
- **Settings › Memory** turns memory on or off, shows graph health, configures the [Wiki Vault](/docs/knowledge/wiki-vault), and holds **Delete all knowledge**.
- **Settings › Documents** configures document search and its embedding model.

## Views

Choose a view at the top of the Knowledge tab:

- **Graph** draws memories and their connections and lets the layout settle into place. It opens with up to 2,000 memories; **Show all memories** draws up to 5,000. Use **Zoom in**, **Zoom out** and **Fit**, and hide or show memory types from the legend.
- **List** shows the whole library, newest first, with search across every memory.
- **Review** is the queue of memories Row-Bot was unsure about. **Mark as reviewed**, **Edit memory** or **Archive memory** settles each one.
