Use **All** or **Pinned** to filter the feed, **Refresh** to read it again, **Pin** to keep an insight in view, and **Dismiss** to hide it (with **Undo**).

## Proposals

- **Suggest a fix** asks Row-Bot to prepare proposals for an insight that has none yet.
- **Apply proposal** makes the change, such as creating or updating a skill. Afterwards the insight says exactly what happened.
- **Reject proposal** declines it.
- Some proposals are review only: merging skills, changing a setting, or correcting a memory. Row-Bot can't make that change itself, so make it yourself if you agree, then reject the proposal.
- **Open investigation draft** opens a prepared conversation for a deeper look.
- **Copy feedback** copies a feedback report you can send yourself; Row-Bot never sends it.

## Skill Library Report

**Analyze skill library** reviews your installed skills and prepares proposals, such as two skills with similar instructions. It prepares proposals for your review; nothing is applied.

## What Is Saved

Insights and their proposals are local Row-Bot data. Applying a proposal changes only what that proposal names.

## Troubleshooting

- If the feed is empty, Row-Bot has nothing to report yet; new insights appear after it analyses recent work.
- If an action's outcome is not confirmed, use **Check outcome** before trying again.

## Phone And Native Desktop

Route: /docs/mobile-native/

Use the full Row-Bot owner product from a phone, connect it from Settings Devices & remote access, and understand native-only desktop behaviour.

# Phone And Native Desktop

A phone connected to your Row-Bot gets the whole owner product in a layout made for a small screen: conversations, Home with Overview, Workflows, Knowledge, Monitor and Insights, approvals, and every Settings page. The native desktop app adds operating-system integration such as the window, tray, microphone, the system's file and folder pickers, and the terminal. Layout never changes Row-Bot's authority or the approval rules of the underlying task.

## The Phone Layout

Row-Bot switches to the phone layout when the window is narrow, whatever the device.

- A slim top bar opens the sidebar as a drawer and opens the command palette.
- In a conversation, the header's **⋯** menu holds **Find in conversation**, **Conversation details**, **Export**, **Rename conversation**, the conversation's panels, and the command palette.
- Design and Developer panels open as full-screen sheets.
- Settings shows a **Settings section** list at the top instead of the side list. It holds every page, in the same six groups as on the desktop: Preferences, Appearance and Buddy; Providers, Models and Voice; Memory, Documents and Tracker; Tools and Skills; Apps; System, Devices & remote access, Updates and Data.

Files Row-Bot sends to your devices show in the conversation on the phone too, for as long as the conversation keeps them; only a file too large for a conversation is a download, which ends after 7 days (see [Sending Files](/docs/chat/tools-approvals-and-terminal#sending-files)).

A phone that reaches Row-Bot over HTTPS can turn on **Notifications on this device** in Settings › Devices & remote access (on an iPhone or iPad, add Row-Bot to the Home Screen first). When an approval or a question waits, the phone shows a short notice saying what it's about, such as "Row-Bot asked you a question: Which venue?". Turn **Show details in notifications** off for notices that say only "Row-Bot is waiting for you". See [Notifications On A Phone](/docs/privacy-safety#notifications-on-a-phone).

Voice works on a phone too: the Talk button starts it with one tap (or opens its menu when a Live voice key is saved), and the voice bar's **Full screen** shows the captions with the newest picture or video under them. The screen stays on while you talk. The phone stops listening when the screen locks or turns off, or when you switch apps, an iPhone Home Screen app included; the bar says so the first time. Microphone use away from the computer needs Tailscale or HTTPS. See [Voice And Buddy](/docs/voice-and-buddy/#home-and-phones).

On a phone, Row-Bot's Browser pane and pages fill the screen, with **Back** to the chat, and you can choose or clone a code folder inside Row-Bot's workspace folder. The interactive terminal, the system's own folder picker and its Save dialog need the Row-Bot desktop app on that computer.

## Connect A Phone

1. On the computer running Row-Bot, open **Settings › Devices & remote access** and choose **Connect a phone or computer**. The command palette finds it as "phone".
2. Choose **How will it reach this computer?**: **Tailscale** (private and encrypted, recommended), **Same Wi-Fi** (at home or the office, over HTTP), **Internet** (from anywhere, through your public link), or another address you set up yourself.
3. Choose how long it should **Stay signed in**: **30 days** or **12 hours**.
4. **Scan the code** with the phone's camera, or open the shown address on it.
5. On the phone, review the connection page and press **Connect** before the code expires.
6. **Your devices** lists every signed-in phone and computer; sign one out when it is lost, replaced, or no longer trusted.

The code expires after 10 minutes and works once. Opening it does not use it up until the phone presses **Connect**. The resulting session is a separate HttpOnly browser credential and never appears in the address.

Connecting grants access to your local Row-Bot instance. Do not share a code, expose the local server broadly, or use Same Wi-Fi HTTP on an untrusted network. Tailscale or an operator-managed HTTPS address is preferred and is required for browser microphone use away from the computer. See [Remote Access And Server Mode](/docs/operations/remote-access) for the complete connection and recovery model.

## Troubleshooting

- If the phone cannot connect, check the route you chose on the computer, the port, the firewall, and whether both devices can reach each other.
- If a code expired or was already used, show a new code rather than copying cookies or local credential files.
- If the connection page opens but the app stays unavailable, confirm the phone pressed **Connect** and that the device wasn't signed out.
- If an approval seems missing, open Overview: **Needs you** lists every waiting approval.
- If the phone layout appears on a computer, widen the window; the layout follows the window's width.

## How Row-Bot Works

Route: /docs/concepts/

Understand Row-Bot's request, knowledge, agent, workflow, and extension models before configuring them.

# How Row-Bot Works

These pages explain the ideas behind Row-Bot without walking through every control. Use them when you want to predict what the app will do, where data goes, why work continues in the background, or what an extension is allowed to change.

- [How A Request Runs](/docs/concepts/request-lifecycle) follows a message from a thread through model context, tools, approvals, and saved results.
- [How Memory Becomes Knowledge](/docs/concepts/memory-knowledge-and-dream-cycle) separates thread history, memory, documents, the Knowledge Graph, Wiki Vault, and Dream Cycle.
- [How Profiles, Goals, And Agents Work](/docs/concepts/profiles-goals-and-agents) explains reusable roles, durable objectives, parent coordination, and child-agent hand-offs.
- [How Background Workflows Run](/docs/concepts/background-workflows) explains schedules, run state, approvals, retries, and delivery.
- [Extensions And Trust Boundaries](/docs/concepts/extensions-and-trust) compares built-in tools, Skills, Custom Tools, plugins, MCP, channels, and accounts.
- [Learning](/docs/learning/) explains how Row-Bot learns from your own work: what it records, how every change is tested before it's offered, and the personal model. [How Row-Bot Learns](/docs/learning/how-row-bot-learns) explains the method it learns with, and how a new method is kept only if it does better.

Each page ends with links to the settings and task guides that change the behaviour it describes.

## How A Request Runs

Route: /docs/concepts/request-lifecycle

Follow a Row-Bot request through context assembly, a selected model route, tools, approvals, and local history.

# How A Request Runs

A Row-Bot request is a controlled loop, not a single message sent blindly to every connected service.

1. **A thread provides continuity.** Your message joins the selected conversation. The thread supplies recent history and any thread-specific model or profile choice.
2. **Row-Bot assembles useful context.** Depending on your settings and request, this can include profile instructions, pinned or task-selected Skills, attachments, and relevant local memory or document results. Enabled skills that are not yet selected stay in a compact searchable catalog. It does not mean the whole local data directory is attached.
3. **The selected model route receives the model prompt.** A local model keeps that inference on the configured local runtime. A hosted, API, subscription, or remote custom endpoint sends the assembled prompt to that provider under its terms.
4. **The model may answer or ask for a tool.** Core tools are bound under the active profile. In Auto mode, Row-Bot can search enabled external MCP, plugin, Custom Tool, and channel capabilities when needed. It then checks that the selected tool is enabled, provider-compatible, and permitted by policy.
5. **Consequential actions stop at an approval boundary.** The approval describes the proposed action and target. Rejecting it prevents that action; approving it does not give unrelated future actions permission.
6. **Tool results return to the active run.** A local file tool, browser, channel, account, plugin, or MCP server has its own execution and data boundary. The model can use the result to continue the loop.
7. **The result is recorded locally.** The thread keeps the conversation and run evidence. Optional extraction, memory, and document features decide what becomes reusable knowledge later.

## Three Boundaries To Keep In Mind

| Boundary | What crosses it | What controls it |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Model route | The assembled prompt and later tool results needed for reasoning. | Selected provider/model, thread override, profile or workflow policy. |
| Tool execution | Arguments needed by a local or external capability. | Tool enablement, workspace or account scope, approval policy. |
| Durable knowledge | Reviewed or extracted information that may be recalled in another request. | Memory, Knowledge, document, embedding, and retention settings. |

Local-first describes where Row-Bot and its durable data live. It does not make a hosted model, web tool, channel, remote MCP server, Live voice or cloud speech provider, or external account local.

## Change How Requests Run

- Choose routes and defaults in [Models And Providers](/docs/configuration/models-and-providers), [Provider Settings](/docs/settings/providers), and [Model Settings](/docs/settings/models).
- Control tools and approvals in [Tools, Approvals And Background Work](/docs/chat/tools-approvals-and-terminal) and [Privacy And Safety](/docs/privacy-safety/).
- Control reusable context in [Memory Settings](/docs/settings/knowledge), [Documents Settings](/docs/settings/documents), and [Skills Settings](/docs/settings/skills).
- Configure automatic or eager external capability loading in [Tools Settings](/docs/settings/tools) and read [Progressive Tools And Skills](/docs/guides/progressive-tools-and-skills).

## How Memory Becomes Knowledge

Route: /docs/concepts/memory-knowledge-and-dream-cycle

Understand thread history, memory, documents, the Knowledge Graph, Wiki Vault, and Dream Cycle as related but distinct layers.

# How Memory Becomes Knowledge

Row-Bot has several kinds of continuity. They work together, but none is a magical copy of everything the app has ever seen.

| Layer | What it represents | How it is used |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Thread history | Messages, attachments, tool traces, approvals, and results in one conversation. | Keeps the current conversation coherent and reviewable. |
| Memory | Reusable facts, preferences, summaries, and events saved or extracted for later recall. | Supplies selected relevant context to future requests when enabled. |
| Documents | Files deliberately added to the document library and split into searchable content. | Finds passages related to a question without placing every document in every prompt. |
| Knowledge Graph | Local entities and directed relationships with source and confidence information. | Connects related people, projects, events, facts, and sources during review and recall. |
| Wiki Vault | Linked Markdown pages generated from reviewed graph material. | Makes a portable, human-browsable projection in a folder you choose. |

## From Conversation To Recall

When extraction is enabled, Row-Bot reads what you said in eligible conversations, every new message once, and saves structured records. Each new memory is compared with the saved ones closest to it first. It is either added, written into the memory it adds to, saved as the newer version of one it changes (the older one is kept as history), or left out because it is already saved. So a later "use the light theme" replaces an earlier "use the dark theme" instead of sitting beside it. Documents are kept apart from what you said: a document never rewrites one of your own memories.

Search combines the available lexical, vector, and graph signals to choose candidates relevant to a later request. Only memories about what the request is about are brought in, a few at most, and often none.

Vector search uses an embedding model, which is separate from the chat model. The recommended local one is Mixedbread Embed Large v1, a 675 MB download you install from Settings › Documents. Until it is installed, or while it is unavailable or still loading, Row-Bot continues with bounded lexical and graph fallback instead of silently downloading during a chat. Install, retry, or repair the local model later in [Documents Settings](/docs/settings/documents), then rebuild document and memory vectors after changing models. Cloud embeddings are an explicit alternative that sends indexed text to the selected provider.

The source record matters. A graph relation or memory should remain traceable to the conversation, document, or process that produced it. Correct the underlying Knowledge record before rebuilding derived indexes or Wiki Vault pages.

An [incognito chat](/docs/chat/#incognito-chats) is left out of all this: nothing in it is read for memory, and a memory is saved from it only when you choose **Save** on the card that asks. Row-Bot can still use what it already remembers there.

## What Dream Cycle Does

Dream Cycle is idle-time knowledge maintenance. When enabled and due, it looks across all your memories for pairs that read alike. For each pair it decides whether they say the same thing (it merges them), whether the newer one replaces the older (the older is kept as history), or whether they are different (it leaves them and doesn't ask again). It also fills in thin memories from what you said, infers relationships that a conversation states, and lets unused inferred relationships fade until they are removed. Long records are never merged or replaced. It records its history so you can review what happened in Monitor.

Dream Cycle is not an autonomous second assistant and it does not make external facts true. It should run only during the configured window while the app is idle. Inferred relationships use confidence thresholds, but important knowledge still deserves human review.

## Lessons From Learning

With [Learning](/docs/learning/) on, Row-Bot can draft a **lesson** from your work: a short "do it this way" note, such as "When two documents share a title, choose by ID". A lesson is tested before it's offered, and goes into use only when you choose **Use this change** (or, if you chose it, when it passes its test). A lesson in use is saved as a memory of how to work, so recall brings it up like any memory when a request is about what it covers, and the reply says "Used a lesson".

Manage lessons in Home › Learning › [Lessons](/docs/learning/lessons). A lesson's memory also appears in Home › Knowledge; if you delete it there, Lessons shows **Memory removed** and Row-Bot stops using it. Learning's own record of how Row-Bot handled your requests is kept apart from memory, and deleting learning data doesn't delete your memories.

## What Wiki Vault Does

Wiki Vault writes a readable view of selected graph material. The graph remains the source of truth; the vault is a generated output. If the destination is synced to a cloud drive, repository, or publishing tool, that folder becomes a separate sharing boundary.

## Configure And Review It

- Review memories in [Knowledge](/docs/knowledge/) (Home › Knowledge) and investigate changes in [Monitor](/docs/monitor/).
- Turn memory on or off, check graph health and configure Wiki output in [Memory Settings](/docs/settings/knowledge); Dream Cycle's hours are in Settings › Preferences, and Learning uses the same hours.
- Review the lessons Learning uses in [Lessons](/docs/learning/lessons), and set Learning up in [Learning Settings](/docs/settings/learning).
- Configure indexed files in [Documents Settings](/docs/settings/documents).
- Set up the export folder in [Wiki Vault](/docs/knowledge/wiki-vault) and correct mistakes with [Provenance And Repair](/docs/knowledge/provenance-repair).
- Back up the related local data as one set using [Operations, Data, And Recovery](/docs/operations/).

## How Profiles, Goals, And Agents Work

Route: /docs/concepts/profiles-goals-and-agents

Understand reusable Agent Profiles, durable goals, parent coordination, and bounded child-agent delegation.

# How Profiles, Goals, And Agents Work

Profiles, goals, and agent runs describe different parts of long-running work.

- An **Agent Profile** is a reusable operating role: instructions, model policy, Skills, tools, delegation limits, and approval policy.
- A **goal** is the durable objective and finish condition for a piece of work that may span several turns.
- An **agent run** is one execution attempt with a prompt, model, status, result, and evidence.
- A **parent agent** coordinates the objective and combines results.
- A **child agent** receives a bounded subtask and returns a hand-off to its parent.

## Why Delegate

Delegation is useful when independent research, inspection, or implementation can happen in parallel or needs a specialist profile. It is less useful when agents would edit the same small resource or when only one decision is needed. The parent remains responsible for deciding whether the combined evidence actually completes the goal.

Child agents do not become invisible background permissions. Their runs remain linked to the parent, and a returned result is evidence rather than automatic authorisation to write, send, publish, or declare the goal complete. Tool availability and approvals still apply to the run doing the action.

Delegation capacity is bounded. Each new run snapshots the application-wide work-round, nesting, per-parent concurrency, app-wide concurrency, and optional child active-time settings. When capacity is full, eligible children wait in a first-in, first-out queue rather than bypassing the limits.

## Status And Hand-Offs

An active goal can accumulate progress across turns, with no turn limit unless you set one. After each turn Row-Bot judges whether the goal made progress, is done, or is blocked; two turns without progress, the same step failing three times, or two progress checks in a row that couldn't run, pause it with the reason so you can decide. A goal doesn't continue by itself after Row-Bot closes and opens again: it comes back paused, and you resume it. Completion should mean the finish condition and required checks are satisfied. A block should identify a real impasse, not merely unfinished work. Stopping an agent ends that run without deleting the parent thread, goal history, or already-recorded evidence.

The work-round budget is checked at model, tool, and resume boundaries so a restart cannot reset it. Repeated no-progress states are blocked and then terminated cleanly, and every terminal path writes one durable final status and reason.

A useful child-agent hand-off says what was checked, what changed, what evidence was found, what remains uncertain, and whether any consequential action still needs the parent or user.

## Configure And Use It

- Create and select roles, set goals and follow delegated agents with [Profiles, Goals, And Agents](/docs/profiles-goals-agents/).
- Choose a profile in a workflow with [Workflows](/docs/guides/workflows).
- Control the models behind runs in [Models And Providers](/docs/configuration/models-and-providers).
- Review waiting work and failures in [Home: Overview](/docs/home/overview) or [Monitor](/docs/monitor/).

## How Background Workflows Run

Route: /docs/concepts/background-workflows

Understand saved workflow definitions, schedules, isolated runs, approvals, retries, and delivery semantics.

# How Background Workflows Run

A workflow is a saved message (or a few) with a schedule and an approval level. A run is one turn of the workflow's own conversation: Row-Bot sends the message there in the background and works on it exactly as in a chat. Keeping the definition and its runs separate lets Row-Bot preserve history when you edit the next schedule or a run fails.

1. **A trigger starts a run.** This can be a manual click, a recurring schedule, a one-time time, a webhook, or another workflow finishing.
2. **The run is a chat turn.** It has every tool a chat has, finds apps and tools the same way, and uses the workflow's Agent Profile, model and approval level. A second message, if the workflow has one, is sent after the first turn ends.
3. **The run gets its own record.** Status, what its tools did outside Row-Bot (with links), and its conversation are recorded so the scheduler can recover cleanly.
4. **Approval can pause the run.** An action that needs a decision waits on the same card a chat shows, in the workflow's conversation and in the sidebar's attention indicator and Overview's **Needs you**. Approving lets the turn go on; saying no ends the run **You said no**. A run still waiting when the next one starts is replaced and its card withdrawn, so runs don't pile up and an old action can't go out late.
5. **Completion and delivery are recorded separately.** A useful result can complete even if an external channel delivery fails, so the app can show the result and the delivery problem honestly.

## Delivery Defaults

The web app always receives run status. External channels are an additional destination.

- **Inherit defaults** means the workflow uses the current workflow-level external channel selection.
- **An explicit empty selection** means web app only, even when a global external default exists.
- **An explicit channel selection** targets those configured running channels.

This distinction prevents a workflow that was deliberately set to app-only from beginning to send externally after someone changes the global default.

## Failure And Retry

A failed run remains evidence. A run that fails on a passing problem (the network, a rate limit, a busy provider) tries again by itself after a wait, twice at most, but never once something has gone out: then it ends and says so, and nothing is sent twice. A run has no step limit; it stops when it keeps repeating itself, when you press Stop, or after a very long run of steps, where it asks **Keep going?** in its conversation. Fix the underlying provider, model, approval, input, or delivery problem before running it again.

Scheduled work can outlive the screen where it was created, but it cannot outlive the local Row-Bot process indefinitely. Pausing a workflow prevents future schedule starts; stopping one active run does not necessarily change the saved schedule.

## Configure And Operate It

- Create schedules, profiles, approvals, messages, and delivery in [Workflows](/docs/guides/workflows).
- Configure external destinations in [Channels](/docs/integrations/channels); each channel is an app in [Settings › Apps](/docs/settings/apps#built-in-ways-to-connect).
- Review live status in [Monitor](/docs/monitor/) and waiting approvals in [Home: Overview](/docs/home/overview), on the desktop or a [phone](/docs/mobile-native/).
- Back up workflow definitions and history with [Operations, Data, And Recovery](/docs/operations/).

## Extensions And Trust Boundaries

Route: /docs/concepts/extensions-and-trust

Compare Row-Bot tools, Skills, Custom Tools, plugins, MCP servers, channels, and accounts by what they add and where they run.

# Extensions And Trust Boundaries

Row-Bot can learn a procedure, gain a tool, load code, connect a server, or authorise an account. Those are different changes and deserve different review.

| Capability | What it adds | Main trust question |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Built-in tool | A maintained capability shipped with Row-Bot. | Is it enabled for this profile, and does this action need approval? |
| Skill | Instructions, examples, and supporting files that shape behaviour. | Do the instructions match your intent and avoid unexpected data or tool use? |
| Custom Tool | Reviewed local code or a command exposed as a reusable tool. | What code runs, in which workspace, with which dependencies and command class? |
| Plugin (package) | A packaged extension that can add code, tools, Skills, apps, configuration, or UI. | Do you trust its publisher, source, permissions, dependencies, and update path? |
| App | Tools from a hosted service, or from a program that runs on this computer. | What can it access, where does it run, and what may it do without asking? |
| Channel | A bridge for incoming messages or outgoing results. | Who can contact it, which conversation receives replies, and may workflows deliver there? |
| Account | Authorisation for a service such as GitHub, Google, or X. | Which service scopes and account data become available to enabled tools? |

## Instructions Are Not Permissions

A Skill or profile can tell the model when to use a capability, but it does not create credentials or bypass Row-Bot's tool and approval policy. Conversely, connecting an app or adding a package can add real executable capability even when no Skill mentions it. Review both the guidance layer and the execution layer.

When you connect an app, you choose what it may do: **Read only**, **Ask before changes** (the default) or **Full access**. Deleting, sending, paying, publishing, running code and unknown actions always ask, whichever you choose; Full access only lets routine changes run without asking.

Progressive discovery preserves this separation. Loading a skill adds instructions to one task; it cannot make a profile-denied tool callable. Searching an enabled external-tool catalog does not enable a tool, change its provider schema, or bypass its approval classification.

## Local Does Not Always Mean Harmless

A local plugin, command, or MCP process can still read files, start programs, or use locally stored credentials. A remote server or account can send data outside the app even if its configuration is stored locally. Use narrow workspaces, least-privilege accounts, disabled-by-default imports, and fictional test data.

Third-party dependency telemetry is not Row-Bot telemetry. Review dependency behaviour before installation and do not expose prompts, files, memories, secrets, screenshots, tool arguments, or channel content unless that transfer is the feature you intentionally selected.

## Browse And Configure Extensions

- Compare extension types and browse screenshots in [Extend Row-Bot](/docs/extending/).
- Browse and review Skills in [Skills](/docs/skills/) and [Skills Settings](/docs/settings/skills).
- Understand automatic capability selection in [Progressive Tools And Skills](/docs/guides/progressive-tools-and-skills) and configure it in [Tools Settings](/docs/settings/tools).
- Find, connect, and choose access for apps and packages in [Apps Settings](/docs/settings/apps), with background in [Hosted And Local Apps](/docs/integrations/mcp) and [Packages](/docs/integrations/plugins).
- Configure external messaging in [Channels](/docs/integrations/channels) and service authorisation in [Accounts And Authorisation](/docs/integrations/accounts).

## Settings

Route: /docs/settings/

Find every Row-Bot settings page: six groups from General to System, with search for any setting.

# Settings

Settings is where Row-Bot is configured: where models come from and which one does each job, memory and documents, tools, skills and apps (your accounts and messaging channels included), and how Row-Bot runs on this computer and your other devices.

Open it with **Settings** at the bottom of the sidebar. The pages are grouped down the left side; **Find a setting** (press / on a Settings page) searches page names and individual settings and jumps to the exact row. The command palette finds them too, and can flip common switches in place. On a phone, a **Settings section** list at the top replaces the side list; every page and setting is still there.

## How Settings Is Organized

| Group | Page | What it changes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **General** | [Preferences](/docs/settings/preferences) | The assistant's name and personality, how Row-Bot opens, and the overnight Dream Cycle. |
| | [Appearance](/docs/settings/preferences#appearance) | Theme, accent colour, density and transparency on this device, and panel sizes. |
| | [Buddy](/docs/settings/buddy) | Your companion's look, personality and motion, and the desktop overlay. |
| | [Learning](/docs/settings/learning) | Learning on or off, what it learns from, how changes are used, its monthly limit, the personal model, creating skills while chatting, and learning data. |
| **Models** | [Models](/docs/settings/models) | The main model and the models for Vision, Image and Video, your starred models, the connected providers ([how to connect each](/docs/settings/providers)), limits for long work, and the catalog. |
| | [Voice](/docs/settings/voice) | Talk, dictation and read-aloud. |
| **Knowledge** | [Memory](/docs/settings/knowledge) | Remembering on or off, graph health and the wiki vault. Memories themselves live in Home › Knowledge. |
| | [Documents](/docs/settings/documents) | Files Row-Bot can search, and where search runs. |
| | [Tracker](/docs/settings/tracker) | Habits, symptoms and health events you track. |
| **Capabilities** | [Tools](/docs/settings/tools) | Capability loading, search tools, built-in tools and custom tools. |
| | [Skills](/docs/settings/skills) | Find, add, try and remove skills, and create or edit your own. |
| **Connections** | [Apps](/docs/settings/apps) | The services Row-Bot can work in, including the GitHub, Google (Gmail and Calendar), Outlook (mail and calendar) and X accounts and the Telegram, WhatsApp, Discord, Slack and SMS channels: find, connect, choose what each may do, change settings, turn off and remove. |
| **System** | [System](/docs/settings/system) | The workspace folder, what Row-Bot may do (commands, files, browser and computer use), Privacy (the anonymous install count), and logs. |
| | [Devices & remote access](/docs/operations/remote-access) | Connect a phone or computer, your signed-in devices, network access and the public link. |
| | [Updates](/docs/operations/updates) | The version you have, background downloads, Restart to update, Repair, and the update channel. |
| | [Data](/docs/operations/#back-up) | Back up and restore, import from another assistant, and irreversible clean-up. |

Goals belong to one conversation and are set in its details card; agent profiles are managed in the sidebar's **Agents** dialog. See [Profiles, Goals, And Agents](/docs/profiles-goals-agents/).

All authenticated owner sessions see the same settings on every device. On phones and tablets, the layout adapts to the screen; the available settings and authority do not change.

## A Good Setup Order

1. Providers
2. Models
3. Documents and Tools
4. Skills
5. System access
6. Apps, including your accounts and channels
7. Voice and Buddy
8. Preferences and Appearance

Accounts and channels used to have their own Settings pages; they are apps now. Old links open the matching app.

## Safety Notes

Credentials belong in Providers or in an app's setup in Apps (accounts and channels included), not in chat messages. Turn on only the tools and apps you intend to use. Review approvals before actions that write files, run commands, use accounts, contact external services, or send messages.

## Settings: Preferences

Route: /docs/settings/preferences

Set the assistant's name and personality, how Row-Bot opens, the overnight Dream Cycle, and this device's appearance.

# Settings: Preferences

Preferences are personal choices: how Row-Bot introduces itself, how it opens, and when it tidies memory overnight. **Appearance**, the page after it in the **General** group, sets how Row-Bot looks on this device.

## Where To Find It

Open **Settings**, then choose **Preferences** in the **General** group, or search for it with **Find a setting**.

## Identity

- **Name** is the assistant's name.
- **Personality** sets the assistant's default tone; a preview shows how it sounds.

**Learn new skills** is now **Create skills while chatting**, in [Settings › Learning](/docs/settings/learning#while-chatting). It works with Learning on or off.

## Opening Row-Bot

**Open in** chooses whether Row-Bot opens in its own app window, in your browser, or asks each time.

## Overnight Tidy-Up

**Dream Cycle** tidies memory while you are away: it merges duplicates, enriches thin memories and infers missing links. Choose the **Hours** it may run (start and end hour). [Learning](/docs/learning/) works in the same hours. Its runs appear in Monitor's **History**, and Home › Knowledge can run it at any time.

## Appearance

**Settings › Appearance** applies to this device only, so a phone and a computer can look different:

- **Appearance**: **System** (follows your device), **Light** or **Dark**.
- **Colour theme**: **Blue**, **Teal**, **Violet** or **Amber**.
- **Density**: **Comfortable** or **Compact**.
- **Reduce transparency** turns off the glass effect.
- **Workspace layout › Panel sizes** restores panel sizes without changing conversations or the look.

A preview shows the result as you choose. In the command palette, "dark mode", "light mode" and "follow the system appearance" change it in one step.

## What Moved

- **Updates** (background downloads, Restart to update, Repair and the update channel) is its own page in the **System** group. See [Updates](/docs/operations/updates).
- **Import from another assistant** (Hermes Agent or OpenClaw) is on **Settings › Data**, with back up and restore. See [Operations, Data, And Recovery](/docs/operations/#back-up).

## What Is Saved

Preferences are global local settings. Appearance is saved on each device. Existing conversations keep their own model, profile and approval choices.

## Privacy And Safety

These settings stay on your computer. Dream Cycle works on local memory and uses your chosen model when it needs one, which may be a hosted provider.

## Control-Level Reference

The [generated Settings Controls reference](/docs/reference/generated/settings-controls#preferences-controls) lists every searchable setting on this page with its deep link, search keywords, and any dependency or security notes.

## Troubleshooting

- If the app opens in the wrong place, change **Open in** and restart Row-Bot.
- If Dream Cycle never runs, check that it is on and that its hours include times your computer is awake.
- If the look differs between devices, that is expected: Appearance is saved per device.

## Settings: Buddy

Route: /docs/settings/buddy

Use Buddy in the sidebar or as a desktop pet, message the selected thread from its bubble, handle approvals, make new looks, and configure how it moves.

# Settings: Buddy

Buddy is Row-Bot's companion: a painted character that comes alive on your screen. It breathes, blinks, looks at your cursor, leans in while Row-Bot thinks, hops when work finishes and looks worried when something fails. Everything about how it moves runs on your computer; nothing is downloaded or generated while it animates.

It starts in the sidebar and, in the native Windows and macOS apps, can be dragged out onto the desktop as a pet. The pet's speech bubble is a smaller view of the thread selected in Row-Bot: it uses that thread's model, tools, approval mode, saved draft, and conversation rather than starting a separate assistant.

## Where To Find It

Open **Settings**, then choose **Buddy** in the **General** group, or search for it with **Find a setting**.

## Put Buddy On The Desktop

1. Turn on **Show Buddy** if the companion is hidden.
2. Press and drag Buddy itself away from its sidebar dock, or choose **Pop out Buddy**. Releasing it back over the dock cancels the move.
3. Let go where you want it. Buddy lands on whatever is under its feet: the top edge of a window, or the floor above the taskbar (Windows) or the Dock (macOS).
4. Drag Buddy whenever you want to move it. It stays always-on-top, but only Buddy itself and its open bubble take clicks; the empty space around it passes clicks to whatever is underneath.

When Buddy sits on a window, it rides along as that window moves. If you switch to another window and keep using it for a few seconds, Buddy hops over to it (at most every 20 seconds, never while its bubble is open or while you drag it). If its window closes, is minimised, maximised or goes full screen, Buddy floats down to the floor. Drop it on the taskbar or desktop to stop it following until you drop it on a window again, or turn off **Sit on the window I'm using** below.

The desktop pet requires the native Windows or macOS application. Browser/server mode, Linux browser-first launch, and the phone layout keep Buddy inside Row-Bot.

## Message The Selected Thread

Click Buddy to open its bubble. Buddy also opens it by itself for an approval, a question, a response that failed or was interrupted, and a finished reply (which tucks away again after a few seconds unless you are typing in it). Press Esc or click Buddy to close it.

The title at the top of the bubble identifies the thread that will receive your next message. Buddy follows the conversation selected in the main Row-Bot window: switch conversations there and Buddy switches with you. The smaller line shows whether that thread is a Chat, Code, or Design conversation and what it is doing. If no thread is selected, Buddy follows your most recent conversation.

- Type into **Message this thread...**. Enter sends; Shift+Enter adds a line.
- The full composer and the bubble share the saved draft for each thread. Switching threads loads that thread's draft without merging it into another conversation.
- Sending captures the thread and the Chat, Code, or Design context shown at that moment, so changing the main-window selection during a run does not silently retarget the request.
- After sending, the bubble shows current progress, the latest response, or an error. If a response was interrupted (for example by a restart), **Resume** continues it.
- Use **Stop** to stop the selected thread's active response. Buddy does not retry the turn by itself.
- Attachments, transcript history, tool traces, model selection, and microphone controls remain in the full Row-Bot thread. Use **Open full thread** when you need them.

The bubble is a text composer, not a second microphone session. While you talk with Row-Bot in the main window (Row-Bot Voice or Live voice), Buddy shows that it is listening and its mouth moves with Row-Bot's voice, docked or on the desktop; it does the same when Row-Bot reads a reply aloud. Talk and Dictate remain in the full thread. A voice turn submitted there belongs to the same conversation and its progress can still appear in Buddy.

## Review Approvals

Buddy never creates a separate approval policy. It projects the selected thread's existing gate:

- The current approval shows **Deny**, **Details**, and **Approve** in the bubble. Ctrl+Enter (Cmd+Enter on macOS) approves.
- **Details** opens the full thread so you can inspect the complete request before deciding.
- If the selected thread or pending generation no longer matches, Buddy opens the full thread instead of approving a stale request.

## Buddy's Menu And Lifecycle

Right-click Buddy (or use the buttons in its bubble):

- **Open Row-Bot** (**Open full thread** in the bubble) restores the main Row-Bot window at the selected conversation.
- **Dock Buddy** returns Buddy to its sidebar dock.
- **Hide Buddy** hides it without docking. Use the tray's **Show Buddy** action to bring it back.
- While Buddy is torn off, closing the main Row-Bot window hides that window instead of quitting the app. Use **Open full thread**, **Open Row-Bot** in the tray, or the tray's quit action as appropriate.
- Tear-off is session-scoped. A fresh Row-Bot launch resets placement to the sidebar dock; a saved hidden preference remains hidden until you show Buddy.
- The bubble follows Row-Bot's appearance setting (System, Light, or Dark). With your device's reduced-motion setting on, Buddy stays still apart from blinking and its expressions.

## Appearance Controls

The Buddy page follows the conversation you have open, because Buddy uses that conversation's profile and approvals; open a conversation first if it asks.

- **Show Buddy** shows or hides the companion.
- **Look** chooses one of the six bundled Buddies or one you made. **New look…** makes one with your image model; **Refresh looks** reads them again.
- **Personality** changes the tone of Buddy's status cues.
- **Bubbles** changes how visual status appears.
- **Sit on the window I'm using** (native apps) lets the desktop Buddy follow you from window to window.
- **Motion** chooses how lively Buddy is: **Calm**, **Normal** or **Lively**.
- **Advanced Buddy settings** holds Buddy's **Name**, optional **Style notes** for new looks, and **Compact size**.

Buddy's picture is also the speaker mark beside Row-Bot's replies in conversations.

## Make A New Look

**New look…** opens the hatch. Describe the Buddy you want, optionally pick a body (**Floater**, **Little biped**, **Winged**, or **Pick for me**, which chooses from your description), and choose **Hatch Buddy**. Your image model paints the character, then paints six small edits of it (eyes closed, mouth open, happy, worried, focused and surprised); Row-Bot cuts it out, fits it with bones and turns the edits into its expressions, all on your computer. That is seven image requests to your provider, which may cost credits. Your current look stays until the new one is ready, and **Stop Hatch** stops it.

Image models that only make new pictures (such as Imagen) cannot paint the expressions; choose a GPT Image or Nano Banana model in Settings › Models.

A look made before Row-Bot 5.3.4 comes alive from its picture without any request. To give it blinks and expressions too, select it and choose **Bring to life** (six image requests).

## Common Workflow

1. Select the thread you want and confirm its name in the main window.
2. Drag Buddy out of the sidebar, click it, and confirm the same name appears at the top of its bubble.
3. Type a short message, review any approval, and use **Open full thread** when you need the complete transcript or tool details.
4. Use **Dock Buddy** when you want it back in the sidebar.
5. Make a new look only after an image model is ready in Settings › Models; choose **Calm** motion if animation is distracting.

## What Is Saved

Buddy visibility, appearance, where it last sat on the desktop, and thread drafts are local app data. The bubble does not copy conversations into a second store. Making a new look calls your configured image model; animating Buddy never does.

## Privacy And Safety

The bubble follows the same privacy and safety boundaries as the selected thread. A hosted model, tool, account, channel, MCP server, plugin, or media provider can still send data externally when that thread uses it. Undocking Buddy does not grant new permissions or bypass approvals.

To sit on your windows, the desktop Buddy reads the position and size of the window you are using, and where your cursor is so it can look at it. It never reads window titles, app names, contents or pixels, and none of this leaves your computer. Turn off **Sit on the window I'm using** to stop it following windows.

## Control-Level Reference

The [generated Settings Controls reference](/docs/reference/generated/settings-controls#buddy-controls) lists every searchable setting on this page with its deep link, search keywords, and any dependency or security notes.

## Troubleshooting

- If Buddy does not appear in the sidebar, turn on **Show Buddy** and reload the current page if needed.
- If a drag snaps back, start the gesture on Buddy itself and release away from the original dock. Drag-to-undock is unavailable outside the native Windows and macOS apps.
- If a hidden desktop Buddy is still torn off, use **Show Buddy** from the system tray.
- If Buddy keeps hopping to windows you don't want it on, drop it on the taskbar or Dock, or turn off **Sit on the window I'm using**.
- If Row-Bot's main window is hidden, use **Open Row-Bot** from the tray or **Open full thread** from Buddy.
- If the bubble shows the wrong conversation, select the intended thread in Row-Bot and verify the bubble's title before sending.
- If an approval needs more context, choose **Review** or **Details** and decide in the full thread.
- Restart Row-Bot to reset desktop placement to the sidebar dock. Then enable **Show Buddy** if a saved hidden preference keeps it out of view.
- If making a new look fails, check that an image model that can edit pictures is chosen and its provider is connected.
- If Buddy shows as a still picture, your computer could not start its animation (no WebGL 2); everything else works.

## Settings: Learning

Route: /docs/settings/learning

Turn Learning off or on, choose what it learns from, how changes are used, its monthly token limit, experimental learning, the personal model and its training, and delete learning data in Settings Learning.

# Settings: Learning

Settings › Learning turns [Learning](/docs/learning/) off and on and holds all its settings: what it learns from, how changes are used, how much it may spend, experimental learning, the personal model, and the learning data on this computer. Learning is on from the start; experimental learning, reading past chats and the personal model are off until you turn them on. **Create skills while chatting** is here too, with Learning on or off.

## Where To Find It

Open **Settings**, then choose **Learning** in the **General** group, or search for it with **Find a setting**. In the Learning tab, **⋯ › Learning settings** opens it too.

## While Learning Is Off

A card says what Learning does, with **Turn on Learning**, which opens the setup sheet (see [Turn It On Again](/docs/learning/#turn-it-on-again)). **How it works** opens a short summary:

- Row-Bot keeps a private record of how it handled your requests, on this computer.
- During quiet hours it looks for things to do better and tests each idea on tasks it hasn't seen. Nothing changes without a test, and it asks you first.
- It can also train a personal model of your own that runs on this computer. Downloads always ask first.
- Everything can be undone, and you can delete the data at any time.

If learning data from before is kept, the card says how much, with **Delete learning data…**. If Learning's saved settings can't be read, the card says so and Learning stays off.

## Status

At the top: **Learning on** or **Learning paused**, with this month's spending ("240K of 2M tokens this month", or "3M tokens this month (no limit)"). While a command is under way it says **Pausing Learning…**, **Resuming Learning…** or **Turning Learning off…**.

The page menu (**More for Learning**) has **Open Learning** and **Pause Learning** or **Resume Learning**.

## Learning

- **Learning** switches it off. "Turn off Learning?" says that Row-Bot stops recording, testing and training, that changes and models in use stay in use (undo them in Learning), and that your learning data is kept until you delete it. Choose **Turn off** or **Keep it on**.
- While paused, the row says "Paused: nothing new is recorded, tested or trained", with **Resume**.

## Learn From

- **My chats**: your chats in Row-Bot, and your own direct chats on Telegram, Slack and other apps.
- **Workflows and goals**.
- **Also learn from the last 30 days of chats** (off unless you turn it on): Row-Bot reads them in the background, and the row shows "Reading 214 past chats · 61 done" while it does.

Chats with other people are never used. Switch any chat off from its menu with **Don't learn from this chat**. A messaging app set up without your own user ID shows a line such as "Telegram chats are used once your user ID is set in Settings › Apps › Telegram."

## Changes And Spending

### Using Changes

- **Ask me first** (the default): a change that passes its test waits for you to review it.
- **Use changes that pass their tests**: lessons, ways of working and skill edits that pass go into use by themselves, listed under Overnight with **Undo**.

New personal-model versions always ask. See [Using Changes](/docs/learning/changes#using-changes).

### Monthly Limit

Learning uses your default model to find and test improvements. **Monthly limit** caps the tokens it uses each calendar month. The row shows how many it used this month, and the hint says what the limit buys, such as "About 20 tests of a change. Local models don't count."

| Choice | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| **500K tokens** to **50M tokens** | A fixed limit: 500K, 1M, 2M (the default), 5M, 10M, 20M or 50M tokens a month. |
| **Custom amount…** | Type any amount from 0.1 to 1,000 million tokens, such as 75 or 2.5. It's saved when you press Enter or leave the field. |
| **No limit** | Nothing caps what Learning spends each month, comparing methods included. It asks first ("Change it" or "Cancel"). What it spends still shows each month. |
| **No model calls** | Learning makes no model calls. Local models still work. |

- Tokens from local models, such as Ollama or a custom endpoint on this computer, don't count.
- When the limit is reached, testing waits for the next month and local training continues. Overview shows the date, with **Raise limit**, which opens this setting.
- With experimental learning on, comparing learning methods uses at most a fifth of the limit, kept for it, and the hint says so. With **No limit**, each method in a comparison still gets the same budget.

### Quiet Hours

When Learning does its work: the same hours as Dream Cycle. **Change** opens them in Settings › Preferences › Overnight tidy-up.

## Experimental

**Try experimental learning** is off unless you turn it on. It adds three things, each still tested and still asking you first:

- **Practice**: during quiet hours, Row-Bot makes up a few tasks like the ones it got wrong, runs them in throwaway sandboxes, and uses those it checks in its tests and, if you train one, in your personal model's training. Overview's **Overnight** says how it went, such as "Practised 12 document tasks it made up: 9 passed".
- **A quick question**: at most once a day, when it can't tell what to change, Overview's **Needs you** asks one question with two answers. It never holds anything up; **✕** waves it away.
- **Comparing ways of learning**: see [How Row-Bot Learns](/docs/learning/how-row-bot-learns).

They use more of the **Monthly limit**.

## Personal Model

See [Personal Model](/docs/learning/personal-model) for what each part does.

- **Train during quiet hours** (off unless you turn it on): trains a model of your own on your work while you're away. Turning it on, on a computer that can train, asks to download the training engine and the starting model ("Download the training engine and Qwen3.5 9B?"): **Download** or **Not now**. Off, a run starts only when you choose **Train now**.
- **Where to train**: **This computer** or **Hugging Face**. Hugging Face uses your own account, priced before each run.
- **Training engine**: installed and its size, with **Remove** (it asks first: nothing trains until you download it again), or **Download…**. It shows the download while it runs.
- **Starting model**: its name, licence and that it comes from Hugging Face, with its size or download size. **Change…** (when training on this computer) opens the starting models, with **Other models**; **Delete** removes a downloaded one (it asks first), and **Download…** downloads it.
- **Download**: while the engine or starting model downloads, or needs you, its progress and **Stop**, **Resume**, **Cancel** or **Try again**.

With **Where to train** set to **Hugging Face**:

- **Hugging Face account**: **Sign in with Hugging Face**, or who you're signed in as, with **Sign out**.
- **Model on Hugging Face**: the model it trains there. Only models this computer can run afterwards are offered. **Other models…** finds and checks any open model.
- **Monthly spending cap**: $10, $20, $50 or $100 a month, with what you've spent this month. Runs in quiet hours start only while they fit the cap. Until your first run: "Chosen with your first run".

See [Training On Hugging Face](/docs/learning/hugging-face).

## While Chatting

**Create skills while chatting** lets Row-Bot offer to save multi-step work as a skill under a reply ([Save how Row-Bot did something](/docs/skills/#save-how-row-bot-did-something)) and suggest improvements to the skills it uses. Nothing is saved until you approve. Turn it off to keep the skill library exactly as you set it. It works with Learning on or off. It used to be **Learn new skills** in Settings › Preferences.

## Learning Data

**Kept on this computer** shows the size of your learning data, including pictures from browser and computer use (up to 10 GB; the oldest go first). Turning Learning off keeps it. **Delete learning data…** lists what it deletes and can't be undone. See [Pause, Turn Off Or Delete](/docs/learning/#pause-turn-off-or-delete).

## Privacy And Safety

Learning's records, tests and models stay on this computer. Its own model calls go to your default model's provider. Hugging Face is used only if you choose it. See [Privacy And Safety](/docs/privacy-safety/#learning).

## Troubleshooting

- **Turn on Learning is missing**: Learning's saved settings can't be read, so Learning stays off.
- **Learning spends nothing**: the limit is **No model calls**, or your default model is local.
- **Training doesn't start**: check **Train during quiet hours**, the training engine and the starting model here, then the Personal model view for what it's waiting for.

## Settings: Providers

Route: /docs/settings/providers

Connect local, hosted, subscription, and custom model providers.

# Settings: Providers

Providers are the model services Row-Bot can call. This page answers whether each provider is connected, what kind of credential it uses, and whether Row-Bot has enough information to use it for chat, tools, designs, code, voice, or embeddings.

## Where To Find It

Providers are on **Settings › Models**, under **Connected**. Search for a provider's name with **Find a setting**, or open it from the model picker's **Connect**. Links to the old Providers page land there.

## Controls

- Each connected provider has a tile; its sheet holds its connection, its models and **Refresh**. **Add a provider** lists the ones not connected yet, by how you pay.
- Local providers show runtimes such as Ollama. Refresh checks what the local service currently exposes.
- Subscription accounts show providers that use a plan you already pay for: ChatGPT / Codex, Claude (your Claude plan) and xAI Grok. Its sheet sets it up, reconnects it, tests it or refreshes its models.
- ChatGPT signs in with a code: open OpenAI's page, enter the code Row-Bot shows, and Row-Bot notices when you approve, on this computer or another device. Grok signs in on xAI's page, which then returns to the computer Row-Bot runs on. From another device, such as a phone or a hosted Row-Bot, that last page doesn't load: copy its address from the address bar and paste it into Row-Bot. Starting a sign-in again replaces one left waiting.
- API providers show services that need an API key or compatible endpoint. Their sheet has the key field for that provider, and a link to the provider's page for making one.
- OpenRouter's sheet also offers **Sign in with OpenRouter** instead of pasting a key: OpenRouter's page opens (it makes you a free account if you need one), and when you approve, Row-Bot saves a key of your own, as if you'd pasted it. Its free models then work, about 50 messages a day; see [Try It Free](/docs/getting-started/first-launch#how-should-row-bot-think).
- Besides OpenAI, Anthropic, Google, xAI, OpenRouter and the others, **Add a provider › API key** offers DeepSeek, Mistral, Groq, Kimi (Moonshot), Z.AI (GLM), Qwen (Alibaba Cloud), Together AI, Fireworks AI, Cerebras, Hugging Face, NVIDIA NIM and Vercel AI Gateway. **Find a provider** narrows the list. Each lists its chat models once its key is saved; where its model list says which models take tools or images, Row-Bot uses that, and a model whose list says it takes no tools is offered for Chat Only. Hugging Face and Vercel AI Gateway are routers: they pass your prompts on to the company serving the model you choose.
- xAI API catalog refresh also discovers live image-generation models and their supported output formats, aspect ratios, resolutions, and quality choices. Row-Bot keeps that capability metadata separate from ordinary chat models.
- Custom endpoint providers let advanced users point Row-Bot at OpenAI-compatible servers such as LM Studio, vLLM, llama.cpp, LocalAI, LiteLLM, or SGLang. [Use Your Own Model Server](/docs/guides/own-model-server) walks through each, and how to reach one at home safely from a Row-Bot elsewhere.
- **Add a provider › On this computer** offers LM Studio, vLLM and llama.cpp. Choosing one opens the server form with its type, name and usual address filled in (localhost:1234, :8000 and :8080); change the address if you moved it, then save. A hosted Row-Bot doesn't offer them, since they'd run on your computer, not its server.
- Custom endpoint Advanced settings can describe reasoning mode, a thinking budget, returned reasoning content, and whether preserved reasoning may be replayed to that endpoint.
- Runtime tests check whether a provider can handle the kind of requests Row-Bot needs. A failed test keeps the provider visible but may stop Row-Bot from offering it for agent work.

## Claude (Your Claude Plan)

Row-Bot runs Claude Code, Anthropic's program, with your own Claude plan (Pro, Max, Team or Enterprise), and your plan's limits apply. You sign in to Claude Code, in Claude Code: Row-Bot offers no Claude login of its own, and never sees, stores or relays your Claude sign-in.

1. In **Settings › Models**, choose **Add a provider › Subscription › Claude (your Claude plan)** (or **With my subscription › Claude** the first time Row-Bot starts), then **Use my Claude plan**.
2. If Claude Code isn't installed yet, Row-Bot installs it from Anthropic first, with its progress: the newest version, downloaded from Anthropic and checked against the checksum Anthropic publishes before it ever runs, and set up by Claude Code's own installer where it always lives in your home folder. Nothing is downloaded until you choose **Use my Claude plan**.
3. Claude's own sign-in opens in a small terminal panel. Open the link it shows, sign in to Claude, then paste the code Claude gives you into the panel. On the computer Row-Bot runs on, Claude usually opens your browser by itself and needs no code: finish signing in there.
4. When Claude Code says it's signed in, the panel closes by itself and its sheet says **Claude plan connected**; Claude models appear in the model picker. It works the same from a phone, on a Row-Bot you reach remotely or one a hosting service runs for you.

The panel runs Claude's sign-in (`claude auth login`) and nothing else: it isn't a terminal you can type commands into. Row-Bot carries what you type to Claude and what Claude shows back to you, and keeps none of it: nothing reaches logs, chats or storage. It closes when Claude's sign-in ends, when you close it, or after ten minutes with nothing happening. Whether you're signed in comes from Claude Code itself, never from Claude's files.

If the code is wrong, Claude says so in the panel and asks again. What its sheet and the panel say otherwise:

| Row-Bot says | What to do |
| --- | --- |
| Claude Code couldn't be installed, and why (no internet connection, not enough disk space, a download that didn't match Anthropic's checksum, a system Claude Code doesn't run on) | Fix what it names, then **Try again**. A download that doesn't match is deleted, never run. |
| Claude's sign-in was closed before it finished. | **Sign in again**. |
| Row-Bot needs Claude Code 2.1.263 or newer. | **Update Claude Code** installs the newest version from Anthropic. |
| Claude signed you out. Sign in again to keep using your plan. | **Sign in again**. |
| Your Claude plan's limit is reached until a time Claude gives (in a chat). | Pick another model for now. |
| Couldn't check | **Check again**, or **Update Claude Code**. |

Claude Code signed in with an API key or another cloud counts as not signed in, so a reply never bills anything but your plan. **Update Claude Code** is also there when Claude is connected.

Row-Bot also keeps Claude Code up to date by itself while your Claude plan is set up: about once a day it asks Anthropic for the newest version and, when it's newer, installs it the same way, checked against Anthropic's checksum, while Claude isn't answering. A chat that starts meanwhile waits the few seconds the install takes. Claude's models are then listed again, so new ones appear. An update that fails keeps the version you have and tries again the next day. A Claude Code you installed with npm or Homebrew is left to them.

### Use Another Claude Account

Claude Code keeps one sign-in on your computer, shared by Row-Bot and `claude` in a terminal. To switch Row-Bot to another Claude account (say from a Max account to another plan you pay for):

1. Open **Settings › Models › Claude (your Claude plan)**. Beside **Claude plan connected**, choose **Use another Claude account** (the two-arrows button).
2. Row-Bot asks first, because this signs Claude Code out on this computer, including `claude` in a terminal. Choose **Sign out and switch**, or **Cancel** to change nothing.
3. Row-Bot runs Claude Code's own sign-out (`claude auth logout`), then Claude's own sign-in opens as in the steps above. Claude's page approves for whichever claude.ai account your browser is signed in to, so make sure claude.ai shows the account you want before you approve.
4. When Claude Code says it's signed in, Row-Bot asks Claude Code again for its model list, so the model picker shows that account's models, and the sheet shows the plan Claude Code's session runs on. (Where one Claude account has more than one plan, `claude auth status` can still name the older one; the sheet goes by Claude Code's session.)

Row-Bot never reads, stores or relays either account's sign-in: Claude Code signs itself out and in. If Claude Code doesn't sign out, the sheet says **Claude Code didn't sign out, so it's still on the same Claude account. Try again.** and nothing else changes. If you close Claude's sign-in after the sign-out, Claude Code stays signed out until you **Sign in again**; `claude` in a terminal shares that sign-in, so it signs in again with you.

Row-Bot starts Claude Code with its non-essential traffic turned off: no telemetry, error reports or automatic updates come from these runs, its installs included. Claude Code's own tools are off; when Claude asks for one of Row-Bot's tools, Row-Bot runs it after its usual approval check. The models are the ones Claude Code lists for your plan. Claude Code keeps its own files (its sign-in, settings and installs) in your home folder; Row-Bot's backups never include them.

Earlier versions signed in to Claude inside Row-Bot. That sign-in is gone and its saved tokens were deleted when you updated; Claude says **Set up again** until Claude Code is ready.

## Common Workflow

1. Pick one provider path first: local Ollama for private local runs, a subscription account if you already use one, or an API provider if you prefer hosted models.
2. Add credentials or sign in only in the sheet of the provider you intend to use.
3. Refresh the provider so Row-Bot can discover available models.
4. Star the models you use most in its sheet, and choose your main model under **Defaults**.

## What Is Saved

Provider connection state is global to the local Row-Bot app. Secrets are stored in the operating system key store when available; Row-Bot settings keep masked status and catalog metadata.

## Privacy And Safety

Review credential, account, channel, provider, or tool settings before enabling features that can contact outside services. Local-only features stay on your machine until you ask Row-Bot to use a provider, account, channel, MCP server, plugin, or tool that sends data elsewhere.

## Control-Level Reference

The [generated Settings Controls reference](/docs/reference/generated/settings-controls#models-controls) lists every searchable setting on the Models page, providers included, with its deep link, search keywords, and any dependency or security notes.

## Troubleshooting

- If a provider is connected but models do not appear, refresh its model list in its sheet.
- If an xAI image model is missing or rejects a media option, refresh xAI's model list so Row-Bot can use the live image-generation catalog. A quality choice that the endpoint rejects is retried once without that optional field; other generation failures are returned without an automatic duplicate request.
- If a runtime test fails, read its message before changing credentials; the model may be chat-capable but not tool-capable.
- If local Ollama is missing, start Ollama and make sure at least one model is installed.

## Settings: Models

Route: /docs/settings/models

Choose the main model and the models for Vision, Image and Video, keep your models starred, connect providers, set each local model's own settings, the Cloud reading limit and limits for long work.

# Settings: Models

The Models page is what Row-Bot thinks with, and where it comes from: the model for each job, your starred models, and the providers you have connected (see [Settings: Providers](/docs/settings/providers) for connecting each kind).

## Where To Find It

Open **Settings**, then choose **Models** in the **Models** group, or search for it with **Find a setting**.

## Defaults

Each job has its own picker, using the same grouped, searchable list as the composer's model picker (provider, how it is paid for, and whether it is available):

- **Main model** is the default model for new conversations and background work. A conversation can still choose its own model in the composer. Background work tied to a conversation, such as checking its goal's progress or compacting it, uses that conversation's model; memory extraction and Dream Cycle use the main model. Either way, Row-Bot uses the lowest reasoning effort that model offers, when it knows the model's reasoning choices.
- **Vision** reads images, screenshots and your camera. Leave it as **Same as main model** if your main model can see, or choose another model. Choose a **Camera** here too.
- **Image** makes and edits pictures.

### Images With Your ChatGPT Plan

Signed in with ChatGPT on a paid plan, Row-Bot can make and edit pictures with ChatGPT's own image model, **GPT Image 2**, with no API key. When you sign in and haven't chosen an image model yet, it becomes your Image model; you can choose another any time.

- Images count toward your ChatGPT plan's limits and use them about 3–5 times faster than messages. When the limit is reached, Row-Bot says when it resets; choose another image model to keep going.
- The Free ChatGPT plan doesn't make images.
- An edit changes the picture from your words and can't use a mask to mark one area.
- **Video** makes short clips and animates pictures.

Turn Vision, Image or Video off when you don't want that job done at all.

The Image and Video pickers offer the models each connected provider's own model list has right now, so a new image or video model appears after **Refresh catalog**, without a Row-Bot update. When a provider stops listing the model you chose, usually because it retired it, the picker says so: choose another.

Image models come from your ChatGPT plan, OpenAI, Google, xAI, OpenRouter, Vercel AI Gateway, Together AI, Requesty, Qwen (Alibaba Cloud), Atlas Cloud, MiniMax and Z.AI; video models from Google, xAI, OpenRouter, Together AI, Qwen (Alibaba Cloud), Atlas Cloud, MiniMax and Z.AI. MiniMax's and Z.AI's own lists leave out their image and video models, so Row-Bot adds the ones their docs name. OpenRouter's image and video pickers offer the models its image and video services take, not its routers such as Auto Router. OpenRouter, Vercel AI Gateway and Atlas Cloud reach many image makers (FLUX, Seedream, Recraft, Imagen and others) with one key, and OpenRouter, Together AI and Atlas Cloud reach video makers such as Veo, Seedance, Kling and Hailuo. Together AI's, MiniMax's, Z.AI's and Atlas Cloud's image models make new images but don't edit them here, and Atlas Cloud's video models make clips from text with each model's own length and size. An OpenRouter image or video model gets the length, size and aspect ratio nearest the one asked for, of those OpenRouter lists for it, and its own for any it lists none of. Buddy's new looks use OpenAI, Google or xAI.

After refreshing the MiniMax catalog, select **MiniMax H3 Image** or **MiniMax H3 Image Highspeed** to generate a picture from a text prompt. If your key was issued in mainland China, start Row-Bot with `ROW_BOT_MINIMAX_CN=1` before connecting the account. This selects the China endpoint for key validation, model refresh, and generation. The default is the global endpoint.

## Local

**Local** lists every way models run on this computer, with equal weight: Ollama, LM Studio, vLLM and llama.cpp servers you connected, and Row-Bot's own download. Each row says whether it is connected and how many models it has; **Manage** opens it in Settings › Providers. The **+** icon (**Add a way to run models locally**) shows every way as a row with **Set up** (the server form with that runtime picked, or Row-Bot's download) and **Get it** (the runtime's own site).

**Download with Row-Bot (llama.cpp)** is one entry among them, shown once something is downloaded. Its line says what it runs on (for example "NVIDIA GeForce RTX 4070 (12 GB) · NVIDIA (CUDA 13)") and whether it is ready, running or downloading, and how much disk it takes.

- The square icon stops the model now; it starts again when a chat needs it. It also stops by itself after 30 minutes without a request, so the graphics card's memory goes back.
- The wrench icon (**Repair**) checks this computer's graphics card and memory again, for example after a driver update.
- The trash icon removes Row-Bot's download (llama.cpp and every model it downloaded), after asking, and says how much space it freed. Each model has its own trash icon too. Other local runtimes and your chats are kept.
- When a Row-Bot release brings a newer llama.cpp build, **Update** shows its size; the older one keeps working until you press it.

### A Local Model's Settings

Each model on this computer has one settings sheet. Open it with the sliders icon (**Settings for _model_**) on its row here or in the Catalog, or from the model picker beside **Manage models**. Each choice saves at once.

- **Context** is how much of the chat the model reads at once. **Automatic** shows the size it picks and, for Row-Bot's download, what it takes on the graphics card (for example "64K · about 2 GB on your card"). A fixed size lists only the sizes that fit this computer. On a Mac, sizes above 32K say "slow first reply on long chats". On Ollama the next message uses the new size; Row-Bot's own server starts again with it when nothing is being answered.
- For a server you run (LM Studio, llama.cpp, vLLM, SGLang), the server sets the context: the sheet shows what it loaded and where to change it. For LM Studio, **Reload in LM Studio at _size_** loads the model again at another size.
- **Thinking** (Automatic, On or Off) is shown for models that can turn thinking on or off. A chat's own Thinking choice still wins.
- **More › Reply length** limits how long one reply may be, in tokens (about three quarters of a word each). **Automatic** keeps the engine's own limit.
- **More › Sampling** is how freely the model picks each word. For Qwen3.5 and Qwen3.8, **Model card** sends the values their makers recommend, for a reply that thinks and one that doesn't, and the sheet shows them. **Engine's own** sends none, so the engine's defaults apply. **Custom** sends your own temperature, top-p, top-k, min-p and presence penalty (LM Studio has no min-p), whether the model thinks or not; an empty field is the engine's own. A value in the endpoint's **Extra request JSON** still wins.

Ollama models without their own context keep the size chosen before this sheet existed (Automatic is 64K); the old setting moved once to the model that was in use. Learning's personal models have no sheet: they run as they were trained.

Row-Bot's download uses the official [llama.cpp](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp) release builds (MIT licence). Its default model is **Qwen3.8 27B** at the build that fits the graphics card: 4-bit for 20 GB or more, 3-bit for 16 GB, 2-bit for 12 GB. Smaller computers are offered **Qwen3.5 9B or 4B**, a smaller model of the generation before. All are Apache-2.0, pinned and checked against their fingerprints. The program listens only on this computer, offline, with a key that changes each time it starts. Its models appear in every model picker under **This computer**. See [Privacy And Safety](/docs/privacy-safety/) for what is downloaded and from where.

## Your Models

**Your models** lists the models you starred, which every picker lists first. Each says what it can do (chat, sees images, makes images or video). The check mark makes a model the main model; its star takes it out. Star more in a provider's sheet or in the Catalog.

## Connected

**Connected** has a tile for each provider you have connected, grouped by where it runs and how you pay: on this computer, subscriptions and API keys. A tile says how it is paid for and how many models it has, or what needs doing, such as **Reconnect**.

- Choose a tile to open its sheet: its state, its one way to connect (an API key, a sign-in, or Claude Code's steps), its models with a star each, and a button to refresh its model list.
- **Add a provider** lists the rest by how you pay: **Subscription**, **API key** and **Your server** (an OpenAI-compatible server). Choosing one opens its sheet to connect it.
- **Custom endpoints** below lists your own servers, with their address, probe and key.

A link to `/settings/models?provider=<id>` opens that provider's sheet.

## Cloud Reading Limit

**Cloud models › Cloud reading limit** sets the most Row-Bot sends a cloud model at once. **Automatic** uses all the model reads; **Limit…** sets a smaller number of tokens, to keep requests smaller. It never changes models on this computer: their context is in each model's own settings.

## Limits For Long Work

These limits apply to new runs; work in progress keeps the limits it started with. **Recommended limits** restores the defaults. A run has no step limit to set: it goes on while it makes progress, and after a very long run of steps asks **Keep going?**.

| Limit | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| **Helper levels** | How deep delegation goes; 1 lets helpers work but not start helpers of their own. |
| **Helpers at a time, per agent** | Delegated agents one agent runs at once; more wait in line. |
| **Helpers at a time, in total** | Delegated agents running across the whole app. |
| **Helper time limit (seconds)** | How long one helper may work; 0 means no limit, and time waiting in line doesn't count. |
| **Goal turn limit** | The turn limit new goals start with; 0, the default, means no limit. Each goal can change it. |

## Catalog

The **Catalog** lists every model your providers offer. Search it and filter by provider and job. Each model has the same **star** as the models on this computer:

- A starred model is in **Your models**, listed first wherever you choose a model: every job's picker and the composer's model picker, for the jobs it can do. It says **In your models**.
- A provider with nothing starred lists all its ready models in the pickers; starring one keeps its list to your stars.

The status line at the top says how many models there are to choose from, and from how many providers. **Refresh catalog** asks your providers what is available now. The lists also keep themselves current: about a minute after Row-Bot starts and then every six hours, a catalog older than six hours is read again from your connected providers (their model lists only, with no prompt and no tokens). Connecting a provider reads its list at once. With no cloud provider connected, nothing is contacted.

## Common Workflow

1. Connect a provider with **Add a provider**, then choose your **Main model**.
2. Choose Vision, Image and Video models if you want those jobs.
3. Star one everyday model and one stronger tool-capable model.
4. Keep the recommended limits unless you have a measured reason to change them.

## What Is Saved

Job models, limits and your starred models are global preferences. A conversation keeps its own model when you choose one in it.

## Privacy And Safety

A hosted model receives the prompts, images or files its job sends it. Choose local models for jobs that should stay on your computer.

## Control-Level Reference

The [generated Settings Controls reference](/docs/reference/generated/settings-controls#models-controls) lists every searchable setting on this page with its deep link, search keywords, and any dependency or security notes.

## Troubleshooting

- If a picker is empty, connect a provider first.
- If a model is missing, refresh the catalog and check whether its provider is connected.
- If a picker says its provider no longer lists your model, the provider has probably retired it. OpenAI, for example, retired its gpt-image-1 models in October and December 2026; choose one of its current image models.
- If a model shows as unavailable, read its reason; reconnecting its provider usually fixes it.
- If a small local model fails before answering, give it a smaller context in its settings or choose a more capable model.

## Settings: Voice

Route: /docs/settings/voice

Configure Talk, dictation, Read aloud, the speech models, and the voice Row-Bot speaks with.

# Settings: Voice
