Voice lets you speak to Row-Bot and hear it. Dictate turns speech into text for the composer. Talk is a spoken conversation. Read aloud speaks a reply you choose. Live voice uses a cloud speech-to-speech provider when you choose one.

## Where To Find It

Open **Settings**, then choose **Voice** in the **Models** group, or search for it with **Find a setting**.

## Controls

- **Talk** chooses what listens to you (**Listen with**): Whisper on the computer running Row-Bot (the default), or a cloud speech service with your own key: **Deepgram Nova-3**, **AssemblyAI Realtime**, **OpenAI Live Transcribe** or **Gemini Transcribe Live**. Each cloud choice shows its approximate price a minute, says your voice goes to that company while you talk, and says **needs key** until its key is saved. Deepgram and AssemblyAI keys are added right there (**Add**); OpenAI and Google use the key in **Settings › Models › Providers**. **Live captions** shows your words while you speak.
- **When you pause** sets how soon Row-Bot answers after you stop speaking: **Give me time to think**, **Balanced** (the default) or **Answer quickly**.
- **Push to talk** makes Row-Bot listen only while you hold **Hold to talk** in the voice bar, or hold **Space** while you aren't typing in Row-Bot's window. With it on, the Windows app adds **Hold a key to talk** (**Off**, the default, **Ctrl + Alt + Space**, **Ctrl + Shift + Space** or **F13**): that key works while voice is open, even when another app is in front. It is kept on this computer. The Mac app doesn't offer it yet.
- **On a phone** says when a phone stops listening (see [Phones](/docs/voice-and-buddy/#home-and-phones)).
- **Faster speech models** (under **Talk**) lists the speech models Row-Bot can download for Talk, with the one recommended for this computer first and why: **Moonshine Base** (111 MB, English) on a processor or a Mac, **Nemotron Speech Streaming** (464 MB, English) on an NVIDIA graphics card the speech runtime can use. A faster speech model writes your words down as you speak, so your side of the captions appears live and Row-Bot answers sooner after you stop. Nothing downloads until you press **Download**; the button names the size, the row shows progress, **Stop** keeps what arrived and the next **Download** resumes it. A finished download becomes what Talk listens with. **Remove** deletes a model (Talk goes back to Whisper if it was using it). **Talk listens with** chooses between Whisper and the models you downloaded. Whisper stays available, and Dictate keeps using Whisper.
- **Microphone and speaker** chooses the **Microphone** Talk and Dictate listen with and, where the browser can play to a chosen device (Chrome, Edge and the Windows app), the **Speaker** Row-Bot's voice plays through. The choice is kept in this browser only. Until Row-Bot may use the microphone, the browser doesn't name your devices: **Show my devices** asks for it.
- **Dictation** (**Dictate with**) turns your speech into composer text on the computer running Row-Bot, with the Whisper **Speech model** size you choose. Voice notes you send Row-Bot on a chat app are transcribed with the same choice, in the language set under **Language**.
- **Language** says what you speak in Talk, Dictate and chat-app voice notes. **Detect automatically** (the default) hears which language you speak. When it can't tell (a short phrase such as "yes", or when it isn't sure), it keeps the last language it heard clearly, English until then. Choose a language if it still guesses wrong. Whisper understands every language in the list; SenseVoice understands Chinese, English, Japanese and Korean; Moonshine Base and Nemotron Speech Streaming understand English only. When the engine Talk or Dictate listens with can't understand your language (the one you chose, or one Row-Bot keeps hearing you speak), the group says so and offers **Use Whisper**; Row-Bot never switches engines on its own.
- **Voices for other languages** (under **Language**, once Kokoro is installed): an answer in Spanish, French, Hindi, Italian or Brazilian Portuguese is spoken with a voice for that language, and you can pick which one; English answers keep the voice chosen under **Read aloud**. Kokoro can't speak other languages (German, Japanese, Chinese or Arabic, for example) yet: those answers stay on screen, and the voice bar says so.
- **Read aloud** sets the voice Row-Bot speaks with (**Speak with**): Kokoro, on the computer running Row-Bot (the default), or a cloud voice with your own key: **ElevenLabs Flash**, **Cartesia Sonic** or **Gemini Flash TTS**. The choice speaks Read aloud on a reply, Talk's spoken answers and voice-note replies on chat apps, so with a cloud voice their text goes to that company; the group says so, with the approximate price. A cloud voice speaks the languages its company lists (ElevenLabs 32, Cartesia 44, Gemini over 130), so **Language** says which ones it can't. **Voice** picks one of the voice's ready-made voices, and **Speech speed** applies to Kokoro. Until Kokoro is installed, the group says so and offers **Install** (a one-time download of the model and voices from GitHub).
- **Describe a voice**: with Gemini, **Describe the voice** ("warm and unhurried") goes with each sentence and sets how it sounds. With ElevenLabs, **Describe a voice** and **Make this voice** ask ElevenLabs to make a new voice from your words alone and save it in your ElevenLabs account (ElevenLabs bills it); it then appears in **Voice** as **Your described voice**. Row-Bot never makes a voice from a recording, and you describe how a voice sounds, not who it is.
- **Wake word** (**Hey Row-Bot**) appears only on the computer running Row-Bot (in the Row-Bot app, or a browser on that computer), never on a phone or another device. It is off until you turn it on. Then, while a Row-Bot window is open, saying "Hey Row-Bot" starts Row-Bot Voice in the open chat, or in a new chat if none is open. It listens on this computer only: nothing is recorded or sent anywhere.
- **Test voice**, beside **Voice**, plays the test phrase in this browser, not on the computer running Row-Bot.
- Local voice controls choose Whisper, the default local STT engine, or the optional FunASR/SenseVoice engine for Talk and Dictate. Once SenseVoice is installed, **Talk listens with** (under **Talk**) and **Speech engine** › **Dictation listens with** (under **Advanced**) choose it for each mode.
- A saved Whisper size, SenseVoice model, or Kokoro voice and speed applies to the next use, without restarting Row-Bot.
- SenseVoice readiness shows whether the platform, packaged runtime, and verified local model snapshot are ready. Its install action is always explicit.
- **Live voice** (under **Advanced**) lists OpenAI Realtime, Gemini Live and Grok Voice with each one's approximate price a minute, what goes to that provider (your voice, the chat's recent messages, the agent profile's name and a few related memories; no memories in an incognito chat), and whether its API key is saved. Under OpenAI Realtime, **Realtime voice** and **Realtime model** set the voice and model it uses. You choose one from a chat's Talk menu.
- **Voice models** lists each speech model and whether it is installed.
- **Diagnostics** says what Settings knows without checking: opening Settings never probes a microphone or a provider.

Talk and Dictate start from a chat's composer or Home's Ask box, not the compact Buddy desktop overlay. If Buddy is undocked, use **Open full thread** before starting a microphone session; Buddy will continue to reflect the selected thread's response and approval state.

## Common Workflow

1. Use Dictate first if you want to review text before sending.
2. Use Talk for a spoken conversation: Row-Bot answers when you pause, and you can talk over it to interrupt. If it answers before you have finished, set **When you pause** to **Give me time to think**, or turn on **Push to talk**.
3. For Talk, download the faster speech model recommended for this computer; Whisper stays the default until you do. Install and select SenseVoice Small when you want the optional FunASR engine.
4. Treat the SenseVoice install as a deliberate approximately 940 MB ModelScope download. After verification, normal transcription stays local and cache-only.
5. Choose Live voice from a chat's Talk menu when you want the most natural conversation and accept that audio goes to that provider, at its price.

## Read Aloud

**Read aloud** is a button on each Row-Bot reply (on a phone, press and hold the reply). It speaks the reply with the voice chosen here (Kokoro, in its voice and speed, or the cloud voice under **Speak with**), and plays it in the browser you are using. Code blocks, tables and web addresses are left out. The first sentence starts quickly and the rest follows in order; press **Stop reading** to stop. Buddy's mouth moves while it reads. Row-Bot reads the reply from the saved conversation, so it only ever speaks what the reply says.

Talk and Read aloud say the words you've taught Row-Bot to pronounce; the chat and captions keep the written words. If Kokoro isn't installed, Read aloud says so and offers **Open Voice settings**; it never falls back to your device's own voice.

## Cloud Speech

A cloud speech service is only used once you choose it, and only with your own key; Row-Bot never pays for it or sends anything to it otherwise. While you talk, only the stretches where you speak go to the listening service, one stretch at a time; with a cloud voice, each sentence Row-Bot says goes to it as text. The connection is made by Row-Bot itself, so the key never reaches your browser, and it is never shown again or written to a log.

If a chosen service's key is missing (or you remove it), Row-Bot uses its own part instead and says so: Settings shows **Needs your … key**, and the voice bar says what is standing in and links here. It never switches to a different company. Prices are approximate, from each company's published pricing on the date shown.

## What Is Saved

Voice preferences are global. Transcribed text belongs to the active thread once submitted. The verified SenseVoice snapshot is stored under the active Row-Bot data directory. Faster speech models are kept in the data folder's `models/speech/`, one folder per model. Provider-backed voice can send audio or transcript data to the selected provider.

A few choices are kept in the browser, not in Row-Bot: the microphone and speaker, the key to hold to talk, that you have read a Live voice provider's disclosure, and that you have seen the phone notice. Another browser or device asks again.

## Privacy And Safety

Review credential, account, channel, provider, or tool settings before enabling features that can contact outside services. Local-only features stay on your machine until you ask Row-Bot to use a provider, account, channel, MCP server, plugin, or tool that sends data elsewhere. The explicit SenseVoice install contacts ModelScope for the model download; it does not send audio, prompts, or usage data, and ordinary inference does not check for updates. A faster speech model’s **Download** fetches one archive from the sherpa-onnx project's GitHub releases and checks it against its pinned fingerprint before using it; listening with it never contacts anything.

## Control-Level Reference

The [generated Settings Controls reference](/docs/reference/generated/settings-controls#voice-controls) lists every searchable setting on this page with its deep link, search keywords, and any dependency or security notes.

## Troubleshooting

- If the microphone is silent, check that the browser may use the microphone, and which one is chosen under **Microphone and speaker** (or from the headphones button in the voice bar).
- If **Read aloud** says "Read aloud needs the Kokoro voice", install Kokoro under **Read aloud** in Voice settings.
- If the voice bar says "The speech service didn't answer" or "The voice service didn't answer", check the key for the service you chose in Voice settings (or in Providers, for OpenAI and Google), and that the service is reachable.
- "SenseVoice isn't ready on this computer." means the engine chosen for Talk or Dictation needs installing: install it in Voice settings, or choose Whisper.
- "The speech model Talk listens with isn't downloaded on this computer." means the faster speech model chosen for Talk is missing: press **Download** on it under **Faster speech models**, or choose Whisper in **Talk listens with**.
- If **Test voice** says "This browser couldn't play the test phrase.", check the browser's sound output and that the page is allowed to play audio.
- If SenseVoice is missing or invalid, use its install or reinstall action in Voice settings. Source installs also require the `voice` extra.
- SenseVoice is unavailable on Intel macOS because the required CPU PyTorch and Torchaudio wheels are not published for that runtime; use local Whisper there.
- If a Live voice provider is unavailable, add its API key in Providers.
- If Talk answers before you have finished, set **When you pause** to **Give me time to think**, turn on **Push to talk**, or use Dictate.

## Settings: Memory

Route: /docs/settings/knowledge

Turn remembering on or off, check graph health, configure the wiki vault, and delete all knowledge in Settings Memory.

# Settings: Memory

The Memory page holds the settings for what Row-Bot remembers between conversations. The memories themselves are in **Home › Knowledge**, where you search, review, edit and delete them. See [Knowledge](/docs/knowledge/).

## Where To Find It

Open **Settings**, then choose **Memory** in the **Knowledge** group, or search for it with **Find a setting**. Old links to Settings › Knowledge or Settings › Wiki open this page.

## Remembering

**Enable Memory** decides whether Row-Bot saves useful facts from conversations and recalls them later. A link opens Home › Knowledge to manage what is saved.

## Graph Health

**Graph health** counts your **Memories**, how many **Connected groups** they form, and how many **Unconnected memories** stand alone. A memory graph thumbnail opens Home › Knowledge. Many unconnected memories usually means Dream Cycle or a review would help.

## Wiki Vault

**Wiki vault** writes your memories as linked Markdown articles in a folder you choose, and brings your edits back. See [Wiki Vault](/docs/knowledge/wiki-vault).

## Delete All Knowledge

**Delete all knowledge** permanently removes the saved graph after reviewing exactly what will go. Row-Bot-managed wiki files and local indexes are cleaned up; files outside Row-Bot's managed wiki are kept. Back up first if you might want it back.

## Related Settings

- Dream Cycle's hours are in **Settings › Preferences › Overnight tidy-up**.
- Where memory and document search runs, and its search model, are in **Settings › Documents**.

## Common Workflow

1. Keep memory on if you want Row-Bot to remember useful details.
2. Install the private search model in Settings › Documents before building a large memory.
3. Review and correct important memories in Home › Knowledge.
4. Turn on the wiki vault when you want a readable local copy outside the app.

## What Is Saved

Memories live in local Row-Bot data. They are sent to a model provider only as relevant context in a conversation that uses that provider.

## Privacy And Safety

The wiki vault is a folder other software can read or sync; treat it as an export. Deleting all knowledge cannot be undone without a backup.

## Control-Level Reference

The [generated Settings Controls reference](/docs/reference/generated/settings-controls#memory-controls) lists every searchable setting on this page with its deep link, search keywords, and any dependency or security notes.

## Troubleshooting

- If recall feels stale, rebuild the memory index in Settings › Documents.
- If Row-Bot remembers something wrong, edit or archive the memory in Home › Knowledge.
- If Dream Cycle is noisy, change its hours or turn it off in Settings › Preferences.

## Settings: Documents

Route: /docs/settings/documents

Manage document ingestion, extraction, and vector indexing.

# Settings: Documents

Documents let Row-Bot search files you add to its local document library. This is different from attaching a file to one chat: indexed documents become reusable context for future questions. Mixedbread Embed Large v1 is the recommended local embedding model; it is separate from the chat model and normal use loads it only from Row-Bot's private cache.

## Where To Find It

Open **Settings**, then choose **Documents** in the **Knowledge** group, or search for it with **Find a setting**.

## Controls

- **Search runs** chooses where search works: **This computer** (your documents never leave it) or **Cloud** (document text goes to the embedding provider). Switching to Cloud asks first.
- **Search model** chooses the embedding model. Mixedbread Embed Large v1 is the recommended local one.
- **Free memory when idle** releases the local search model's memory after heavy document work.
- **Index health and maintenance** shows the state of your document vectors and memory index:
  - **Index size** is for advanced search models that need a fixed number of dimensions.
  - **Document index** and **Memory index** each offer **Rebuild**, which recreates them with the current search settings.
  - **Search model files** offers **Download** to install the selected local model, **Retry** to load an already cached copy again, and **Repair** to replace a damaged download. Download and Repair need network access.
- **Upload documents** adds files to Row-Bot-managed storage for indexing.
- **Your documents** lists what Row-Bot has processed, with each document's status and progress, and can remove a document after review.

## Common Workflow

1. Under **Search model files**, choose **Download** before adding a large document library.
2. Upload a small test document and wait until it is indexed.
3. Ask a question in a chat that should require the document.
4. Rebuild vectors only when you change the search model or suspect stale results.

## What Is Saved

Uploaded files, extracted text, vectors, and local embedding model caches are stored under the active Row-Bot data directory. In Docker, the named /data volume preserves the cache. The active chat only sees relevant results when document search is enabled. A cloud embedding provider is opt-in and sends indexed text to that provider; the recommended local model does not.

## Privacy And Safety

Review credential, account, channel, provider, or tool settings before enabling features that can contact outside services. Local-only features stay on your machine until you ask Row-Bot to use a provider, account, channel, MCP server, plugin, or tool that sends data elsewhere.

## Control-Level Reference

The [generated Settings Controls reference](/docs/reference/generated/settings-controls#documents-controls) lists every searchable setting on this page with its deep link, search keywords, and any dependency or security notes.

## Troubleshooting

- If search misses obvious content, rebuild vectors and check the embedding provider.
- If the local model is missing, use **Download** under **Search model files**. Use **Retry** for a cached model or **Repair** for a damaged download.
- If local indexing uses too much memory, turn on **Free memory when idle**.
- If a document contains private material, remove it from the document library before sharing screenshots or logs.

## Settings: Tracker

Route: /docs/settings/tracker

Turn tracking on or off, open a tracker to see its entries, start one in chat, and delete trackers.

# Settings: Tracker

Tracking keeps structured personal logs, such as habits, symptoms, moods or health events, that you ask Row-Bot to record in a chat ("I drank 8 glasses of water", "Log a headache, 6 out of 10"). Row-Bot keeps each kind of record as a tracker.

## Where To Find It

Open **Settings**, then choose **Tracker** in the **Knowledge** group, or search for it with **Find a setting**.

## Controls

- **Track in chat** turns tracking on or off. While it is off, Row-Bot doesn't record or read trackers.
- **Trackers** lists each tracker with its kind and how many entries it has. Choose a tracker's name to see its latest entries (the newest 50, with the total); nothing there changes an entry. Its delete button deletes that one tracker and its entries, after you confirm.
- **Start a tracker in chat** opens a new chat with "Start tracking " ready in the message box, so you can say what to track. Trackers are added by asking Row-Bot in a chat.
- **Danger zone › Delete all trackers** deletes every tracker and entry, after you confirm.

## Common Workflow

1. Choose **Start a tracker in chat** and say what you want to track.
2. Keep logging in any chat ("Log 30 minutes of running").
3. Open the tracker here to check its latest entries, or ask Row-Bot to summarise them.
4. Delete a tracker you no longer use.

## What Is Saved

Tracker data is local Row-Bot data. It can influence answers only when Row-Bot is allowed to retrieve or summarize it.

## Privacy And Safety

Review credential, account, channel, provider, or tool settings before enabling features that can contact outside services. Local-only features stay on your machine until you ask Row-Bot to use a provider, account, channel, MCP server, plugin, or tool that sends data elsewhere.

## Control-Level Reference

The [generated Settings Controls reference](/docs/reference/generated/settings-controls#tracker-controls) lists every searchable setting on this page with its deep link, search keywords, and any dependency or security notes.

## Troubleshooting

- If a tracker is missing, check that **Track in chat** is on, then ask Row-Bot in a chat to start it.
- If a summary seems wrong, open the tracker here and check its latest entries.
- If privacy matters, do not include tracker details in prompts sent to hosted providers.

## Settings: Tools

Route: /docs/settings/tools

Configure progressive external-tool loading, search and knowledge tools, built-in tools, and custom tools.

# Settings: Tools

Tools settings control how Row-Bot exposes enabled external capabilities to the model, its search and retrieval helpers, the small built-in tools it can use, and the custom tools you add.

## Where To Find It

Open **Settings**, then choose **Tools** in the **Capabilities** group, or search for it with **Find a setting**.

## Capability Loading

- **Only the ones a request needs (recommended)** lets Row-Bot search enabled MCP, plugin, Custom Tool and channel capabilities when a request needs them. The tools Row-Bot uses all the time (pages, questions, helpers, the shell and background processes, workflows, memory and the web) are always there; rarely used built-in ones, such as the tracker, video editing and the updater, are found the same way as app tools.
- **All of them, every time** is the eager compatibility mode. It sends every enabled external schema allowed by the current provider and policy, which can consume more context.

Both modes preserve tool enablement, provider compatibility, Agent Profile restrictions, workspace policy, approval gates, prompt-injection handling, and execution budgets.

## Search & Knowledge Tools

**Search & Knowledge Tools** enables or disables configured research and reference tools such as arXiv, DuckDuckGo, Tavily web search, Wikipedia, Wolfram Alpha, and YouTube. Provider-specific setup fields store the credentials required by optional search services.

## Built-In Tools

**Built-in tools** are small tools for everyday tasks, such as the calculator, weather, charts and the URL reader. Each has its own switch, and the heading counts how many are on. These used to be a separate Utilities page. Developer tools are among them; the command palette can turn them on ("turn on developer tools").

## Custom Tools

**Custom tools** turns a folder's scripts into tools Row-Bot can run. **Add from a folder** (in the desktop app) inspects the folder and drafts the tool; this sends short excerpts of the folder to your chosen model, which may cost money with a paid provider. You can also ask Row-Bot in a chat to make a tool from a repository, or use the Custom Tool Builder in a code folder's Developer panel. Review a custom tool's commands before turning it on.

## Recommended Workflow

1. Keep **Only the ones a request needs** for normal use.
2. Enable only the search and integration tools you intend Row-Bot to use.
3. Confirm external services are healthy before relying on them.
4. Use eager mode temporarily only when testing compatibility with an older model or integration.
5. Review approvals before any action that writes, sends, or changes external state.

## What Is Saved

The capability-loading choice and tool settings are local global preferences. Per-task skill activation is stored separately and does not change this tool policy.

## Privacy And Safety

Auto mode reduces schemas in the model prompt, but it does not make a networked tool local. When Row-Bot actually calls a hosted model, remote MCP server, plugin service, account integration, or channel, the data required by that operation can leave your machine. Disabled or profile-denied tools are not made available by discovery.

## Troubleshooting

- If an external tool is not found, check its app in [Settings › Apps](/docs/settings/apps), its Custom Tool or channel configuration, and the active Agent Profile.
- If a direct tool worked previously but discovery does not select it, use a precise prompt and inspect Row-Bot Status for effective tool groups.
- If a provider rejects tool schemas, choose a compatible tool-capable model or temporarily test eager mode.
- If search results are noisy, turn off the search tools you don't need.

For the full runtime model, see [Progressive Tools And Skills](/docs/guides/progressive-tools-and-skills).

## Settings: Skills

Route: /docs/settings/skills

Find, add, try, update, and remove skills, and open the skill editor to create or edit one.

# Settings: Skills

Skills are instruction packs that teach Row-Bot how to approach a kind of work. Some work with an app, such as GitHub: the skill's card says **Works with GitHub**, and its page says whether that app is connected, with a way to open or connect it. **Settings › Skills** works like [Settings › Apps](/docs/settings/apps): one library to find skills and one page per skill.

## Where To Find It

Open **Settings**, then choose **Skills** in the **Capabilities** group, or search for it with **Find a setting**. The command palette's **Add a skill** opens it too.

## Find A Skill

Search by name or by the job, such as "pdf". Search is instant and local; nothing you type leaves this computer. **Search online catalogs** also asks the live catalogs, such as ClawHub, and sends them your search words. The page lists **Your skills** first, then **Featured** and **All skills**. **Add from link or file** adds a skill from a skill page, a GitHub repository, or a .zip or .skill file; nothing is fetched until you agree on the skill's page.

## The Skill Page

- **Use it in chat with /_name_** shows the slash command that loads it.
- **Settings** says whether chats use it ("Available in every chat without a profile." or "Turned off: chats don't use it.") and which agent profiles include it. To change which profiles use a skill, edit the profile's skills; see [Profiles, Goals, And Agents](/docs/profiles-goals-agents/).
- **What's inside** (collapsed) lists its files and scripts, for example "6 files · 1 script", and marks each script. Scripts never run when you add a skill; if Row-Bot runs one later, your approval rules apply.
- **Try it** opens a new chat with a draft that uses the skill. The draft stays in the composer; nothing is sent until you send it.
- The **⋯** menu has **Turn off**, **Advanced settings**, **Check for updates** for a skill from a catalog, and **Remove…** for a skill you added or created.

## Add A Skill

**Add** opens **Add _skill_**, which says where it downloads from and that it "Adds the skill and turns it on". Agree, and Row-Bot checks the skill's files and adds it. Scripts inside a skill never run when it is added.

A skill changes instructions only. It does not add credentials, grant tools that an agent profile denies, or skip approvals.

## Use A Skill In Chat

Type `/` in a chat and choose the skill from the **Skills** group. Chosen in an empty message, it turns the skill on for the whole chat; chosen inside a message, it focuses only that turn on it. See [Mention an app or a skill](/docs/chat/#mention-an-app-or-a-skill).

## Turn Off Or Remove A Skill

- **⋯ › Turn off** stops chats using the skill and keeps it; **Turn on** brings it back.
- **⋯ › Remove…** deletes the skill's files from this computer. Skills built into Row-Bot can be turned off but not removed, and a skill that came with a package is turned off or removed with its package.

## Create Or Edit A Skill

**Create a skill** opens the skill editor for a new skill. On a skill's page, **⋯ › Advanced settings** opens the editor for that one skill, where you edit it, pin it, and review proposed changes to it.

## Old Links

Old links to the Skills section of the former Integrations page open this page.

## Control-Level Reference

The [generated Settings Controls reference](/docs/reference/generated/settings-controls#skills-controls) lists every searchable setting on this page. How Row-Bot picks skills automatically is in [Progressive Tools And Skills](/docs/guides/progressive-tools-and-skills), and writing good skills is in [Skills](/docs/skills/).

## Troubleshooting

- If a skill is never used, check that it is in **Your skills**, try it with **/_name_**, and make your request match its purpose.
- If a skill is used too eagerly, edit it with clearer boundaries or remove it.

## Settings: Apps

Route: /docs/settings/apps

Find and connect the services Row-Bot can work in, including your accounts and messaging channels, choose what each app may do, change its settings, and turn apps off or remove them.

# Settings: Apps

Apps are the services Row-Bot can work in, such as Notion, GitHub or a tool that runs on this computer. Your GitHub, Google, Outlook and X accounts, the Telegram, WhatsApp, Discord, Slack and SMS channels, and the tools that use your own key are apps too. **Settings › Apps** is where you find them, connect them, choose what each one may do, change their settings, and turn them off or remove them.

## Where To Find It

Open **Settings**, then choose **Apps** in the **Connections** group, or search for it with **Find a setting**. The command palette's **Connect an app** opens it too, and requests such as "connect google" or "connect telegram" open that app's page. In a chat, **+ › Apps › Find more apps** opens it; see [Apps in a chat](/docs/chat/#apps-in-a-chat).

## Find An App

Search by an app's name or by what you want done, such as "send email" or "take meeting notes". Search is instant and local: Row-Bot searches catalog copies kept on this computer, and nothing you type leaves it. Once you have typed a search, **Search online catalogs** also asks the live catalogs, such as Hermes, and sends them your search words.

The page lists:

- **Your apps**: the apps you have added, with anything that needs attention first. Each app is one card, even when you connected it more than one way; its chips name the ways. Each shows its status: **Ready**, **Off**, **Sign in needed**, **Key needed**, **Finish setup**, **Working…**, **Needs attention**, or **Removed** for a package whose saved data was kept. [Troubleshooting](/docs/troubleshooting/#apps-and-skills) says what to do about each.
- Category chips (Productivity, Developer, Data, Design, Communication, Finance and Local tools), then **Featured**, then **All apps**. **Communication** lists the messaging channels. While you search, the chips and Featured make way for the results.

While the app catalog is first being built, the page says **Preparing the app catalog…** and more apps appear in a moment.

### Search Results

A search answers with one result first:

- **Best match**: the result that fits best, when its name matches what you typed and its vendor or Row-Bot stands behind it, or the community made it well (many people starred it and it is kept up). It shows what the app does, how it connects, and its stars, such as **★ 1.2k · active**.
- **Also good**: four more results whose names match. Without a best match they are **Top results**, and when none of them comes from a vendor or Row-Bot a line says **No official or reviewed app matches "_search_". These are made by the community.**
- **More results (_n_)**: everything else, folded. Open it to see the rest grouped as **Official**, **Reviewed by Row-Bot**, **Built in** and **Community**, with **Show more** for the next page. A result found only in a description, not in a name, is always here.

Each app appears once in results; its other ways to connect are on its page. One server listed several times (the same package in several catalogs, the same repository under the same name, a near-identical copy from the same publisher, or a fork with fewer stars than the original) is one result; its page lists every catalog it is in. Listings that look like placeholders, staging copies or duplicates are left out, and **More results** says how many; **Show all results** shows them too.

A search word has to start a word: "reddit" finds "Reddit tools", not "subreddit".

### Who Stands Behind A Result

Each result says who stands behind it, decided by rule, never by what a listing says about itself:

- **Official** with a check, and **by _Vendor_**: the service's own vendor publishes it. Row-Bot confirms this from the vendor's domain or GitHub organisation.
- **Reviewed** with a check: Row-Bot reviewed how it installs and signs in. An app the vendor doesn't publish itself can still be reviewed, as Reddit is.
- **Built in**: it comes with Row-Bot.
- **Community · _publisher_**: anyone else. This isn't a warning; check who publishes it and what it may do on its page before you connect it.
- **Made by you**: a connection you added yourself.

An app with both an official and a reviewed way shows **Official**; its page lists each way with its own label.

### Filters

While you search, chips under the search box narrow the results. They apply to everything found, so the counts stay true:

- **Apps**, **Skills** or **Plugins**: what kind of result.
- **Official & reviewed only**: only results their vendor or Row-Bot stands behind, and built-in ways. Row-Bot remembers this one on this device.
- **Runs anywhere**, **Hosted** or **On this computer**: where it runs.
- **No sign-in**: only ways that work without an account or a key.

On a phone the filters are in one **Filters** sheet; its button shows how many are on.

A result also says how the app connects: **Hosted · Sign-in**, **API key**, **Hosted** or **Runs on this computer**. Package entries from the Hermes catalog say **Checked when you add**; one made for the Hermes app itself can't be added, and its page says why. Logos come only from Row-Bot or its saved copies; browsing never downloads them, and a letter stands in until a logo is ready.

## The App Page

Open an app to see its page (for example `/settings/apps/notion`). The header shows its logo, name, publisher and status, one main action, and a **⋯** menu.

The main action is whatever comes next: **Connect**, **Add**, **Set up**, **Sign in**, **Sign in again**, **Add key**, **Continue setup**, **Turn on**, **Fix**, **Retry**, **Try it** or **Delete saved data**. **Try it** opens a new chat with a draft that uses the app; nothing is sent until you send it. The **⋯** menu holds what applies of **Turn off**, **Check for updates** (for a package from GitHub), **Advanced settings** and **Remove…**; for a built-in way to connect it holds **Open its settings**.

- **Overview**: what it does, things to ask, and where your data goes.
- **Access**: what it may do, grouped as **Looks things up**, **Makes changes** and **Always asks first**, with a count and the choice, such as "8 of 12 actions on · Ask before changes" (or **Custom** once you set actions one by one), and **Choose** to change it in **Change what _app_ can do**, which saves with **Save**. See [Choose what an app can do](#choose-what-an-app-can-do).
- **Settings**: for a connected app, the account, whether a key is saved (in your system keychain), each setting, and anything it needs on this computer, with **Change settings**. An app that can show its results as an interactive view also has **Show views in chat** here; see [App views](/docs/chat/#app-views). See [Change settings after setup](#change-settings-after-setup). For a built-in way, **Set up** or **Open** opens its own settings.
- **Ways to connect**: when an app can be connected more than one way, every way, the recommended one first. See [Ways to connect](#ways-to-connect).
- **Skills for** the app: skills made for it, yours first. An app lets Row-Bot use a service for you; a skill teaches Row-Bot how to do a task, and some work with an app.
- **Included**: for a package, the apps and skills it brought. Each of those says **Installed as part of _package_**.
- **Details**: source, version, licence, other catalogs it is listed in, and its identifier.

## Ways To Connect

Some apps can be connected in more than one way: through a server the service hosts, through a server that runs on this computer, or through a way built into Row-Bot. The app's page lists them under **Ways to connect**, the recommended one first and marked **Recommended**. Each way says how it connects (**Built in**, **Hosted · Sign-in**, **Hosted · API key**, **Hosted** or **Runs on this computer**) and who publishes it; the one you are looking at says **This one**. Choose another way to open its page.

For example:

- **GitHub**: GitHub's hosted server (with a token, or with your own OAuth app), then the GitHub account built into Row-Bot, then GitHub's server on this computer.
- **Google**: the Google account built into Row-Bot first.
- **Slack**: Slack's hosted server, then the Slack channel built into Row-Bot.
- **Tavily**: Row-Bot's built-in **Tavily web search** with your Tavily key, then Tavily's hosted server, then its server on this computer.

Each way keeps its own credentials. A GitHub account token and a GitHub server connection, for example, never share a token: connecting one doesn't sign in the other.

## Built-In Ways To Connect

Some ways to connect are part of Row-Bot itself, so their cards and pages say **Built in**:

- the **GitHub**, **Google**, **Outlook** and **X** accounts;
- the **Telegram**, **WhatsApp**, **Discord**, **Slack** and **Text messages** (SMS) channels;
- tools that use your own key: **Tavily web search** (a Tavily key) and **Wolfram Alpha**.

A built-in way is set up and changed in its own settings, not with a setup sheet. Its **Set up** (or **Open** once it is set up), and **⋯ › Open its settings**, open those settings for that one account, channel or tool only, with **Back** to the app page:

- an account opens its step-by-step guide, **Check**, **Reconnect** and **Disconnect**, and what Row-Bot may do with it. See [Accounts And Authorisation](/docs/integrations/accounts).
- a channel opens its connect steps, **Start** and **Stop**, pairing and paired accounts. See [Channels](/docs/integrations/channels).
- a key tool opens its switch and its key, which stays in your system keychain.

Old links to the Accounts and Channels settings pages open the matching app, for example **Apps › Google** or **Apps › Telegram**.

## Connect An App

1. Choose the main action. A sheet named after it, such as **Connect Notion**, lists what will happen: where requests go, whether you sign in in your browser or paste a key, anything Row-Bot needs to download, and that apps get turned on. **How Row-Bot keeps this safe** explains the protections.
2. Agree, and Row-Bot does the setup itself, showing each step as it goes.
3. It pauses only when it needs you: to sign in (your browser opens), to add a key or a setting, to check what it will install, to open a program, or to choose what the app can do.
4. Choose what the app can do, then **Allow** on **Here's what _app_ can do**, and the app is ready. For an app you sign in to, the **Connect _app_** sheet asks first, **What can _app_ do?**: **Look things up** (the default; where the service offers it, Row-Bot asks it for read access only) or **Look things up and make changes** (changes always ask you first). For other apps the choice is on **Here's what _app_ can do**.

### What A Setup Can Ask For

- **Add your key** or **Add your settings**: a key or token is kept in your system keychain; a setting such as a workspace, region or folder is saved with the app. **Where do I get this?** opens the service's own page for it. Optional settings can be left empty.
- **Sign in to _app_**: when Row-Bot first connects, it checks whether the service asks you to sign in, so an app whose listing doesn't say can still sign in. Row-Bot signs in through your browser with its own published details, or registers itself with the service. A few services, such as GitHub, accept only your own OAuth app: Row-Bot asks for its **Client ID** and, if it has one, **Client secret (optional)**, both kept in the keychain, and shows the callback address to register, `http://127.0.0.1/api/v1/settings/mcp/auth/callback`. If a sign-in expires and can't be renewed, the app says **Sign in needed**.
- **Get ready to run _app_** and **Install what _app_ needs**: an app that runs on this computer may need Node.js or uv, which Row-Bot sets up for its own use, and an npm package, Python package, container image or bundle, which is installed into its own folder, never system-wide. Before anything installs, Row-Bot shows **Exactly what will be installed**: each package's exact version and checksum, checked again when it installs. Install scripts never run. Python apps use Row-Bot's own uv and Python. Container images need Docker Desktop, already installed, and never get access to your folders, ports or network. If what an app would install changes after you agreed, Row-Bot shows it again and waits.
- **Open _program_**: apps that work with a program on this computer, such as Blender, check that it is running. Open it, then choose **Check again**.

Searching and reading an app's page never install or run anything; nothing installs until you agree and choose **Install**.

### Sign In From A Phone Or Another Computer

On the Row-Bot desktop app, an app's sign-in opens the browser on the computer Row-Bot runs on and comes back by itself. From any other signed-in device, such as your phone over [remote access](/docs/operations/remote-access/), the sign-in step says what that device needs, and how long its link or code still works (five minutes):

- **Row-Bot has a public HTTPS address** (one approved address in **Settings › Devices & remote access**) and Row-Bot registers itself with the service: choose **Open sign-in page**, sign in, and come back. The service returns to Row-Bot by itself.
- **Otherwise**, the step shows three steps. **Open sign-in page** and allow access. Your browser then ends on a page that doesn't load, at an address starting with `http://127.0.0.1`; that's expected. Copy that whole address from the address bar, paste it into **Paste that address here**, and choose **Finish**. Row-Bot reads only the sign-in's one-time answer from it and never opens it.
- **Where the service offers a code**, Row-Bot shows it instead: go to the page it names, on any device, enter the code and allow access. The step carries on by itself.

A pasted address works once, for the sign-in that gave it. Row-Bot says plainly when it isn't the address, comes from a different sign-in, was already used, or the sign-in has ended; start again for a new link.

**Stop** cancels a setup and keeps what was already done. A setup left waiting for more than 30 minutes stops by itself, also keeping what was done. If Row-Bot can't confirm that a change finished, the page shows **Finishing your last change…** with **Retry**; it checks the result and never repeats the change blindly.

## Choose What An App Can Do

| Choice | What it means |
| --- | --- |
| **Read only** | Looks things up. Cannot change anything. |
| **Ask before changes** | Looks things up and asks you before every change. The default for apps that don't sign in. |
| **Full access** | Makes routine changes without asking. Risky actions still ask. |

**Customise** sets each action on its own: **Use without asking**, **Ask first**, **Off**, or **As chosen above**. To change it later, use **Choose** in the app's **Access** section.

An app you signed in to for reading only says **Read access only** in its **Settings**. Choosing **Ask before changes** or **Full access** later adds a step, **Allow _app_ to make changes**, with one more sign-in so the service grants the wider access.

Some apps overlap with what Row-Bot already does, for example Notion with documents or Slack with channels. Their access step notes it, such as "Row-Bot also has its own Documents tools.", and the choices work as usual. Changes to files and repositories, such as creating a file or a pull request, always ask first.

**Info: Some actions always ask**
Deleting, sending, paying, publishing, running code and anything Row-Bot can't identify always ask first, whatever you choose. Full access only covers routine changes such as creating or editing. Apps connected before this version keep asking before routine changes until you choose otherwise.

### In Chats And Workflows

An app's access applies wherever Row-Bot uses it, together with the chat's or workflow's **Approvals**. Under **Auto**, an action the app's access asks about goes to the reviewer, which approves it only when it clearly matches your request and otherwise asks you (a workflow waits for you); **Hands-off** runs it; **Block** leaves out anything that would ask. Approval cards name the app and the action, such as "Allow Notion to delete page?"; see [Approvals](/docs/chat/tools-approvals-and-terminal#approvals).

## Change Settings After Setup

A connected app's settings stay editable. Its **Settings** section shows what it is set to now: the account, whether a key is saved, each setting (a switch reads **Yes** or **No**), and where it runs. **Change settings** opens **Settings for _app_** with every setting the app has, optional ones too:

- A saved key is never shown. Its field stays empty and says **Saved in your system keychain. Leave it blank to keep it.** Type a new key only to replace it.
- **Save** keeps your changes, and Row-Bot checks the connection again. If the app now offers actions it didn't have before, Row-Bot asks what they may do first; the rest keep the access you chose.
- An app that was on reconnects with the new settings; one that was off stays off until you turn it on. The page then says **Settings saved.**

A built-in way's settings are changed in its own settings: choose **Open**, or **⋯ › Open its settings**.

## Turn Off Or Remove

Both are in the app's **⋯** menu.

- **Turn off** stops Row-Bot using the app and ends its connection. Its settings and saved keys are kept, and **Turn on** brings it back.
- **Remove…** opens **Remove _app_** and removes the app with its settings and access choices. Its saved sign-in and keys stay in your system keychain unless you switch on **Also delete saved keys and data**, which is offered when it has any.
- **Removing a package** removes it and everything it brought, but keeps its saved data and keys: its card then says **Removed**, and **Delete saved data** deletes them. Switch on **Also delete saved keys and data** to delete them straight away. An app that came with a package can be turned off, but is removed with its package.

Removing never revokes access at the service; do that in the service's own settings. Shared runtimes such as Node.js and uv, and what Row-Bot downloaded to run an app on this computer, stay installed. A built-in way has neither action; use its own settings instead, such as an account's access switches or **Disconnect**, a channel's **Stop**, or a key tool's switch.

## Add From Link Or File

**Add from link or file** adds something that isn't in a catalog. Paste an https link (an app's address, a GitHub repository or a skill page; Row-Bot detects which, and **This is** lets you change it), or choose a .zip or .skill file (up to 20 MB) for skills and packages, or a .mcpb bundle (up to 128 MB).

A bundle is checked as soon as you choose it: Row-Bot reads its manifest, checks that it runs on this computer and, if it is signed, that the signature matches its contents. A bundle with a broken signature, or made for another system, is refused. The settings a bundle asks for become its **Add your settings** step. A key pasted as part of a link is never saved with the address: Row-Bot asks for it as a key instead.

Nothing is downloaded or run until you agree on the item's page.

## Advanced

**Advanced** on the Apps page (`/settings/apps?view=advanced`) holds:

- **Apps in chats**: **Use apps** lets chats and workflows use your connected apps, with changes asking first; turn it off to stop every app at once, and each keeps its settings. **Show app views in chat** shows interactive views from apps that have them; it is on by default.
- **Catalogs**: see [Update catalogs](#update-catalogs).
- **On this computer**: **Runtimes**, the Node.js and uv that Row-Bot sets up for apps that run on this computer, with **Check again** and **Install Row-Bot's own** Node.js or uv in its **⋯** menu.
- **Your own connection**: **Add a custom connection** opens the connection editor for a service that isn't in a catalog.

An app's **⋯ › Advanced settings** opens the raw settings for that one app only.

## Update Catalogs

Row-Bot ships a copy of each catalog, so search works offline. **Apps › Advanced › Catalogs** lists each catalog with its state: **Included with Row-Bot**, **Searched when you ask**, **Updating…**, **Updated** with the time and number of entries, or **Couldn't update. The last copy is still used.** Catalogs that are only included with Row-Bot share one line, **Also included with Row-Bot**.

- **Update** refreshes one catalog, and **Update all** every catalog that can be updated.
- **Update catalogs automatically** is off by default. Turn it on and choose **Every day**, **Every week** or **Every month**.
- **Windows connectors** appears only on Windows builds that have them. **Composio**, a hosted broker, stays off until you turn on **Use Composio** after reading what it means; see [Hosted brokers](/docs/integrations/mcp#hosted-brokers-composio).

A failed update keeps the last copy. Behind a proxy, see [Troubleshooting](/docs/troubleshooting/#apps-and-skills).

## Old Links

Settings no longer has Integrations, MCP, Plugins, Accounts or Channels pages. Old links to them open **Apps**, or **Apps › Advanced** for catalogs and runtimes, or the item they named: an old account or channel link opens that app, such as **Apps › Google** or **Apps › Telegram**, and an old Channels link that named no channel opens the **Communication** apps. Skills are on their own page: see [Settings: Skills](/docs/settings/skills).

## Privacy And Safety

Searching, browsing and opening an app page stay on this computer. A catalog is contacted only when you choose **Search online catalogs**, **Update**, or automatic updates; updating the Hermes catalog also reads each new package's manifest, never its code. Once you agree to connect, add or update something, Row-Bot reads it from its source, for example to check its listing again or to download what it installs. Requests to an app go where its page says once you use it. Keys, tokens and OAuth client secrets are kept in your system keychain, never in settings files, logs or what the page shows. Row-Bot's sign-in details are published at `https://row-bot.ai/oauth/client-metadata.json`; they contain no secret and name only this computer as where a sign-in returns. Checking that a program is open looks only at this computer. Apps that run on this computer are not sandboxed, so add only apps you trust.

## Control-Level Reference

The [generated Settings Controls reference](/docs/reference/generated/settings-controls#apps-controls) lists every searchable setting on this page with its deep link and search keywords.

## Troubleshooting

Each status has one fix: the main action on the app's page. An app that is on but needs a sign-in, a key or attention is also listed in Overview's **Needs you**, with the same fix. [Troubleshooting](/docs/troubleshooting/#apps-and-skills) lists every status, and catalog, proxy, Windows connector and app view problems.

- If an app's tools are missing in chat, check that it is **Ready**, that it is checked in that chat's **+ › Apps**, that **Use apps** is on in **Apps › Advanced**, and that the chat's agent profile allows it.
- A built-in account or channel that won't work: choose **Open** on its app page and use its own **Check**, **Reconnect** or **Start**.

## Settings: System

Route: /docs/settings/system

Choose Row-Bot's workspace folder and what it may do on this computer (commands, files, browser and computer use), manage logs, and see what Row-Bot sends and contacts.

# Settings: System

System settings describe where Row-Bot works on this computer and what it may do there: run commands, work with files, drive a browser, and, if you opt in, operate desktop apps with Computer Use.

## Where To Find It

Open **Settings**, then choose **System** in the **System** group, or search for it with **Find a setting**.

## Workspace

**Workspace folder** is where Row-Bot keeps its own files on this computer, such as new draft code folders. Choosing a folder needs the Row-Bot desktop app.

## What Row-Bot May Do

Risky actions still ask first, as each conversation's **Approvals** setting decides.

- **Run commands** turns the shell tool on or off. The command palette can flip it too ("turn off shell").
- **Work with files** controls the file tools.
- **Browser and computer use** opens their setup:
  - **Browser** turns the browser tool on and chooses its runtime: a supported installed Chrome or Edge, or Row-Bot's exact managed Playwright Chromium. **Install browser runtime** and Repair are explicit actions; normal start-up only checks readiness and never downloads a browser.
  - **Desktop apps** sets up **Computer use**: Row-Bot works in an app on this computer with your mouse and keyboard while you watch. It stays off until you set it up, which installs a verified Cua Driver after you accept its telemetry notice. See [Computer Use](/docs/computer-use/).

## Logs

**Log detail** sets how much Row-Bot writes to its local log. **Open log folder** opens it. Monitor's **Logs** shows the same log inside the app.

## Privacy

- **Install stats** is one row: **Share install stats**, on by default, turns it on or off, and its status says when it last sent. This is the only place Row-Bot shows it. **Details** under it, closed until you open it, says exactly what goes, when, where and for how long; see [Install Stats](/docs/privacy-safety#install-stats). Where `ROW_BOT_INSTALL_COUNT=0` turned it off, the row says so instead of showing a switch.
- **Delete what was sent…** is inside **Details** once something may have been sent. After you confirm, it asks Row-Bot's stats service to delete everything it holds for this installation, and turns install stats off.
- **What else Row-Bot contacts**, also closed until you open it, lists the rest and why, one line each: **update checks** (GitHub, about once a day; see [Updates](/docs/operations/updates#what-updates-contact)), **connection checks** (every hour while **Check connections every hour** is on in Monitor) and **catalogs** (model lists and the Apps & Skills catalogs, when you connect, refresh or update them, or on a schedule you turn on). The models, tools, apps and channels you use contact their own services.

## Advanced System Settings

Additional blocked command patterns, app availability for Computer Use, and removing the managed Computer Use runtime live under **Advanced system settings**.

**Let the agent read Row-Bot's data folder** is there too, off by default. Row-Bot's data folder holds your conversations, settings and keys, so shell commands that name it are refused. When it is on, such commands follow the chat's approvals: **Ask** asks, **Auto**'s reviewer approves one only when you clearly asked for it, **Hands-off** runs them, and **Block** still refuses them. File tools never read or change that folder.

## What Moved

- Connecting a phone or another computer, signed-in devices, network access and the public link (tunnel) are on **Settings › Devices & remote access**. See [Remote Access And Server Mode](/docs/operations/remote-access).
- **Open in** (app window or browser) is on **Settings › Preferences**.
- Updates are on **Settings › Updates**. See [Updates](/docs/operations/updates).

## Common Workflow

1. Keep the workspace folder somewhere you back up.
2. Turn on commands, files or the browser only when you intend to use those tools.
3. Turn on Computer Use only on an interactive Windows or macOS desktop after reading its setup and safety guide.
4. Raise **Log detail** while troubleshooting, then lower it again.

## What Is Saved

System settings are global for the active Row-Bot data directory. Workspace files are not uploaded to Row-Bot; external providers may still receive content when a model or tool request sends it.

## Privacy And Safety

Commands, file access, browser automation and Computer Use widen what Row-Bot can do on this computer. Keep approvals on **Ask** in conversations that use them, and review each request.

## Control-Level Reference

The [generated Settings Controls reference](/docs/reference/generated/settings-controls#system-controls) lists every searchable setting on this page with its deep link, search keywords, and any dependency or security notes.

## Troubleshooting

- If Row-Bot cannot read a file, check whether it is inside the folder it was given and that **Work with files** is on.
- If Browser reports a missing or mismatched managed runtime, use **Install browser runtime** or Repair. Do not copy another Playwright cache into Row-Bot's managed location.
- If Computer Use is unavailable, open its setup and follow the reported runtime or operating-system permission step.
- If choosing the workspace folder does nothing, use the Row-Bot desktop app.

## Extend Row-Bot

Route: /docs/extending/

Choose between built-in tools, Skills, Custom Tools, packages, apps, channels, and accounts, and how Row-Bot sets apps and skills up.

# Extend Row-Bot

Start with the narrowest extension type that can solve the task. Every extension adds capabilities; some also add code, dependencies, network access, credentials, or external side effects.

For the conceptual differences between tools, Skills, plugins, MCP, channels, and accounts, read [Extensions And Trust Boundaries](/docs/concepts/extensions-and-trust).

| Extension | Use It For | Review Boundary |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Built-in tool | A capability already shipped and maintained with Row-Bot. | Enable only the tools a profile needs; consequential operations still use approval policy. |
| Skill | Reusable instructions and workflow knowledge. | Open **What's inside** before adding it; adding turns it on, and its scripts never run when added. |
| Custom Tool | A reviewed local command or repo-specific helper made from a folder in Settings › Tools or a code folder's Developer panel. | Inspect its source, command classification, dependencies, and workspace scope. |
| Plugin (package) | A packaged bundle that can provide tools, skills, apps, configuration, or UI. | Review its page, publisher, **Included** items, and downloads before adding it. |
| App | Tools from a hosted service, or from a program that runs on this computer. | Review where requests go and choose **Read only** or **Ask before changes** until you trust it. |
| Channel | A messaging adapter for receiving or delivering work. | Verify account, recipients, pairing, tunnel, and delivery defaults before starting. |
| Account | Authorisation for GitHub, Google, Outlook, X, or another service used by tools. | Review requested scopes and disconnect unused accounts. |

## Safe Evaluation Sequence

1. Read the extension's page: what it does, who publishes it, and its source.
2. Check where requests go, what it needs (a sign-in, a key, downloads), and what it includes. Nothing is fetched or run until you agree.
3. Add it only from a source you trust.
4. Choose **Read only** or **Ask before changes** for an app until you trust it.
5. Test with fictional data and a non-consequential task; **Try it** prepares a draft without sending it.
6. Keep the conversation's approval mode at **Ask** until behaviour is familiar.
7. Turn off or remove extensions that are no longer maintained or needed.

Third-party dependency telemetry is not Row-Bot telemetry. Review and accept any dependency behaviour before installation, and never allow it to receive Row-Bot prompts, files, memories, secrets, screenshots, tool arguments, or channel content unless that transfer is the explicit feature you chose.

Connect apps and packages in [Settings › Apps](/docs/settings/apps), where your accounts and channels are apps too, and add skills in [Settings › Skills](/docs/settings/skills). Open an item's page, read what will happen, and agree; Row-Bot then does the setup and asks what the app may do. Raw settings for one item stay under its **⋯ › Advanced settings**.

## How Apps And Skills Are Set Up

This section is for developers working on Row-Bot or building against its local API. Five guides go further:

- [Catalog Source Adapters](/docs/extending/source-adapters): add a catalog, and the passive-read rules.
- [Contribute To The App Catalog](/docs/extending/app-catalog): app records, verified vendors, icons, featured skills and coverage.
- [MCP Bundles (.mcpb)](/docs/extending/mcp-bundles): what Row-Bot reads, checks and runs in a bundle.
- [Sign-In And Client Metadata](/docs/extending/sign-in-and-client-metadata): CIMD, dynamic registration and your own OAuth app.
- [Hosting MCP Apps Views](/docs/extending/mcp-apps): the sandboxed frame, its bridge and its limits.

**Plans.** For each action on an item, the server computes an install plan: an ordered list of typed steps (`consent`, `inputs`, `runtime`, `local_app_check`, `sign_in`, `test`, `access`, `enable`). `POST /api/v1/integrations/plans/review` returns the plan with a consent token bound to the session and the plan's digest. `POST /api/v1/integrations/plans` starts it with that token; the server runs it in the background, and the client polls `GET /api/v1/integrations/plans/{id}`. A plan paused for input resumes with `POST …/plans/{id}/continue` and stops with `POST …/plans/{id}/cancel`, keeping completed steps. A paused plan expires after 30 minutes. When the outcome of a step is uncertain, the plan reports it rather than re-running it.

**Intents.** `connect`, `add`, `turn_on`, `fix`, `access`, `settings` (change a connected MCP app's declared inputs: one `inputs` step with every setting, then `test`, `access`, which pauses only when the tools changed, and `enable`, which reconnects only if it was on), `turn_off`, `remove` (with `cleanup` to also delete saved keys and data, bound to the consent) and `update`.

**Built-in ways.** `integrations/builtin.py` lists Row-Bot's own accounts, channels and key tools as items (`builtin:account:<id>`, `builtin:channel:<id>`, `builtin:tool:<id>`) with their status read from their owners. They have no plan: their page opens the owner's settings scoped to that item (`?edit=1`). Each keeps its owner's credentials; an account's token is never another app's key.

**Endpoints.** All under `/api/v1/integrations/`: `sources` (with `sources/{id}/update` and, for a broker, `sources/{id}/opt-in`), `apps`, `icons` (a batch of logos as data URIs), `items`, `items/search`, `items/resolve`, `items/settle`, `uploads`, `detail`, `plans/review`, `plans`, `plans/{id}`, `plans/{id}/continue`, `plans/{id}/cancel`, `catalog-schedule`, `views` (with `views/apps`) and `workflow-templates` (with `workflow-templates/{id}/use`). `items` reads installed items or the local catalog index (by `scope`); `items/search` with `refresh` is the explicit **Search online catalogs**; `items/resolve` identifies a pasted link without fetching it (an app link with a query string is refused, since keys belong in the keychain); `uploads` stages a picked file, from any signed-in device; `items/settle` is the **Retry** on an unfinished change: it checks that item's unfinished owner commands again and settles each only when its owner proves how it ended, never re-sending one. The old `/settings/integrations` API routes are removed.

**Tool access.** Each MCP tool is classified by effect:

- High-impact tools always ask: those with `destructiveHint`, or whose name or description has a verb such as delete, send, post, publish, deploy, merge, push, commit, run, execute, pay, transfer, upload, comment, share, invite, permission, reset or overwrite. A routine verb on a sensitive noun (release, message, email, script, password, role, member, collaborator, token, secret, key, admin, owner, webhook, pull request, user, visibility, membership, file, repository) is high-impact too. A tool whose change shows only in its description is unknown and always asks.
- Routine changes (create, add, update, edit, write, set, rename, move and similar; tag, label, archive, link or copy only as the name's leading verb) ask unless the tool is listed in the server's `tools.run_without_asking`, which **Full access** or a per-tool **Use without asking** sets.
- Unknown effects always ask.
- Annotations only make a tool stricter; `readOnlyHint` is the one exception and never outweighs a change verb in the name.

Policies saved before `run_without_asking` existed have no entries in it, so their routine changes keep asking. A server that overlaps a native capability gets `PlanAccess.note` ("Row-Bot also has its own … tools."); presets apply as usual. See [MCP](/docs/integrations/mcp) for the user-facing description.

**Search.** The local index (`integrations/index.py`) ranks vendor-verified and featured entries first, never lets a Registry namespace word (`io`, `github`, `com`) match unless the query is the namespace, and hides low-quality listings (template titles, staging copies, empty descriptions, duplicate title and description) behind `all=true`, reporting how many as `hidden`. `sources.rank` merges one deployment listed twice and groups one card per app; `IntegrationAbout.ways` lists an app's other ways to connect.

**Declared inputs.** What a connection needs from the person is declared once, whatever the source (a Registry header, URL variable, environment variable or argument; a plugin's `mcp.json` `${VAR}`; a Hermes recipe's keys; a bundle's `user_config`). The saved configuration keeps the template (`"Authorization": "Bearer {token}"`, `https://{tenant}.example.com/mcp`, `"--region", "{region}"`) with the declarations in `inputs` (`key`, `label`, `description`, `secret`, `required`, `target`, `name`, `default`, `choices`, `help_url`, `format`, `flag`). Plain values go to `input_values`; secrets go to one keychain credential with `input` bindings. Values are filled in only at connection time (`integrations/inputs.resolve`). A URL variable may fill a path segment, a query value or a subdomain label under a fixed registrable domain, never the host; variables that change what runs (`PATH`, `NODE_OPTIONS`, `LD_PRELOAD` and similar) are never declared. A bare token typed for an `Authorization` header is sent as `Bearer`.

**Sign-in.** The `test` step detects a sign-in (a 401 with protected-resource and authorization-server metadata) and turns `sign_in` on. Row-Bot then uses the person's own client, its Client ID Metadata Document, dynamic client registration, or a pause for the person's own client ID and secret. A refresh that fails marks the app **Sign in needed**. See [Sign-In And Client Metadata](/docs/extending/sign-in-and-client-metadata).

**Runtimes and locks.** A local server's package is resolved into a lock before it installs: `npm` (the registry's shrinkwrap, a managed `npm install --package-lock-only --ignore-scripts`, or a self-contained package's own metadata), `pypi` (managed uv: `uv pip compile --generate-hashes --only-binary :all:`), `oci` (`docker pull`, then the image's repository digest) or `mcpb`. Each lock lists every item with its version and integrity and has its own digest. The `runtime` step pauses `digest_changed` with that review, and continues only with `review_digest` equal to it; a plan whose saved recipe changed under it fails `plan_changed`. Installs go into a private folder per server (npm tarballs checked against their `sha512`, wheels installed with `--require-hashes --no-deps`), install scripts never run, and the launch is the reviewed one. Docker runs `run -i --rm --pull=never` on the locked digest, with no mounts, published ports, privileges or network changes. Nothing runs before consent.

**MCP bundles.** `mcp_client/bundles.py` reads and checks a `.mcpb` without running it; a bundle is locked by its file's digest, and `{bundle}` in its launch is its extracted folder. See [MCP Bundles (.mcpb)](/docs/extending/mcp-bundles).

**Local apps.** An app in `apps.json` may declare `local_check` (`{"port": 9876}` or a process name). The `local_app_check` step connects only to `127.0.0.1` on that port or looks for that exact process, and pauses with **Check again** until it is there.

**Hermes catalog.** Updating the Hermes source also reads each new pin's `plugin.json` (manifest only, never code); a package without an Agent Plugins manifest is native to Hermes and listed as unavailable. Hermes MCP recipes are read at their pin after consent, shown for review (`digest_changed`) and then set up with the steps above.

**Live checks.** `tests/e2e/test_github_live.py` (`e2e`, `live_provider`) checks a GitHub connection made in the UI against an isolated data folder, without ever handling its token: run it with `ROW_BOT_TEST_MODE=0`, `ROW_BOT_GITHUB_LIVE_DATA` set to that folder (the suite gives every test its own folder, so the live one is named separately) and `ROW_BOT_GITHUB_LIVE=connected`, then `removed` after removing the app. Mark a recipe `tested_with_row_bot` only after its live check passes.

## Accounts And Authorisation

Route: /docs/integrations/accounts

Connect your GitHub, Google, Outlook and X accounts as apps, set Google and Outlook up with your own app, use several X accounts, and keep scopes, tokens and data flow understandable.

# Accounts And Authorisation

Accounts let selected tools act through services such as GitHub, Google, Outlook or X. A model provider account supplies models; an integration account supplies service access. They are configured separately.

Each account is an app in **Settings › Apps**: **GitHub**, **Google**, **Outlook** and **X**. On the app's page the account is a **Built in** way to connect, and it is set up in its own settings, which show only that account.

## Connect Safely

1. Open **Settings › Apps** and choose the app, or type "connect google", "connect github" or "connect x" in the command palette.
2. On the app's page, choose **Set up** (or **Open** once it is set up). The account's own settings open with a numbered setup guide; each step links to the page it needs, and finished steps are ticked.
3. Prefer the supported OAuth or local CLI flow rather than pasting broad tokens.
4. Verify the service, account, and scopes in the external authorisation page.
5. Back in Row-Bot, **Check** confirms the account works.
6. Test a read-only action before approving writes, posts, email, calendar, or repository changes.

Each account shows its state (**Connected**, **Not checked yet**, **Needs reconnecting** or **Not connected**) with **Check**, **Reconnect** when a sign-in expired, and **Disconnect**. Disconnecting asks first and removes the sign-in from this computer; it doesn't revoke access at the service, which you can do in the service's own settings.

## GitHub

1. Sign in with the GitHub CLI on this computer (**Sign in with the GitHub CLI**, offered when the CLI is installed), or **Create a token**: a fine-grained token for the repositories Row-Bot should use.
2. If you made a token, paste it under **GitHub token**. It stays in your keychain.
3. **Check GitHub** confirms Row-Bot can reach GitHub. Public repositories work without an account; **Use public access only** says so.

GitHub's page also lists GitHub's hosted server and its server on this computer as other ways to connect. Each keeps its own token: the GitHub account's token is never used for a GitHub server connection, or the other way round.

## Google

Row-Bot has no Google sign-in of its own. You create an OAuth client in your own Google Cloud project, give Row-Bot its file, and sign in with it. The account connects **Gmail** and **Google Calendar**. The guide, **How to set up Google**, links straight to each Google page:

1. **Create a project**: sign in to Google Cloud and create a project for Row-Bot. Any name works.
2. **Turn on both APIs**: one link turns on the Gmail and Google Calendar APIs for that project.
3. **Open Branding**: give your sign-in a name, such as "My Row-Bot", and your email address.
4. **Open Audience**: choose **External**, then add your own Google address as a test user.
5. **Create the client**: in the Row-Bot desktop app, create a client of type **Desktop app**. To sign in from another device, create a **Web application** client instead and add the redirect URI the guide shows under **Authorised redirect URIs** (see [Sign In From Another Device](#sign-in-from-another-device)). Download its file straight away, because Google shows its secret only then. In Row-Bot, choose that file with **Choose file…** under **Google sign-in file**; any file name works.
6. **Sign in with Google**, then finish signing in in your browser.

**Gmail access** and **Calendar access** choose what Row-Bot may do: it can search, read and draft email, but sending always asks first; it can see events, and adding, changing, moving or deleting one asks first. An event that invites guests, or emails them a change, is yours to approve even under Auto.

Google's own hosted Workspace servers are a developer preview open only to testers, so the Google account with your own client is the recommended way to connect Google.

### Google Sign-Ins In Testing Last 7 Days

Google limits apps whose publishing status is **Testing**, as a new app made with the steps above is:

- A sign-in lasts 7 days from when you agree to it; after that Google stops Row-Bot renewing it.
- At most 100 test users can sign in.

When the sign-in expires, Row-Bot shows it: **Apps › Google** says **Sign in needed** with **Sign in again**, the account's settings say **Needs reconnecting** with **Reconnect**, and Overview's **Needs you** lists **Sign in to Google**. Signing in again gives you another 7 days.

To stop it, publish your app: in Google Cloud, open **Audience** and choose **Publish app**, so its status is **In production**, then sign in again. Because Gmail and Calendar access are sensitive or restricted Google scopes and your app isn't verified by Google, Google then shows its unverified-app warning when you sign in; continuing is fine for an app you made for yourself. An unverified app can be used by at most 100 people, and you don't need Google's verification for your own use.

## Outlook

Row-Bot connects Outlook through a Microsoft app you register yourself, with no client secret. It works with a work or school mailbox, Microsoft 365, and personal outlook.com addresses. **Settings › Apps › Outlook** has the guide:

1. In Microsoft Entra, open **App registrations** and choose **New registration**. Name it Row-Bot.
2. Under **Supported account types**, choose accounts in any organisational directory and personal Microsoft accounts.
3. Under **Redirect URI**, choose **Public client/native (mobile & desktop)** and enter `http://localhost`. Then, in **Authentication**, turn on **Allow public client flows**, so you can also sign in with a code from another device.
4. In **API permissions**, add these Microsoft Graph delegated permissions: `User.Read Mail.ReadWrite Mail.Send Calendars.ReadWrite offline_access`.
5. Paste the **Application (client) ID** from the app's Overview. Add the **Directory (tenant) ID** only to keep sign-in to your own organisation.
6. **Sign in with Microsoft** in your browser, or **Sign in with a code**: enter the code Row-Bot shows on Microsoft's page, on this device or any other.

**Outlook mail access** and **Outlook calendar access** choose what Row-Bot may do. Row-Bot can:
- search, read, draft, move and flag email;
- list events, find free times, and create and change events.

Sending, replying, forwarding and deleting email, and creating, changing, cancelling or answering an event, always ask first. An event with attendees sends them its invitation and every change, so it's yours to approve even under Auto.

Microsoft's hosted Microsoft 365 server (Work IQ) is listed on Outlook's page as another way to connect. It needs your tenant ID, an administrator's consent and Copilot Credits.

## X

1. In the X developer portal (**Open the developer portal**), create a project and an app, with OAuth 2.0 read and write turned on.
2. Copy the callback address the guide shows into the app's sign-in settings. Another device may show a different one; X accepts several, so add each one you sign in from.
3. Paste the app's client ID and secret.
4. **Connect X**, then finish signing in in your browser.

**X access** chooses what Row-Bot may do. Posting and deleting ask first.

### Several X Accounts

**Settings › Apps › X** lists each account you've connected, with its handle, name, status and **Remove**. To add another:
1. Switch to that account on x.com in your browser.
2. Choose **Add another account**.

- Every post, reply, quote and delete names its account. The approval card shows the account, the full text and each picture or video.
- To change a post before it goes out, choose the pencil on its card: edit the text, or take a picture off, then **Save edits**. Row-Bot asks again with your version, on a new card. The count shows the length as X counts it (each link counts 23) against the account's limit: 280 characters, or 25,000 with an X subscription.
- A post longer than the account can send is refused before the card, with how much to cut.
- Reading an account's recent posts gives each post's views, likes, reposts, replies, quotes and bookmarks, and their totals.
- A post can have a time, up to 7 days ahead. Its card says when it goes out. Approving it schedules it, and **Home › Review** lists it under **Scheduled** with **Cancel this post** until then.
- With several accounts, a post that names no account is refused, and Row-Bot asks which one to use.
- On Auto, only you can approve a post: the reviewer never does. Hands-off is still your own choice.
- If X doesn't confirm a post, Row-Bot checks the account's latest posts to find it, and never sends it again.
