**Use my Claude plan** installs Claude Code from Anthropic on your server, then opens Claude's own sign-in in a small panel. Open the link it shows, sign in to Claude, and paste the code Claude gives you into the panel. Row-Bot never sees, stores or relays your Claude sign-in.

- **"Claude Code couldn't be installed: …"** names the reason, such as no internet connection, not enough disk space, or a download that didn't match Anthropic's checksum (it's deleted, never run). Choose **Try again**.
- **Claude turned the code down:** Claude's own message shows in the panel and it asks again. Paste the code again, all of it.
- **"Claude's sign-in was closed before it finished."** The panel was closed, or nothing happened in it for ten minutes. Choose **Sign in again**.
- **"Row-Bot needs Claude Code … or newer."** Choose **Update Claude Code**.
- **"Claude signed you out."** Choose **Sign in again** in **Settings › Models › Claude (your Claude plan)**.

[Claude (Your Claude Plan)](/docs/settings/providers#claude-your-claude-plan) explains the panel.

## Can't Find Local Models

Your hosted server has no graphics card, so it can't run chat models itself, and Row-Bot doesn't offer Ollama on it. Row-Bot's own search model for memory and documents does run there; only chat models need more. To use models on hardware of your own:

- **Connect your own model server.** Run Ollama, llama.cpp, vLLM or LM Studio on a computer with a graphics card, and add it as a custom endpoint: **Other ways › Use my own model server** at first launch, or **Add a provider › Your server** in **Settings › Models**. Your hosted Row-Bot reaches it over the internet, so it needs an address the internet can reach, with a key or a tunnel in front: see [Reach It From Anywhere](/docs/guides/own-model-server#reach-it-from-anywhere).
- **Use the desktop app,** which runs Ollama on your own computer. [Move your Row-Bot there](/docs/getting-started/in-your-browser#moving-to-your-computer-and-back) whenever you like.

What Row-Bot says:

- **"Row-Bot couldn't reach https://… Check it's running and reachable from the internet."** The model server isn't running, or its address works only on your home network. Try the guide's [check from outside](/docs/guides/own-model-server#check-it-from-outside).
- **Allow a private address?** Seen from your server, a private address such as `192.168.1.20` or `10.0.0.5` is inside your host's network, not your home. Allow it only if your model server really runs there. For one at home, use an address the internet can reach.

## Moving

- **The backup didn't save.** A big backup can take longer than the click. When the row says it's ready, choose **Download backup** again to save it.
- **No Restore from backup at first launch on your computer.** It's only in **Settings › Data**. Choose **Set up later** at first launch, then open **Settings › Data** and choose **Restore from backup…**.
- **The restore hasn't happened yet.** It applies the next time Row-Bot starts: on your computer, quit Row-Bot and open it again; on your hosted Row-Bot, restart the pod in PikaPods, or redeploy the service in Railway. **Cancel restore** stops it before then.
- **"That backup comes from a newer Row-Bot."** Update the Row-Bot you're restoring on first. On PikaPods it updates when PikaPods installs the new version, usually within a week; on Railway, update the service in its settings.
- **Models and apps ask you to sign in again.** That's expected: backups never hold passwords, keys or sign-ins, and the restore lists what to set up again. For your Claude plan, choose **Use my Claude plan** again.
- **Your phone and websites are signed out.** Signed-in devices and Row-Bot's browser sessions stay behind. [Add your phone](/docs/getting-started/in-your-browser#add-your-phone) again, and sign in to websites again in Row-Bot's browser.
- **The search model or speech model is missing.** Downloaded models and runtimes stay behind. Download them again in **Settings › Documents** or **Settings › Voice**.
- **"The restore didn't finish, so Row-Bot kept your profile as it was."** Nothing changed. Check the file is the backup you meant, and try again.

## Frequently Asked Questions

Route: /docs/faq/

Short answers to the questions people ask most about Row-Bot: privacy, costs, models, devices and safety.

# Frequently Asked Questions

## Does Row-Bot send my data anywhere?

Your chats, memories, documents, workflows and settings stay on your computer. Row-Bot sends something out only for what you use, such as a hosted model, a web search, an app or a channel. Apart from that, it sends a daily install count (a random ID, the version and the system), which you can turn off in one click. [Privacy And Safety](/docs/privacy-safety/) has a table of every connection.

## Can I use Row-Bot without the internet?

Yes, with a model on this computer: choose **On this computer** in Setup and Row-Bot downloads one that fits (or use Ollama). Chats, memory, documents and workflows then work offline. Anything that needs the internet, such as web search or a hosted model, tells you when it can't reach it.

## Can Row-Bot run a model without Ollama?

Yes. Row-Bot works with Ollama, LM Studio, vLLM, a llama.cpp server of your own, or its own download: **Download with Row-Bot (llama.cpp)** in Setup's **On this computer** (or **Local** in Settings › Models) downloads the official llama.cpp program and Qwen3.8 27B at the build that fits your graphics card (or a smaller model on a smaller computer), after you press the button that names the size. It runs only while a chat needs it and stops after 30 minutes idle. See [Local](/docs/settings/models#local).

## What does it cost?

Row-Bot is free and open source. You pay only your model provider: nothing for a local model; your existing ChatGPT, Claude or Grok plan; or per use with an API key. The ring beside **Send** shows how much of the model's context a chat fills. To see usage across chats, ask "How many tokens did I use this week?".

## Which model should I use?

Use the most capable one you have. On first run, Row-Bot tags up to three local models **Recommended**, larger ones that use tools first. Workflows, pages and code work best on a model that uses tools well. See [Model Picker](/docs/chat/model-picker).

## Will Row-Bot do things without asking me?

Only at the level you choose. **Ask** asks before anything that makes changes. **Auto** has a reviewer approve what clearly matches your request, and asks you about the rest. **Hands-off** runs everything and records it. **Block** runs nothing that makes changes. **Always ask me** on a workflow step or an app keeps it asking you whatever the level, and saving memory from an incognito chat always asks. See [Approvals](/docs/chat/tools-approvals-and-terminal#approvals).

## Can I use it from my phone?

Yes. Connect your phone in **Settings › Devices & remote access**. It gets the same chats, approvals, pages and the Browser pane. See [Phone And Native Desktop](/docs/mobile-native/).

## What can Row-Bot do?

Ask it: "What can you do?". It answers from its own list of features and what you have set up. These docs cover each one, and [What's New In 5.3](/docs/getting-started/whats-new) lists the latest.

## How do I keep a chat out of memory?

Make it [incognito](/docs/chat/#incognito-chats): **New chat ▾ › New incognito chat**, or the chat's **⋯ › Incognito**.

## How do I update, back up or move Row-Bot?

Row-Bot updates itself in the background and asks you to restart. Back up and restore in **Settings › Data**. See [Updates](/docs/operations/updates) and [Operations, Data, And Recovery](/docs/operations/).

## Something isn't working. Where do I start?

Check the sidebar's attention indicator, Overview's **Needs you** and [Monitor](/docs/monitor/), which offer one-click fixes. Then see [Troubleshooting](/docs/troubleshooting/).

## Keyboard Shortcuts

Route: /docs/reference/keyboard-shortcuts

Every keyboard shortcut in Row-Bot, on macOS and on Windows and Linux.

# Keyboard Shortcuts

On macOS use ⌘ where Windows and Linux use Ctrl.

## Everywhere

| Shortcut | Action |
| --- | --- |
| ⌘K / Ctrl+K | Open the command palette |
| ⌘⇧O / Ctrl+Shift+O | New chat |
| Ctrl+` | Open or close the terminal |
| Esc | Close the palette, a menu or a dialog |
| / | Find a setting, on a Settings page |

## In A Conversation

| Shortcut | Action |
| --- | --- |
| Enter | Send |
| Shift+Enter | New line |
| ⌘F / Ctrl+F | Find in the conversation |
| ⌘. / Ctrl+. | Show or hide the conversation details card |
| ⌘Enter / Ctrl+Enter | Approve the focused approval |
| 1–4, then Enter | Pick an option on a question card, then answer |
| `@` | Mention an app, an agent, a resource or a file |
| `/` | Choose a skill or a [slash command](/docs/reference/slash-commands) |

## Models, Designs, Terminal And Computer Use

| Shortcut | Action |
| --- | --- |
| Shift+F10 on a model row | Star it, or take its star away |
| ⌘Z and ⌘⇧Z / Ctrl+Z and Ctrl+Shift+Z | Undo and redo in the Design panel |
| Ctrl+C in the terminal | Stop the command that is running |
| Esc while computer use runs | Stop computer use at once |

## Slash Commands

Route: /docs/reference/slash-commands

The commands you can type with / in a Row-Bot chat or a messaging channel, and what each does.

# Slash Commands

Type `/` in the composer to see the commands and your skills. In Telegram, Discord, Slack and WhatsApp, send the same commands as a message. `/help` lists them wherever you are.

## Chat

| Command | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `/new` | Start a new conversation |
| `/stop` | Stop the reply that is running |
| `/reasoning [level]` | Show or set the reasoning for this chat's model. Without a level it lists the valid choices |
| `/export` | Open export for this conversation |
| `/incognito on` or `/incognito off` | In a channel: keep the conversation out of memory, or stop. In the app, use the chat's **⋯ › Incognito** |

## Skills

| Command | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `/skills` | Open the Skills picker for this chat |
| `/skill-name` | Use one skill. With other text, it focuses that message on the skill; alone, it turns the skill on for the chat |
| `/noskill` | Remove a skill from this chat |
| `/skill-reset` | Reset this chat's skills to the defaults |

## Agents And Goals

| Command | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `/agent [--worktree] [--model=…] [--reasoning=level] [profile] <task>` | Start a helper on a task, for example `/agent --reasoning low summarise the thread` |
| `/agents` | Show the helpers this chat started |
| `/profiles` | List the agent profiles this chat can use |
| `/profile [name]` | Show or set this chat's agent profile |
| `/goal <aim>` | Give the chat a goal it keeps working towards. `/goal pause`, `/goal resume`, `/goal status` and `/goal clear` control it |

## Information

| Command | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `/status` | A short summary of Row-Bot's state |
| `/tools` | The tools that are on |
| `/help` | The commands available here |

In a messaging channel, `/model` shows or switches the model, and `/approval` shows or switches the approval level.

| Models | Voice | Configure realtime talk, dictation, the Whisper model size, and read-aloud. | `/app-v2/settings/voice` | [/docs/settings/voice](/docs/settings/voice) | settings-voice |
| Knowledge | Memory | Turn memory on or off, check graph health, configure the wiki vault, and delete all knowledge. Memories themselves are managed in Home Knowledge. | `/app-v2/settings/knowledge` | [/docs/settings/knowledge](/docs/settings/knowledge) | settings-knowledge |
| Knowledge | Documents | Choose where search runs and its model, maintain the search index, and upload documents. | `/app-v2/settings/documents` | [/docs/settings/documents](/docs/settings/documents) | settings-documents |
| Knowledge | Tracker | Turn the habit and health tracker on or off and manage its local records. | `/app-v2/settings/tracker` | [/docs/settings/tracker](/docs/settings/tracker) | settings-tracker |
| Capabilities | Tools | Configure progressive external-tool loading, search and knowledge tools, built-in tools, and custom tools. | `/app-v2/settings/tools` | [/docs/settings/tools](/docs/settings/tools) | settings-tools |
| Capabilities | Skills | Find, add, try and remove skills, and open the skill editor to create or edit one. | `/app-v2/settings/skills` | [/docs/settings/skills](/docs/settings/skills) |  |
| Connections | Apps | Find and connect the services Row-Bot can work in, including the GitHub, Google and X accounts, messaging channels and key-based tools built into Row-Bot; choose what each app may do, change its settings, turn apps off or remove them, and manage catalogs and custom connections. | `/app-v2/settings/apps` | [/docs/settings/apps](/docs/settings/apps) |  |
| System | System | Configure the workspace folder, what Row-Bot may do (commands, files, browser and Computer Use), and logging. | `/app-v2/settings/system` | [/docs/settings/system](/docs/settings/system) | settings-system |
| System | Activity | See every action Row-Bot took with a tool, its outcome and who allowed it; filter it, export it as CSV, or clear it. Switch, edit or delete your Always allow rules. | `/app-v2/settings/activity` | [/docs/privacy-safety/](/docs/privacy-safety/) |  |
| System | Devices & remote access | Connect a phone or computer, review signed-in devices, and choose network access or a public link. | `/app-v2/settings/access` | [/docs/operations/remote-access](/docs/operations/remote-access) | settings-remote-access |
| System | Updates | See your version, download updates in the background, restart into them, go back with Repair, and choose the update channel. | `/app-v2/settings/updates` | [/docs/operations/updates](/docs/operations/updates) |  |
| System | Data | Back up and restore Row-Bot data, import from another assistant, and run irreversible clean-up. | `/app-v2/settings/data` | [/docs/operations/](/docs/operations/) |  |

## Learning Controls

Group: General. Open in Row-Bot: `/app-v2/settings/learning`. Guide: [/docs/settings/](/docs/settings/).

Dependencies: Training needs the training engine and a starting model, downloaded only after you agree.

Security: Learning is on from the start, for learning from your corrections; experimental learning, reading past chats and the personal model are off until you turn them on. Its records, tests and models stay on this computer; its own model calls go to your default model's provider, and Hugging Face is used only if you choose it.

## Apps Controls

Group: Connections. Open in Row-Bot: `/app-v2/settings/apps`. Guide: [/docs/settings/apps](/docs/settings/apps).

Dependencies: Apps that run on this computer may need Node.js or uv, which Row-Bot prepares after you agree. Channels need the matching channel extra and third-party account configuration.

Security: Nothing is fetched or run until you agree; deleting, sending, paying, publishing, running code and unknown actions always ask first. Signing in to an account opens an external authorisation flow, and a running channel can receive or deliver real messages.

## Activity Controls

Group: System. Open in Row-Bot: `/app-v2/settings/activity`. Guide: [/docs/privacy-safety/](/docs/privacy-safety/).

Security: The log stays on this computer for 90 days; summaries leave out what tools read, and incognito chats show no words. Only you can clear it. A rule starts only from an approval card, never covers sending, deleting, paying or anything only you approve, and never applies in a chat other people share.

_This page has no individually searchable settings._

## Channels

Generated reference for messaging channels.

# Channels

## Channels

| ID | Channel | Description | Configuration | Capabilities |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| discord | Discord | Row-Bot - Discord Channel Adapter =================================== Discord bot using discord.py with Gateway Intents (WebSocket) | Bot Token, Your Discord User ID (optional) | buttons, document_in, document_out, photo_in, photo_out, reactions, slash_commands, streaming, typing, voice_in |
| passive-catalog | Passive Catalog | Static metadata for rendering core channels before adapters are loaded |  | buttons, document_in, document_out, photo_in, photo_out, reactions, streaming, typing, voice_in |
| slack | Slack | Row-Bot - Slack Channel Adapter ================================ Socket Mode Slack bot that bridges messages to the Row-Bot agent | App Token (xapp-...), Bot Token (xoxb-...), Your Slack User ID (optional) | buttons, document_in, document_out, photo_in, photo_out, reactions, slash_commands, streaming, voice_in |
| sms | SMS | Row-Bot - SMS Channel Adapter (Twilio) ======================================= SMS/MMS channel using Twilio REST API for outbound | Account SID, Auth Token, Twilio Phone Number, Your Phone Number | slash_commands |
| telegram | Telegram | Row-Bot - Telegram Channel Adapter ================================== Long-polling Telegram bot that bridges messages to the Row-Bot agent | Bot Token, Your Telegram User ID | buttons, document_in, document_out, photo_in, photo_out, reactions, streaming, typing, voice_in |
| whatsapp | WhatsApp | Row-Bot - WhatsApp Channel Adapter ==================================== WhatsApp bot using Baileys via a Node.js bridge subprocess | Your Phone Number (optional) | document_in, document_out, photo_in, photo_out, reactions, slash_commands, streaming, typing, voice_in |

## Safety And Approvals

Route: /docs/reference/generated/safety-approvals

Generated reference for approval policy and safety modes.

# Safety And Approvals

## Approval Decisions

| ID | Label | Decision | Description | Source |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| approve | Ask | ask | Prompts the user before a sensitive action continues. | `src/row_bot/approval_policy.py` |
| auto | Auto | review | A reviewer model approves actions that clearly match the person's request and asks the person about the rest; it fails safe to asking. | `src/row_bot/approval_policy.py` |
| block | Block | block | Read-only or blocked mode for actions that would change external state. | `src/row_bot/approval_policy.py` |
| full | Hands-off | allow | Approves every action without asking and records each one; chosen by the person, never in a conversation other people share. | `src/row_bot/approval_policy.py` |
| mcp-destructive-tools | MCP destructive tool classification | ask | External MCP tools that look destructive require approval by default. | `src/row_bot/mcp_client/safety.py` |

Home no longer has a Designer tab: a design now opens in its conversation's Design panel.

Read [Code Folders](/docs/developer/) for how to bind, clone and work on one.

## Home

Route: /docs/home/

Home's tabs: Overview, Workflows, Knowledge, Monitor and Insights, and Learning while it's on.

# Home

Home is the start page for everything that isn't a single conversation. Choose **Home** in the sidebar, then one of its five tabs:

- [Overview](/docs/home/overview) asks Row-Bot anything, lists what needs you, and shows live status and recent work.
- [Workflows](/docs/home/workflows) lists saved workflows and reminders, runs them in one click, and opens the workflow editor.
- [Knowledge](/docs/home/knowledge) shows the memory graph and the full memory library, with review, editing and Dream Cycle.
- [Monitor](/docs/home/monitor) keeps the latest health checks with one-click fixes, plus activity, history and logs.
- [Insights](/docs/home/insights) lists what Row-Bot noticed and the proposals it prepared for your review.
- [Learning](/docs/learning/), a sixth tab while Learning is on, shows what needs you, what it did overnight, its changes and lessons, and your personal model.

Designs and code folders are not Home tabs: each opens in its conversation's panel. See [Designs](/docs/designer/) and [Code Folders](/docs/developer/).

## Full Guides

- [Workflows guide](/docs/guides/workflows)
- [Knowledge guide](/docs/knowledge/)
- [Monitor guide](/docs/monitor/)

## Home: Knowledge

Route: /docs/home/knowledge

Use Home Knowledge to explore the memory graph, search and review memories, and run Dream Cycle.

# Home: Knowledge

The Knowledge tab is where you see and manage what Row-Bot remembers: the memory graph, the full memory library, the review queue, recent recalls and changes, and Dream Cycle.

## What You Can Do Here

- **Explore the graph.** It opens with up to 2,000 memories; **Show all** draws up to 5,000.
- **Search and filter** the whole library by words or status, including the review queue.
- **Open a memory** to see its details, connections, sources and when it was recalled.
- **Add, edit, merge, archive, restore or delete** memories, one at a time or in bulk. Deleting is always reviewed first.
- **Run Dream Cycle now** to tidy memory outside its overnight hours.

Settings for remembering, graph health and the wiki vault are in **Settings › Memory**.

## Next Step

Open the [Knowledge guide](/docs/knowledge/) for the full walkthrough.

## Home: Monitor

Route: /docs/home/monitor

Use Home Monitor to see Row-Bot's latest health checks, fix problems in one click, and read activity, history and logs.

# Home: Monitor

The Monitor tab answers: is everything healthy, what needs attention, and what happened recently? Row-Bot keeps the latest result of every check, so the tiles stay current after you switch tabs or restart.

## What You Can Do Here

- **Needs attention** lists problems with a one-click fix, such as **Restart** a stopped channel or **Reconnect** an account.
- **Health tiles** show each area's latest checks; open one for every check and its fix.
- **Run diagnosis** runs every check now; **Copy diagnosis report** copies a summary for support.
- **Check connections every hour** controls the checks that contact your providers, accounts and the internet.
- **Activity**, **Maintenance**, **History** and **Logs** show what ran and why.

## Next Step

Open the [Monitor guide](/docs/monitor/) for the full walkthrough.

## Home: Workflows

Route: /docs/home/workflows

Use Home Workflows to run saved workflows in one click, create or edit them on the page, and set delivery defaults.

# Home: Workflows

The Workflows tab lists your saved workflows and reminders: when each runs next, how its last runs went, and what it is doing now.

## What You Can Do Here

- **Run** starts a workflow at once; **Stop** appears while it runs.
- **New workflow** and **Edit** open the workflow editor on this page.
- **Enable** or **Disable** a workflow's schedule.
- **Delivery defaults** choose the channels results are also sent to.
- The **⋯** menu on a row opens its run history, steps, settings or conversation, or duplicates or deletes it.

## Next Step

Open the [Workflows guide](/docs/guides/workflows) for the full walkthrough.

## Settings: Accounts

Route: /docs/settings/accounts

Settings no longer has an Accounts page; the GitHub, Google, Outlook and X accounts are apps in Settings Apps.

# Settings: Accounts

Settings no longer has an Accounts page. Your GitHub, Google, Outlook and X accounts are apps now: open **Settings › Apps** and choose **GitHub**, **Google**, **Outlook** or **X**. On the app's page the account is a **Built in** way to connect, and **Set up** (or **Open** once it is set up) opens that one account's own settings: its setup guide, **Check**, **Reconnect** and **Disconnect**, and what Row-Bot may do with it.

Read [Settings: Apps](/docs/settings/apps#built-in-ways-to-connect) and [Accounts And Authorisation](/docs/integrations/accounts).

Old Accounts links open the matching app in Row-Bot.

## Settings: Channels

Route: /docs/settings/channels

Settings no longer has a Channels page; Telegram, WhatsApp, Discord, Slack and SMS are apps in Settings Apps.

# Settings: Channels

Settings no longer has a Channels page. Each channel is an app now: open **Settings › Apps** and choose **Telegram**, **WhatsApp**, **Discord**, **Slack** or **Text messages** (SMS); the **Communication** category lists them together. On the app's page the channel is a **Built in** way to connect, and **Set up** (or **Open** once it is set up) opens that one channel's own settings: its connect steps, **Start** and **Stop**, pairing, and paired accounts.

Read [Settings: Apps](/docs/settings/apps#built-in-ways-to-connect) and [Channels](/docs/integrations/channels).

Old Channels links open the matching app in Row-Bot, or the Communication apps when they named no channel.

## Settings: Integrations

Route: /docs/settings/integrations

Settings no longer has an Integrations page; apps are in Settings Apps and skills are in Settings Skills.

# Settings: Integrations

Settings no longer has an Integrations page. What it held now lives on two pages:

- Services Row-Bot can work in, packages, catalogs and custom connections: **Settings › Apps**. Read [Settings: Apps](/docs/settings/apps).
- Skills: **Settings › Skills**. Read [Settings: Skills](/docs/settings/skills).

Old Integrations links open the matching page in Row-Bot.

## Settings: MCP

Route: /docs/settings/mcp

Settings no longer has an MCP page; connections are apps in Settings Apps.

# Settings: MCP

Settings no longer has an MCP page. MCP connections are apps in **Settings › Apps**; **Use apps**, catalogs, runtimes and **Add a custom connection** are under **Apps › Advanced**. Read [Settings: Apps](/docs/settings/apps) and [MCP](/docs/integrations/mcp).

Old MCP links open the matching place in Row-Bot.

## Settings: Plugins

Route: /docs/settings/plugins

Settings no longer has a Plugins page; packages are in Settings Apps.

# Settings: Plugins

Settings no longer has a Plugins page. Packages are added, turned off and removed in **Settings › Apps**, and the apps and skills a package brings show **Installed as part of _package_**. Read [Settings: Apps](/docs/settings/apps) and [Plugins](/docs/integrations/plugins).

Old Plugins links open the matching place in Row-Bot.

## Settings: Utilities

Route: /docs/settings/utilities

Settings no longer has a Utilities page; the built-in tools are part of Settings Tools.

# Settings: Utilities

The built-in tools that used to live under Utilities are now in **Settings › Tools › Built-in tools**.
Read [Settings: Tools](/docs/settings/tools).

## UI Tour

Route: /docs/ui-tour/

A short guided tour of Row-Bot: the sidebar, Home, a conversation, panels, the command palette and Settings.

# UI Tour

Use this short tour if you want the quickest mental map before reading detailed pages.

1. Start with the [Row-Bot Interface](/docs/app-shell/navigation): the sidebar, Home, a conversation and its details card, panels, the terminal, and the ⌘K command palette.
2. Read [Home: Overview](/docs/home/overview), the first page Row-Bot opens: the Ask box, what needs you, live status and recent work.
3. Read [Chat](/docs/chat/) for conversations, the composer, models, attachments, tool traces and approvals.
4. See how a conversation works on a design or code folder in [Designs](/docs/designer/) and [Code Folders](/docs/developer/).
5. Open [Settings](/docs/settings/) when you are ready to connect providers, choose models, and set up memory, tools, apps (your accounts and channels included) and devices.
6. Keep [Privacy And Safety](/docs/privacy-safety/) nearby when enabling external services or action tools.
